children.translated_text: First <s>kāṇḍa</s> (section)
and the Father who is full-bodied and whose splendor is concealed in the five faces —
The great Mother who is the abode of the pure <s>kalā</s> (creative power) and the source of wondrous new creation,
which is the family of the supreme nectar (<s>anuttarāmṛtakula</s>), throb within me.
may that Heart, composed of the emission born from the flash of the union of those two (<s>yāmala</s>),
By whose rays of knowledge, shining forth on all sides,
our heart-lotuses have blossomed — may that <s>Guru</s> be victorious!
He who bestowed upon me the floods of meaning, brilliant with the five streams of the meaning of the twelve half-[<s>kalās</s>] accompanied by self-awareness (<s>abhimarśa</s>),
[those floods of meaning] whose vow is to destroy misfortune —
may <s>Śambhunātha</s>, purified by the glorious <s>Sumati</s>, gracious toward the people of true devotion,
be pleased with me, gratified by the flowers of [my] speech!
I bow to the venerable one named <s>Cukhalaka</s>, even weightier than the <s>gurus</s>,
by whose sacramental initiation I stand, freed from [false] apprehension.
Even weightier than he, the glorious <s>Bhūtirāja</s>, of great intelligence,
may he be victorious — he whose daring is the rescue of the devoted people!
Victorious are the compositions of the delight of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), spreading in all directions,
which issued from the glorious <s>Utpaladeva</s>, [himself] born from the awakening of the glorious <s>Somānanda</s>!
Victorious is the speech of the <s>guru</s>, the glorious <s>Lakṣmaṇagupta</s>,
who teaches the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition) that severs the cycle of that [limited] vision!
By whom my bee-like intellect, intoxicated solely by the wonder of innumerable fresh savors,
has been satiated with the supreme enjoyment (<s>anuttarasaṃbhoga</s>) —

children.text: tadekamayatām āpya svātmany eva tathā sthitā /
children.translated_text: having attained complete identity with that [consciousness], and abiding thus in its own Self,

children.text: tad asyāḥ pronmiṣanty eva vividhā nādasaṃpadaḥ //
children.translated_text: from it there flash forth the diverse riches of sound (<s>nāda</s>).
Requested again and again by good disciples, [their ears] resonant [with desire],

children.text: vākyārthaṃ vartaye śrīmanmālinyāṃ yat kva cit kva cit //
children.translated_text: I expound the meaning of the sentences of the glorious <s>Mālinī</s> [Tantra], here and there.
Through propriety and the rejection of what is otherwise, between the expressed and the expressor, mutually,

children.text: vartanāvarta etasmin sādhu śāstraṃ ca vārttikam //
children.translated_text: in this revolving [exposition] — the scripture and the <s>vārttika</s> (commentary) are well [composed].

children.text: ye 'harniśaṃ prakāśante sarvasya ca na gocare /
children.translated_text: Those who shine day and night, yet are not within the range of everyone —
we bow to those <s>Abhinavaguptas</s>, masses of rays of the moon of <s>Śiva</s>!
Victorious are the rays of the moon of knowledge arisen from the mouth of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord),
capable of destroying the adversary of the bliss of the world!
Because of the unrestricted reality of true existence, partaking of the sole unity of beings —
that great knowledge which arose before, [possesses] the majesty of the fullness of those rays.
That [knowledge], thus extended, free from the rejection and acceptance that belong to its own <s>māyā</s>,
differentiated only by the variegated rays of the wonder of the expansion of manifestation (<s>vitatībhāvanā</s>) —
that is the Heart of the Supreme Lord, whose nature is self-awareness (<s>abhimarśa</s>).
And therein, through his own <s>Śakti</s> (Power), always consisting of his own Self, the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>),

children.text: yadā saṃghaṭṭam āsādya samāpattiṃ parāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: when encountering the union, enters the supreme <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) —
then his supreme Face, the locus of the outpouring of emission (<s>visarga</s>),
beautiful with the bliss of the world arisen from the supreme expansion (<s>anuttaravikāsa</s>),
abides as the seed of everything, undivided from the future Face.
That is considered [to include] the throb of the heart (<s>hṛtspanda</s>), vision (<s>dṛk</s>), the essence of the Supreme, the wave of dissolution (<s>nirnāma</s>), and so forth.
This supreme triad (<s>trika</s>) is primary, possessing the non-differentiation of all powers.
Herein, through the cessation of the contraction of doubt regarding the arising of entities,
the triad of knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), knowledge (<s>icchā</s>), and action (<s>karma-dṛk</s>) [consists] merely of immersion in one's own bliss.

children.text: tathā ca guravaḥ śaivadṛṣṭāv itthaṃ nyarūpayan /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>gurus</s> established in the <s>Śaiva</s> vision as follows:
When he abides absorbed in the experience of the mere delight of consciousness (<s>cidāhlāda</s>) —

children.text: tad icchā tāvatī jñānaṃ tāvat tāvat kriyā hi sā /
children.translated_text: that is <s>icchā</s> (will); that much is <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); that much indeed is <s>kriyā</s> (action);
it operates through the harmony of the exceedingly subtle triad of powers.
He would be one whose supreme [nature] is the delight of consciousness, undivided from that.
Now, since in such a [state], being the Self of all, there is the abandonment of contraction —
how [can there be] the riches of scripture and the like, rooted in the fabrication of conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>)?
It is said: all this awareness (<s>bodha</s>) is entirely composed of the radiance of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>).
Because of its identity with the form of light (<s>prakāśa</s>), it is dense with the self-awareness of consciousness (<s>cidāmarśa</s>).
And this self-awareness — that which is light (<s>prakāśa</s>) — shines forth;

children.text: sa eva kiṃ na śāstraughaḥ kim anyair yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: is that not itself the flood of scriptures? What need of other displays of reasoning?
Therein, penetrated by the supreme deity of speech (<s>paravākdevatā</s>), it is solely that [pure word];
but it is not variegated by the mundane, illusory (<s>māyīya</s>) mass of letters.
It is said in the glorious <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>: "The shining of that which abides in the Self

children.text: asty eva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: certainly exists; without it, the awareness (<s>āmarśa</s>) of will does not operate."
They know self-awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) as the essential nature of manifestation; otherwise,
even light (<s>prakāśa</s>) colored by objects would be equivalent to gems and the like.
Moreover, whatever self-awareness enters the domain of the wonder of consciousness (<s>ciccamatkāra</s>),
whose objects are pleasure, pain, and the like — that [awareness] becomes clear;
through the connection with the arising that rests upon the interval of other [moments of] self-awareness,

children.text: paścāt susphuṭatām eti tathā ca gurur ūcivān /
children.translated_text: afterwards it becomes very clear. And thus the <s>Guru</s> has said:
"Just as pleasure and the like, established through self-experience (<s>svasaṃvid</s>), subsist,

children.text: na hi vyavasthāsamaye vedyate tat svasaṃvidā /
children.translated_text: but at the time of determination, that is not experienced through self-experience —
so too, this must necessarily be accepted, on the basis of the proof of self-experience."
Thus here too, afterwards, on the path of the arising of knowledge and so forth,
until it reaches the stage of being apprehended — the ground that is entirely composed of non-difference —
through the clarity of the aspect of the noble self-awareness appropriate to it,

children.text: tādṛk sa eva śāstratvaṃ prāgvisargaḥ prapadyate //
children.translated_text: that very prior emission assumes the character of scripture.

children.text: etad eva tu yuktaṃ syāt tathā hy anupadhau pare /
children.translated_text: And this alone would be proper; for thus, even in the <s>Parama</s> [tradition], regarding the other,
in the meaning of scripture too, some trace of practice is perceived.
That [trace] certainly possesses the powers of future knowledge and so forth, whose abode is the state of clarity;
through coloring, it is then augmented by the diversity of this and that.
Just as the face [appears] in its place of manifestation — in water, in a mirror, in a gem,
in a sword — [with] conditions of flickering, round, subtle, elongated, and so forth.

children.text: tad itthaṃ parame rūpe prodbhūtā jñānasaṃpadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the supreme form, the riches of knowledge have arisen,
beautiful through the triad of uninterrupted heart, seed, and self.
But when <s>Bhairava</s>, augmented by <s>Śakti</s>, wishes to emit
the floods of entities, whose inner nature consists of waves of his own arising form —
then those very riches of knowledge, having resorted to
a slight constraint of action and practice born of those conditions, as it were,
while everywhere assuming identity with the floods of those waves,
nevertheless, in <s>Bhairava</s> of awareness, beautiful with the bliss of the world,
satiated merely by the fullness of entities, possessing [all] powers,
[even though] the state of the power-holder is surpassed by his own full power —
that very stream of knowledge, whose nature is self-awareness, bursts forth,
in which, through the teaching of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>), some delight operates.
Cultivated through the intimacy of the conduct of its own consciousness,
even the multitude of enjoyments, for the fortunate, leads to the state of supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
Where it is said: "Filled with the agitation of the stirring of his own <s>Śakti</s> and so forth,
the Lord's love of worship [arises] especially from among the [divine] Mothers."
Through the excess of the power of sovereignty, having obtained the designation of Lord,
this Lord, the majesty of consciousness, has arisen and is elaborated.
Herein too, in the joining and separating of infinite aspects of entities,
through the cohesion of the prior ten-[fold] non-differentiation, [it] has assumed innumerability.
Due to those very conditions, bereft of the designation of consciousness-knowledge,
the diverse glories of scriptural, practical, and cognitive [knowledge] are extended.

children.text: mukhyas tv eṣa prapañco 'yaṃ pañcātmatvena carcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the principal elaboration is this, discussed as fivefold;

children.text: tathā ca vakṣyate tattvam abhinnam api pañcadhā //
children.translated_text: and thus it will be stated: "Reality, though undivided, is fivefold."
Through sovereignty over [all] activities, through being the impeller of what depends on that,
through the cessation of will, through self-abiding — by such collections of statements.
Now, in such an extensive composition, the distinctions produced by place, time, and <s>kalā</s> (limitation)

children.text: bhedā na saṃbhavanty eva bāḍham om iti vacmahe //
children.translated_text: cannot exist at all. Indeed, we say: "Yes, <s>Om</s>."

children.text: na hy atra kālatattvasya nāmamātraṃ vibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: For herein, not even the mere name of the reality of time is perceived;

children.text: vaibhavy api mahākālī śaktir nātra vijṛmbhate //
children.translated_text: even in the expanse, the great power of <s>Kālī</s> does not burst forth here.

children.text: tarhy abhinne svasaṃpūrṇe tadā paścāt punar yadā /
children.translated_text: Then, in the undivided, self-complete [reality] — then, afterwards, again when,

children.text: parataś ceti ko nv eṣa vācoyuktiparigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: and beyond — what is this adoption of mere verbal propriety?

children.text: atra brūmaḥ satyam eva vastutas tu sphuṭātmani /
children.translated_text: Here we say: Truly indeed, in reality, in that which is clear in nature,
even in the manifestation of the emission of reality, even in time whose nature has opened forth —
awareness does not have these conceptualizations of before and after;
for time becomes a differentiator by [being] a qualifier.

children.text: viśeṣaṇaṃ ca tat proktaṃ samaśīrṣikayaiva yat /
children.translated_text: And that is said to be a qualifier which, by difference,

children.text: bhedena vedyatām eti yathā nīlaṃ saroruhaṃ //
children.translated_text: comes to be known, as [for example] a blue lotus.

children.text: na ca bodhasya vedyatvaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
children.translated_text: But the knowability of awareness is never established;
knowability is the state of being manifest, and that is through the grace of light (<s>prakāśa</s>).

children.text: prakāśaḥ sa sa bodhaś ca na ced bodhāntarasthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: That light is itself awareness; otherwise, from the positing of another awareness,
from the restriction of illumination, an infinite regress would surely follow.

children.text: ata eva vimūḍhā ye bodham aprathamānakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those deluded ones who would say that awareness
is not self-manifest but is of the nature of manifesting objects — they are deceived by their own words.

children.text: tasmāt kālo na bodhasya bhedakatvāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, time is not capable of being a differentiator of awareness;
nor is time capable of becoming a differentiator of the knowable.

children.text: viśvaṃ hi bodhābhinnaṃ tad atathātve na bhāsate /
children.translated_text: For the universe is non-different from awareness; without being so, it does not appear.
Pervaded by light, an entity wondrously shines forth.
Thus there would be the illumination of the universe — eternal for everything;

children.text: sati prakāśe bodhākhye sa prakāśatvam aśnute //
children.translated_text: when there is the light called awareness, it attains the state of being illuminated.

children.text: aprakāśo 'pi bhāvaś cet prakāśātmā sa vedyate /
children.translated_text: Even a non-luminous entity, if known as having the nature of light —

children.text: aprakāśas tv asau bhāva ity atra śaraṇaṃ tamaḥ //
children.translated_text: but if that entity is non-luminous, then darkness would be the refuge in this matter.

children.text: yaś cāprakāśo bhāvātmā prakāśātmā sa cet kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if the entity that is non-luminous in nature is made to have the nature of light,

children.text: nūnaṃ sa bhāvo naṣṭaḥ syāt svāprakāśatvavicyuteḥ //
children.translated_text: then surely that entity would be destroyed, through the loss of its own non-luminosity.

children.text: nātadrūpaṃ prakāśaṃ ca kartuṃ vidhir api kṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the creator (<s>Vidhi</s>) is not capable of making that which is not of such form into light.

children.text: nanv etāvad idaṃbhāvaḥ prakāśe sati bhāsate //
children.translated_text: Now, this much [is certain]: the this-ness [of an entity] appears when there is light.

children.text: astv etad eva kiṃtv ittham aprakāśaḥ prakāśatām /
children.translated_text: Let that be so; but thus, the non-luminous [becomes] luminous.
And when the non-luminosity of an entity is made luminous —

children.text: naivaṃ prakāśito bhāva iti vastusthitir bhavet /
children.translated_text: the entity is in no way illuminated — such would be the actual state of affairs.

children.text: tad alaṃ vyatiriktena prakāśena śivas tathā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, enough with a separate light! <s>Śiva</s> is thus [established].

children.text: tasmāt prakāśa evāsau gīto yaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that which is called the supreme <s>Śiva</s> is itself light (<s>prakāśa</s>).
He alone, of inconceivable majesty, whirling with unbridled sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>),

children.text: prakāśate tathā tais taiḥ svabhāvair acyutasthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: shines forth with those various own-natures, [his] position unshaken.

children.text: nātra sarvatra sarvajñabhāvaḥ kaś cana śaṅkyate //
children.translated_text: Herein, everywhere, no state of omniscience is to be doubted.

children.text: ahaṃ caitro ghaṭaṃ vedmi na paṭaṃ, veda taṃ tv ayaṃ. /
children.translated_text: "I, <s>Caitra</s>, know the pot but not the cloth; this one knows that [cloth].

children.text: nāyaṃ vetti paṭaḥ, so 'haṃ jāne ghaṭapaṭāv iti //
children.translated_text: This one does not know the cloth. That I know both the pot and the cloth."

children.text: vediṣyāmi na vā, pūrvam ajānāṃ naiva vā kva cit, /
children.translated_text: "I will know, or perhaps not; before, I did not know, or perhaps never anywhere;
I know sequentially, simultaneously, by both, or by neither."

children.text: sarvaṃ vedmi, na kiṃ cic ca jāne. naivāsmi kaś cana /
children.translated_text: "I know everything; I know nothing at all. I am not at all

children.text: bhāvātmā, nanu naivāham. ahaṃ sarvaṃ ca sarvadā. //
children.translated_text: any entity whatsoever. Indeed I am not. I am everything, always."

children.text: sarvam asmy aham evaikaḥ kiṃ sarvam itarad bhavet /
children.translated_text: "I alone am everything. What could anything else be?"
— thus, this one light alone bursts forth in manifold ways.

children.text: nanv eko yady asaḥ kaś cit, prakāśo na tadā paraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, if it is one, [yet] someone is nonexistent — then there would be no other light.

children.text: kathaṃ bhaved. aho mūḍhaḥ kathaṃ vyutpādyatām ayam //
children.translated_text: How could it be? Ah, [he is] deluded! How is this one to be instructed?
The one light, through sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>), shines forth in variegated form.

children.text: vastutaś ca na citro 'sau, nācitro bhedadūṣaṇāt //
children.translated_text: And in reality, it is neither variegated, nor non-variegated — because of the fault of division.
If, in the illumination of a pot, the illumination of a cloth were possible,

children.text: nāsau ghaṭaprakāśaḥ syād dviprakāśo hy asau bhavet //
children.translated_text: then that would not be the illumination of the pot; for it would be a double illumination.

children.text: so 'pi cāstv eva, no nāsti tad idaṃ tvatpracoditam /
children.translated_text: Let that too exist! But no, what you have proposed —

children.text: ghaṭātmanā prakāśo 'sya mā bhūd ity avatiṣṭhate //
children.translated_text: that there be no illumination of this [cloth] in the form of the pot — that remains [your position].
But that is improper: since light is awareness, its self-bursting-forth

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ yadi tat ko 'yaṃ vṛthā vāgjālaḍambaraḥ //
children.translated_text: is its defining characteristic; if so, what is this vain web of words?
Delimited illumination is said to be the characteristic of the insentient;

children.text: jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate //
children.translated_text: awareness is distinct from the insentient, since it is not limited.

children.text: tasmād arkasya sadbhāve siddhe kaḥ khalu bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the existence of the sun is established, what fool indeed
would say: "How does this [sun] illuminate the entire earth with its own rays?"
Therefore, when this light is established, whatever conceptualizations of light [are made] —
all those are the preservation of the conduct of the consorts who have been enjoyed by all.

children.text: asiddhau ca prakāśasya ko 'haṃ kiṃ tvaṃ tamo 'pi kim /
children.translated_text: And if light were not established — who am I? What are you? What even is darkness?

children.text: na kiṃ cid api vā kiṃ syāt tūṣṇīṃ syād api vā katham //
children.translated_text: Would it be nothing at all? Or would there be silence? But how even [silence]?
Therefore, for those entities who have attained the share of <s>Bhairava</s> through identity with light,

children.text: bhāvānām api kālo 'yaṃ na kiṃ cit kartum arhati //
children.translated_text: this time is not capable of doing anything [to them].
Now then, in what manner is that — the sequence of statements beginning with 'that' and so forth?

children.text: śrūyatām uktam apy etat punar nirbhajya bhaṇyate //
children.translated_text: Listen: though already stated, it is being said again with analysis.

children.text: yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa evāyaṃ pratibhāti tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: That which is <s>Prakāśa</s> (luminous consciousness) — this very [reality] shines forth in various ways,

children.text: naiva cānyasya kasyāpi sa tu bhāty eva kevalam //
children.translated_text: and nothing else whatsoever exists; it alone shines, simply.
That very [consciousness], supremely generous, is the illuminator of everything;
being autonomous (<s>svatantra</s>), its will-power (<s>icchāśakti</s>) is called <s>svātantrya</s> (absolute freedom).
And that [consciousness] reposes in its own Self, because nothing other [than it] exists;
this very repose in one's own Self is called the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) of the Lord.
This very greatness of his <s>svātantrya</s> (freedom) — the non-separate existence from his own nature —
causes the phantasmagoria of entities to shine forth in his own luminous abode, his own self-luminosity.

children.text: bhāsanā ca kriyāśaktir iti śāstreṣu kathyate /
children.translated_text: And this illumination is called <s>kriyāśakti</s> (the power of action) in the scriptures —
by which the diverse articulation of tattvas and the like is differentiated.
But how can illumination be conceived without being illuminated [itself]?

children.text: tad asyāntaḥsthitaṃ bhānaṃ jñānaśaktir ahaṃ smṛtā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the internal luminosity that resides within it is known as <s>jñānaśakti</s> (the power of knowledge), called 'I.'

children.text: etāvad asya devasya yad rūpaṃ svātmamātrataḥ /
children.translated_text: This much is the nature of this Lord, from his own Self alone;

children.text: sa unmeṣa iti proktaḥ pañcaśaktis tato vibhuḥ //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening/blossoming); hence the Lord is [endowed with] five <s>śaktis</s> (powers).

children.text: triśaktir ekaśaktir vā devo vā kevalaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether the Lord is said to have three <s>śaktis</s>, or one <s>śakti</s>, or stands alone —

children.text: śaktir evātha devī sā sāraśāstre nirūpyate //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> is indeed the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) — this is determined in the essential scripture.
And it will be stated hereafter, from [the verse] beginning 'The Creator of the world has declared...' —
that She, being one, goes to multiplicity — so says the Great Lord.
And this [Lord], established in the well-being of his own Self, in the repose of overflowing <s>ānanda</s> (bliss),
is expressed by cognate verbal compositions such as '<s>Bhairava</s>' and the like.

children.text: savidhaṃ dūragaṃ vāpi yady apy asya na vastutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Although in reality there is nothing whatsoever near or far from this Lord —

children.text: śabdajātaṃ bhavet kiṃ cid anyad apy atha vā prabhoḥ //
children.translated_text: neither any word-category nor anything else —

children.text: tathā ca bhāsayaty eva deva eṣa tathā tathā /
children.translated_text: nevertheless, this Lord illuminates in various and various ways;
therefore, following that [illumination], this entire order of conceptual construction [proceeds].

children.text: na ca tat kalpanāmātraṃ tathātve 'py atha kā kṣitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is it mere conceptual construction — for even if it were so, what harm?

children.text: tathā saṃkalpatāṃ devo yad vā kalpayatāṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: Let the Lord conceptualize thus, or let those who conceptualize do so.
Thus, this [Lord], whose nature is <s>Prakāśa</s> (luminous consciousness), transcending the thirty-seven [tattvas],
while causing the appearance of diversity, illuminates <s>kāla</s> (time).
This very causing of the appearance of diversity is declared to be <s>kālaśakti</s> (the power of time);
therefore, appearing in conformity with this <s>kālaśakti</s>,
the coloring [of consciousness] such as 'that' and so forth proceeds from our [limited perspective].

children.text: na cāsau tatra nāsty eva tatra yan nāsti tat kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: Yet that [coloring] is neither non-existent there [in the ultimate reality], nor is it entirely absent — for what is not there, whence [could it come]?

children.text: anyatra tanyatāṃ nāma tat prakāśavaśaṃ sthitam /
children.translated_text: Let it be stretched elsewhere, if you will — it remains under the control of <s>Prakāśa</s> (consciousness).
But if so, [the objection arises:] in the other network of <s>tattvas</s> (categories), in the pure and impure [levels],
or even in the pure-and-impure level, or in the sphere of <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) —
there would be no distinction, because of the existence of pure <s>Bhairava</s> [everywhere].

children.text: narīnṛtyāmahe hanta yatnād vyākhyeyam eva naḥ /
children.translated_text: We are indeed dancing [joyfully]! We must explain with effort
what revolves spontaneously in the heart of the fortunate one!
For the distinction of pure and impure has no place in discourses on ultimate reality;

children.text: sa tu tatkṛta evāste mūḍhānāṃ dhiyi niścalaḥ //
children.translated_text: but that [distinction] remains, fashioned by that [māyā], firmly fixed in the understanding of the deluded.

children.text: nanu śuddhetaratvākhyo yadi bhedo na vāstavaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if the distinction called 'pure and impure' is not real,
then this very scripture, which wishes to expound [the truth], contradicts [itself] thereby.

children.text: aśuddhatvaṃ hi tattvānāṃ dīkṣayā śodhanaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the impurity of the <s>tattvas</s>, and hence their purification through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) —
and so forth — since the [scriptural] position here is predominantly centered on distinction.

children.text: ucyate nādvaye 'muṣmin dvaitaṃ nāsty eva sarvathā /
children.translated_text: We reply: it is not that in this non-dual [reality] duality does not exist at all;
for it has been stated that even in the all-pervading [Lord], barren of [real] distinction, the appearance of distinction [occurs].

children.text: tad eva khalu saṃsāre māyāvidyādibhiḥ padaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That very [appearance], in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), by such terms as <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and the like,

children.text: bandha ity ucyate tatra rūḍhāḥ saṃsāriṇo matāḥ //
children.translated_text: is called <s>bandha</s> (bondage); those established therein are regarded as <s>saṃsārins</s> (worldly beings).
From following the deliberation upon that [bondage], the determination of pure and impure and so forth [arises] for them.

children.text: kiṃ ca śāstram idaṃ samyag bhagavadyogadeśakam //
children.translated_text: Moreover, this scripture properly teaches the <s>yoga</s> (union) with the Lord.
And the <s>yoga</s> with the Lord is declared to be non-dual (<s>advaita</s>), free from pairs of opposites (<s>nirdvandva</s>).
Its instruction would be like this — if [the teaching] proceeds as far as [it appears] dual.
That which is expected [as possibly dual] is examined and examined again, [and shown to be non-dual];
for in non-duality, in the all-pervading <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: ābhyāsikī sthitir nāsti tau hi bhedaikajīvitau /
children.translated_text: there is no habitual state of entering and dwelling [as separate acts] — for those [concepts] have their life solely in duality.
Therefore, for the removal of all doubts about non-duality that may arise,

children.text: gurūṇāṃ ca śiśūnāṃ ca yatnaḥ sarvo vijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: the entire effort of both teachers and students unfolds.
Hence, here [in this text], duality is suspected and suspected [at every turn], and everything is set forth [to refute it];

children.text: tad yāvadgati saṃbhāvya na tu kutrāpy udāsyate /
children.translated_text: to the extent possible, it is anticipated — it is not treated with indifference anywhere.

children.text: tathā hi yadi nāmṛṣṭaṃ dvaitaṃ tarhy ekam eva sat //
children.translated_text: For if duality has not been wiped clean, then there is only one [reality] —
the <s>Brahman</s> of consciousness — enough with the determinations of counting and constructing <s>tattvas</s>!
Why then is the thirty-five-fold nature of the <s>tattvas</s> established?
Therefore, having grasped the [apparent] establishment of duality's distinctive existence to its fullest extent,

children.text: kṛtvā yas tatpratikṣepas tena niḥśaṅkatā bhavet //
children.translated_text: it is through its refutation that freedom from doubt would arise.
And this very [method] of instruction in [true] knowledge is by penetrating [the objections];
whatever [objections] may arise from the side of the opponents are split apart.

children.text: tathā hi śrīmatā stotre bhaṭṭanārāyaṇena tat /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the illustrious hymn by <s>Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa</s>,
'Salutations to You' — by raising and [then] shattering the delusion of those bewildered in <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: jñānānandaṃ ca nirdvandvaṃ deva vṛtvā vivṛṇvate /
children.translated_text: and by first enveloping [them in] '<s>jñānānanda</s> (knowledge-bliss), free from pairs of opposites' — [the hymn] reveals [the truth].
'Free from pairs of opposites' — by this, the state of non-duality (<s>nirdvaita</s>) is made manifest.
'And delusions are raised' — the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) here brings wonder.
And here, [the principle] 'it is non-duality alone' will be set forth further ahead.
The purification of the paths (<s>adhvaśuddhi</s>) and the like — [the demonstration] that these are untenable in duality — will be stated.

children.text: abhedena vinā naitan nanu bhedaṃ vināpi kim //
children.translated_text: Without non-difference [nothing works] — but then, what about without difference either?

children.text: satyaṃ kiṃtv advaye tattve bhedo 'pi na na yujyate /
children.translated_text: True; but in the non-dual <s>tattva</s> (reality), difference too is not unfitting.

children.text: idaṃ hi tat parādvaitaṃ bhedatyāgagrahau na yat //
children.translated_text: For this is that supreme non-duality (<s>parādvaita</s>) which is not [defined by] the rejection or acceptance of difference.
In difference, however, since all entities of the universe are established in their own respective natures,

children.text: abheda iti śabdo 'yaṃ manye bhedayate rasāt //
children.translated_text: this word 'non-difference' (<s>abheda</s>), I think, [actually] differentiates, in essence!
The Supreme Lord, it is said, manifests the construction of difference
Enough — the subject at hand is being examined.
and <s>kāla</s> (time) also unfolds accordingly.
in whatever way [He does];

children.text:
na tathāpi ca yāti bhinnatāṃ
paramārthena kadācid eva saḥ /
yugapat sa hi saṃvidātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet even so, He never truly goes into separateness in ultimate reality; for He is simultaneously of the nature of consciousness.

children.text: saṃvedane yad aham eṣa karomi citraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I, this variegated [one], experience' or 'I know' —
But if so — in this cognition whose essence is the reflective awareness of one compact state —

children.text: jānāmi vā tad apare 'pi na maitracaitra
prāyā vidadhyur athavāpi kathaṃ na vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: accomplish [this same awareness], or how could they not know [it]?
do not others too — not merely <s>Maitra</s> and <s>Caitra</s> [i.e., Tom, Dick, and Harry] —

children.text: idaṃ hi prabrūmaḥ svaparam iha nāsty ekam abhidam /

children.translated_text: Ah, the knot of <s>māyā</s> is most dense here for you! For we say this: there is no 'own' and 'other' here — there is one, non-different [reality].
these diverse expansions, shine in the Supreme Light — so it has been declared.
'I know' — this manifestation of the particular forms of pots, bodies, and the like,

children.text: tasmād ghaṭaṃ vedmy aham ity amutra
bhedo na kaścin nanu me ghaṭo 'yam /
children.translated_text: there is no distinction — 'surely this pot is mine' —
Therefore, in 'I know the pot,' therein
but this is not [truly] not-His — this is <s>Śiva</s>, this very [reality].
[yet] there is the appearance of distinction: 'it shines [as different]';
For this very reason, those headed by <s>Dvaipāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>), in the teachings of their own scriptures,
declare that 'mine-ness' (<s>mamakāra</s>) alone is death — because of its capacity to fragment [reality].
Thus, the colorings that arise from the adventitious conditions produced by the operation of <s>kāla</s> (time) —
'that' and so forth — are extended even in the Supreme Reality, [as appearances] of consciousness.

children.text: tatra pūrṇaikarūpatvāt sarvaṃ sarvatra cāpi tat /
children.translated_text: Therein, because of [its] nature as complete and singular, everything is everywhere in that [reality];

children.text: anyathā khaṇḍanāyogān na pūrṇā pūrṇatā bhavet //
children.translated_text: otherwise, due to the impossibility of fragmentation, completeness would not be complete.
Therefore, in the abode of <s>Bhairava</s> who is all-bearing in [His] completeness,
this teaching of the scripture has a fivefold nature — that of <s>Śāmbhava</s>. Subordinating the position of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Aṇu</s>,

children.text: nyakkṛtyaiṣa parāṃ devīṃ svātmany udrecya vartate /
children.translated_text: it elevates the Supreme <s>Devī</s> into its own Self and [thus] operates.

children.text: itthaṃ sa visisṛkṣuḥ san bhāvān visraṣṭṛtāpadāt //
children.translated_text: Thus, He, desiring to emit the entities, from the state of the Emitter —
first attained the state of surging, compact <s>ānanda</s> (bliss).
And in the state of the Emitter, even while partaking of the <s>āveśa</s> (immersion) of <s>visarga</s> (emission),
[about to] become empty, by the fullness of the compact <s>ānanda</s>-consciousness,
meanwhile, saturated with the <s>āveśa</s> of emission [which is] a portion of <s>ānandaśakti</s> (the power of bliss),
remaining [thus], full of the flood of his own <s>śaktis</s>, he became [and] will become.
[He is] of empty <s>śakti</s> — thus, of the nature of the triple cognition of variegated [experience].

children.text: tadāsau devadevaḥ syād visraṣṭari pade sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Then, that Lord of lords would be [clearly manifest] in the state of the Emitter.
Now, in the present aspect — are the past and future established [within it]?

children.text: kiṃ nāma bhavatā jñātaṃ te svatantre 'pi ke cana /
children.translated_text: What indeed have you understood? Those [aspects], even though autonomous,
are divided into past and future from the boundary of the present.

children.text: yac ca yatra na viśrāntaṃ tad vibhajyeta vai kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that which has not come to rest anywhere — how could it be divided?

children.text: kathaṃ cāvadhibhāvaḥ syād vartamānasya te prati //
children.translated_text: And how could the present have the nature of a boundary with respect to those [past and future]?

children.text: tayor avadhimattvaṃ vā tat praty api kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Or how could those two [past and future] have the nature of being bounded with respect to it [the present]?

children.text: viśvasya viśvam avadhis tadvad vā jāyate na kim //
children.translated_text: The universe is the boundary of the universe — or does it not arise just so?
Therefore, past and future are established within the cognition called 'present';

children.text: rūḍham eveti tatraiva yadi viśrāntim āvahet //
children.translated_text: and precisely therein, if [the yogin] were to bring [his awareness] to repose —
and if, right here, without projecting the entire
mandala of rays of conceptual construction, he were to remain for a moment, his own state arrested —
then he attains the stream that carries the nectar-flood of supreme <s>ānanda</s> (bliss),
whose sole savor is the wonder of the expansion of one's own nectar.

children.text: tathā hi sūryaraśmyoghapūrṇaḥ syāc candramā yadā /
children.translated_text: For example, when the moon is full of the flood of the sun's rays,

children.text: tadā sūryakarān bhūyo yāvan na visisṛkṣati //
children.translated_text: so long as it does not wish to emit the sun's rays again —
for that long, well-established in repose within the enjoyment of its own orb,
it is called the vessel for the satiation of the inner deities of the universal [rays].
Thus, when in the inner heart there abides the moonlight of one's own awakening,
adorned with the host of rays that are the sun of the illumination of entities —
one who reposes, in the inner beauty of the noble essence of <s>cit</s>-nectar —
since the inner flood of one's own nectar is not emitted outward —
from that very [interior], churning and surging inwardly,
of the nature of the 'I'-awareness that is the satiation of the inner circle of deities —
[this state] arises as long as the sequence of one's own faculties is unleashed;
when the assemblage of rays is restrained, through the absence of [external] manifestation,

children.text: na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyac ca vartamānād vibhajyate /
children.translated_text: neither past nor future is divided from the present;

children.text: avibhāgas tayor yāvat tāvat kā vartamānatā //
children.translated_text: as long as there is no division of those two, so long, what is 'present-ness'?
For that [present-ness] goes to differentiation by the natures of past and future;
therefore, having rested in this boundaryless <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness) for even a particle of a moment,
the <s>yogin</s>, devoted to the devouring of <s>kāla</s> (time), becomes a <s>khecara</s> (sky-wanderer) in an instant.

children.text: uktaṃ hi bhāvābhāso yaḥ kālaḥ sa kalanātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: For it has been stated: the appearance of entities is <s>kāla</s> (time), which is of the nature of <s>kalanā</s> (articulation);
the expansion of the rays of one's own consciousness — the [appearance and] non-appearance of entities — is none other than that.
Therefore, by blocking the mandala of paths through the restraint of one's own rays,
one becomes a <s>khecara</s> (sky-wanderer), devoted to the sole relish of devouring <s>kāla</s> (time).
Thus it has been stated by the Supreme Lord in the <s>tantra</s> called <s>Śrīḍāmara</s>:
'Having restrained one's own circle of rays and having drunk the unsurpassed nectar,
in the present — undelimited by both [past and future] times — one becomes blissful.'
But 'restraint' is not [truly applicable] in this [state] which is free from contraction;

children.text: tadabhāvān na visphāro grāsatṛptī tathātra ke //
children.translated_text: in the absence of that [restraint], there is no 'expansion'; then what are 'devouring' and 'satiation'?
However, by the method stated [above], restraint, expansion, devouring, and the like appear;

children.text: na tathābhāsanāc cānyad vastu viśvatra kiṃ cana //
children.translated_text: and there is no entity anywhere in the entire universe other than [such] appearance.
But enough of this extended conversation within the gathering of the <s>khecarīcakra</s> (the circle of sky-dwelling goddesses)!
And what [indeed] is the connection of this <s>Abhinavagupta</s> with the sequence of mystical experience?
We speak of the subject at hand: the variegated cognitions emitted by the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) —

children.text: yāvat tāvad tad ūrdhvordhvaṃ sroto yad bhedavarjitam //
children.translated_text: to that extent, that higher and higher stream which is free from distinction —
from it, the scriptures called <s>Saura</s>, <s>Bhargaśikhā</s>, and so forth were extended.
And in the <s>Bhargaśikhā</s>, the Lord, the Supreme Deity, has declared:

children.text: ūrdhvasrotodbhavaṃ jñānam idaṃ tat paramaṃ priye /
children.translated_text: 'This knowledge, O beloved, born from the upper stream, is supreme;
from the supreme sound (<s>nāda</s>), designating the form of higher and higher consciousness,
it indicates the distinction from the <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) that issued from the face of <s>Īśāna</s>.'
Here too, colored by the admixture of portions of prior distinction,
the attainments of knowledge weave those various confusions of scripture.

children.text: iha yāvat tu mukhyeyaṃ ṣaḍātmā śāstrasaṃtatiḥ //
children.translated_text: But here, the principal [tradition] is this sixfold continuity of scripture.
The <s>Trika</s> scriptures which belong to the first half of this [sixfold tradition] —
those are spoken of by the teachers under the designation of 'six halves.'
But this verbal sequence [is not to be taken literally]; it is because of the hidden secret nature [of the teaching].

children.text: evaṃ hi dvādaśārdhārdham ityādy api na kiṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: For if so, would it not also become 'twelve halves of halves' and so on?
Here, the triad of powers in its primary [form] is established in a state of completeness,
without mutual obstruction — full, of the nature of full consciousness.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ tu tritayaṃ kasyāṃcid guṇitājuṣi /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, the triad [exists] in a certain [power] that partakes of being predominant,
while in another [power] that partakes of being subordinate — this is called <s>yāmala</s> (coupled pair).
Subsequently, when the mass of objects is emitted, through the conjunction with the condition of various distinctions,
in the five powers of the self, which are [now] devoid of [their original] unity —
having the forms of the flash of consciousness, will, knowledge, action,
resplendent by virtue of the <s>pañcabrahma</s> (five <s>Brahmā</s> [faces/mantras]), born from the awareness of the emerging aspect of existence —
the form that has attained the nature of the scripture unfolds in exactly five ways.
For firstly, so long as the Blessed One brings forth the unfolding
of the mass of existents lying within, up to the infinite — so long is the state of the <s>Īśa</s> face.
Of the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action) that abides within, undifferentiated,

children.text: kramād unmiṣite tāvān eṣa sphāraḥ pratāyate /
children.translated_text: when it gradually opens, this expansion extends to that extent.
The clear expansion of the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action) will attain the status of <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
For in the essential nature of the <s>māyā</s> principle, it will be stated as '<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Īśānī</s>.'
Of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose body consists of the five <s>mantras</s>, who creates
the pure, impure, and mixed universe — the connection with the impure creation

children.text: asty eva pūrvakoṭyāṃ hi sarvam eva vyavasthitam //
children.translated_text: does indeed exist at the very first extremity, for everything is already established [there].

children.text: tathā hi svagṛhāt kvāpi yiyāsoḥ prathamakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: For just as, at the first moment when one desires to go somewhere from one's own house,

children.text: yāvat kiṃ cana gantavyaṃ yac ca tanmadhyavṛtti tu //
children.translated_text: whatever is to be traversed and whatever lies in between —
even in an instant, the possession of omniscience and omnipotence [is present].
This is precisely [the capacity] of those who are skilled in the unwavering particular aspects.
For just as [a swordsman's] intellect, comparable to contact with the edge of a fine-steel sword-point,
simultaneously with the flash [of awareness], draws out the particular aspects;
an expert whose knowledge of the reality of jewels is clear, [apprehends] those

children.text: tāṃs tān viśeṣāṃś cinute ratnānāṃ bhūyasām api //
children.translated_text: various particular aspects of many jewels shown [to him] at the [instant of] lightning;
[and a musician], absorbed in a <s>vīṇā</s> skillfully played
with the touch-lightness of an array of many notes in a single expanse, knows the variety;
one whose auditory sense rests on the edge [of perception] through the flow of dense practice
indeed knows even the excess or deficiency of <s>śrutis</s> (micro-intervals) within those note-portions.
Let alone in this doctrine of non-difference — [where] this is accomplished effortlessly —

children.text: etad yatra vibhāte 'pi bhede vāstavam advayam //
children.translated_text: even where difference is manifest, there is real non-duality.

children.text: bhedaikajīvite śāstre yāvad etad sthitaṃ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: So far as this is clearly established even in a scripture whose life consists solely of difference —
for <s>Pātañjali</s> (the follower of <s>Patañjali</s>), in the chapter named '<s>Vibhūti</s>' (powers),

children.text: nyarūpyata `prātibhād vā sarvam' atra mayāpi ca /
children.translated_text: has formulated: 'Or, from <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive flash), [one knows] everything.' And by me also [it is said]:
In the <s>prātibha</s> — the first opening [of awareness],
which is of the nature of consciousness, undivided — there abides the self of all flashing-forth, the arising of the fruit of all accomplishments.
Thus, in the world being created, what is forcibly taken up for creation,
though impure, and though possessing the variety of diverse forms,
in the form of a generic aspect — [like] a petal, beautiful in its aspect of difference —
remains in a half-opened state. This is the state that partakes of both difference and non-difference.
Therefore, in that [principle] called <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
which is of the nature of <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) — due to a slight taint of impurity, there is the state of being both supreme and non-supreme.
Therefore, from this [state] which is enjoyed by <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord), those who partake of the stage above —
from eagerness to manifest <s>māyā</s>, and likewise those who possess the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) thereof —
there arises diverse consultation (<s>mantraṇa</s>) consisting of the commencement of many activities,
and from the continuity of great knowledge there arises what bestows <s>Śiva</s>-hood.
For that other [lower] state of being is enveloped by the supreme state;

children.text: na tu rūḍhim upāgacched aśuddhordhvavidhāv iva /
children.translated_text: it does not, however, take firm root as it does in the higher realm of the impure.
Therefore, those established in other teachings — <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, Buddhist, and the like —

children.text: yathā samyaṅ na mucyante na tathā śaivasaṃskṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: are not properly liberated in the same way as those consecrated in the <s>Śaiva</s> [tradition].
In the <s>Atimārga</s>, <s>Krama</s>, <s>Kula</s>, <s>Trika</s>, <s>Srota</s>, and inner [paths] and the like —

children.text: parameśānaśāstre tu ye samyag dīkṣitā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: however, those men who are properly initiated in the teaching of the Supreme Lord —

children.text: teṣāṃ naivāpavargasya lābhe bhedo 'sti kaś cana //
children.translated_text: for them there is no difference whatsoever in the attainment of liberation.
Nor is there any other means to liberation beyond this.
Only in some [paths], through effortlessness, by the process of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living),

children.text: śīghram eva parā siddhir yathāsmaddarśaneṣv iti /
children.translated_text: the supreme accomplishment [comes] quickly — as in our [Trika] viewpoints.
In some, through the sequential procedure of the series of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) in proper order, over a long time,

children.text: tais taiḥ kriyākalāpaiś ca labhyate paramaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: and through various aggregates of rituals, the supreme fruit is obtained.

children.text: ata evāsti saṃhāradṛśām kauliky apīha dṛk //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even those with the vision of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>) have the <s>Kaulika</s> (Kaula) vision here.
As stated: 'Beginning with <s>Kālapāda</s>, one should initiate even a <s>śvapaca</s> (dog-cooker, outcaste).'
The five [powers] beginning with the flash of consciousness, which were previously declared
without differentiation, in the supreme Lord of consciousness, <s>Bhairava</s>, through inherence —
those very [powers], differentiated through the aspect of the limiting adjunct of [created] existence,
nourish the aspect of difference alone, though formerly they partook of non-difference.
For just as the enjoyment of cooked rice, which nourishes the body,
[can] through the accumulation and excess of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), cause the body to waste away.
Now, even in the non-difference of the Lord, who is the Self of all, due to his not departing from his own [nature] —

children.text: vikāriṣv eva yogyānām upādhīnāṃ gatiḥ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: whence comes the applicability of limiting adjuncts, which are capable [of affecting] only changeable things?
That difference in <s>Bhairava</s> through the conditioning of those adjuncts arises from the existence of [created] states —
this [objection] is not fit to ascend the ground of our doctrine.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ vikāriṇo bhāvāḥ santīti hy atisāhasam //
children.translated_text: For [to say] that changeable states exist in silence is indeed too rash.

children.text: devaḥ sa eva viśvātmā tathārūpeṇa bhāsate /
children.translated_text: The Lord, that very universal Self, shines in precisely such a form.
The appearance of the differentiated in the unconditioned, undifferentiated [Lord] is through limiting adjuncts.

children.text: nanv itthaṃ tad asatyaṃ syāt kathaṃ satyaṃ tad eva hi /
children.translated_text: But if so, would that [appearance] not be unreal? How can it be real?

children.text: tathāvabhāsanād anyat kva kiṃ satyaṃ nirūpyatām //
children.translated_text: Since it appears in precisely that way — what else and where is established as real? Let it be determined!

children.text: nanv evaṃ svapnasaṃsāraḥ kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃtv asau kila /
children.translated_text: But if so, the dream-world — what is real? However, that [dream]
is said to be 'unreal' only because it is barren of producing the desired object — nothing more.
And this will be established ahead in detail, furnished with reasoning.

children.text: tasmād unmeṣaśaktir yā pūrvam āsīd abhedinī //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the power of unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>) that was formerly non-differentiating —
that, being of the nature of the unfolding of [created] existence, has attained the state of <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.

children.text: yad abhinnaṃ tad agrāhyaṃ yac ca grāhakam īśvaram //
children.translated_text: What was undifferentiated — that [was both] the un-graspable and the grasper, the Lord.

children.text: adhunā tat sthitaṃ grāhyaṃ bhedāt tadgrāhakaṃ bhidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now it stands as the graspable, through differentiation, and its grasper [stands as] the differentiator,
called '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (person), from the connection with the commencement of creation.
And the primary face is also called [thus] because of the very clear re-cognition [it involves].
Therefore, here, [there are described things] that obstruct the state of expansion-existence (<s>visarga</s>) —
such as the aggregation of various diseases, seizures, poisons, and the like.
Those states whose diseases have been pacified and well-settled through various rational methods —
here [at this level] they become very clear — these states whose function consists solely of difference.

children.text: bhāvatvam eva yat sarvaṃ tat tv idaṃ pūrvajaṃ mukham //
children.translated_text: That which is simply the state of being an existent — all of that is this first-born face.
And <s>Īśāna</s>'s [designation as] the upper face is due to the superiority of [its] qualities in every respect.
However, there are no constructions of directional difference in what is devoid of the measurement of space and time.

children.text: yo hi yasmād guṇotkṛṣṭa iti cordhvo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: For whatever is superior in qualities to whatever — that will be 'above' [it].
Then, when [the Lord] properly wills the states through the power of the glory of will —

children.text: tadecchāyāṃ samārūḍhāḥ sā cecchā caiva nirmalā /
children.translated_text: when they are mounted upon that will, and that will itself is pure,
by which, through the state of identity [with the will], they touch the unity of consciousness —
however, concealed by the covering of will tinged by limiting adjuncts,

children.text: te tadānīṃ sthitā bhāvā devas tu svaiṣaṇāsthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: those states at that time remain hidden; but the Lord is established in his own desiring.
With consciousness-face turned away, he does not inhabit

children.text: pūrṇām adhyuṣitas tena suṣupta iva bhāsate //
children.translated_text: the supreme, complete state — therefore he appears as if in deep sleep.

children.text: asuptaś ca prabuddhatvāt tasya svāpo nimīlanam /
children.translated_text: Yet he is not asleep, being awake. His sleep is a closing [of eyes]
that does not truly exist in the ultimate sense — [it is only apparent] in the consciousness of <s>Bhairava</s>-bliss.
For when that supreme light has assumed the state of being closed,
[one may ask:] from dissolution, where does this 'closed-ness' of it appear?
An unmanifest thing is not a [real] thing — like a sky-lotus, or the window of a sky-house.
Or even that [sky-lotus] has a constructed form [and] appears in the light of consciousness.

children.text: tad amīlita evāyaṃ nimīlann iva tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this [Lord] is actually open-eyed, [only] standing as if closing [his eyes].
For the power of the mighty ones, who accomplish the impossible, is beyond conceptualization.

children.text: idaṃ sukhena ghaṭate duḥkhena ghaṭate tv idaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'This is easily accomplished; this is accomplished with difficulty' —

children.text: ity ābhāsanavaicitrye svatantro hi sa eva naḥ //
children.translated_text: in this variety of manifestation, he alone [the Lord] is indeed autonomous for us.

children.text: tad eva tasya svātantryaṃ śaktir niyatināmikā /
children.translated_text: That very autonomy of his is the power named <s>niyati</s> (regulation/destiny),

children.text: yayā ruddhaḥ paśur jātu svātantryaṃ naiva vindati //
children.translated_text: by which the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) never obtains autonomy.
In relation to the soul, the Lord's accomplishment of the impossible is spoken of by the force [of this];

children.text: na hi viśvātmanaḥ kiṃ cit sughaṭaṃ vātha durghaṭam //
children.translated_text: for nothing is easy or difficult for the universal Self.

children.text: kiṃ muhur muhur etenāsakṛn nanu nirūpitam /
children.translated_text: Why [speak of this] again and again? Has it not been established many times already?

children.text: hantāvismṛtiśīlaṃ tvāṃ praty etat syād apārthakam //
children.translated_text: Alas! For you who are prone to forgetfulness, this would be purposeless;

children.text: ekam uddiśya kiṃtv etatsaṃrambho na virājate /
children.translated_text: however, in targeting one [particular person], this effort does not fail to shine,
for why should the monsoon clouds [exist] for the prosperity of a single sprout?

children.text: marmasthānam idaṃ cātra vyutpādyo hi janaḥ sa ca /
children.translated_text: And this is the vital point here: the person to be instructed is indeed one who
is pervaded, in the soil of the heart — [soil] ploughed by the mass of <s>karmas</s> — with softness,
by thickets of endlessly sprouting <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructions) arisen from the seed of <s>māyā</s>,
cultivated by the propriety of speech born from the conviction of difference.
Until this [soil] is, again and again, [burned] by the flames of the great forest-fire of [true] knowledge,

children.text: nālabdhā tāvad asyaitad dvaitaṃ rohet punaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: until that is not obtained, this duality will sprout again and again in him.
When the tree of difference is split by hordes of sharp axe-like reasonings,
ignited by the fire of true knowledge, it never sprouts again.
Thus, when the Lord is seated in the aspect of deep sleep,
the states, though existing, come to a state of non-existence — like a hole or a wood-apple [that appears empty inside].

children.text: atra tādṛśam eva svaṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyanirbharam /
children.translated_text: Here, its own knowledge, of just such a nature, saturated with dispassion,
indescribable, without support, unfolded in its distinct aspects.
[Those] wearing garlands of skulls as ornaments, dwelling in the cremation ground,
turned away from us, operating in the domain of the aggregate of elements —

children.text: bhoktā hy ahaṃ kaḥ kila deha eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: and who indeed is the enjoyer? This body —
All that is to be enjoyed [reaches] the limit of disgust,
of essence is ever found in any part of it.
is mere skin and bones; not even the slightest trace
Those who thus practice, ascending moment by moment
to the supreme wealth of dispassion, close [their eyes to the world] — struck by that [realization].
'What is this?' — even toward suffering, the activities of the senses rush forth;

children.text: etad evam iti prāyo virajyante sukhād api //
children.translated_text: 'It is just so' — [with this understanding] they mostly become dispassionate even from pleasure.
When there is freedom from craving for the mass of objects both seen and heard of, [they are] those of mastered intellect;
that supreme [state] of the designation '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (person) is also [called] <s>guṇavaitṛṣṇya</s> (freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s>).

children.text: nanv akāṇḍe 'pi pṛcchāmaḥ kiṃ cid yadi na kupyate /
children.translated_text: Now, even if we ask something out of turn — if [the teacher] does not become angry:
Why, out of turn, at the boundary where the pot [of the Sāṅkhya's categories] of the section on difference [and] the section on difference [breaks] —

children.text: tarhi saṃvid iyaṃ śuddhā svabhāvād eva cet katham /
children.translated_text: then, if this consciousness is pure by its very nature, how is it that
one craves with relish even impure enjoyments?
Now, where has the pride of being 'not prone to forgetfulness' gone?

children.text: alaṃ vā buddhyupālabdhair uktam apy etad ucyate //
children.translated_text: Enough of reproaches from the intellect — though [this] has been said, let it be said [again]:
Consciousness is, by its very nature, of the ultimate nature of light;
it shines through its conjunction with the manifestation of the entire universe — this has been well demonstrated.

children.text: ataś ca saṃvido devyā viśvasmin bhāvamaṇḍale /
children.translated_text: And so, of the goddess Consciousness, in this entire circle of existents,
does the springing forth within her own self become liable to refutation?
Even when difference is manifested by the power of the Supreme Lord,
even then consciousness 'runs' toward the states — thus it is analyzed.
Just as a clod, a lake, a flame, a breath, a pot, [and] the sky — [each] standing [in its respective state] —
attains the nature of earth, water, great fire, wind, infinite space, [and] void —

children.text: yāty eva mitirūpeyaṃ saṃvit svocchalitā kramāt /
children.translated_text: this consciousness, having sprung forth, progressively in the form of measurement,
pursues only states that are homogeneous with the nature of consciousness.
And thus this was formulated by a certain Supreme Lord:
'Who is able to make the water of a pond flow downhill [i.e., to its natural level]?'
But when that [pond] is full, streams [flow] in all directions.

children.text: nanu kiṃ kāṃś cid evetthaṃ saiṣā svaniyater balāt //
children.translated_text: Now, does it [consciousness] run thus toward only certain [objects], by the force of its own regulation?

children.text: itthaṃ dhāvati tac cāsyā rāgatattvātmakaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus it runs — and that body of hers is of the nature of the <s>rāga</s> (attachment) principle;

children.text: tatrāpi ca tathā rāgābhāsa eva sa dhāryatām //
children.translated_text: yet even there, let that be held as a mere appearance of <s>rāga</s>.
But in what is of the nature of consciousness, let there be some attachment that is of the nature of 'non-dyeing' [i.e., untainted].

children.text: nanv itthaṃ cet kathaṃ nāma sā kutrāpi virajyate //
children.translated_text: But if so, how then does consciousness become dispassionate anywhere?

children.text: hanta prakṛta evāyaṃ vādaḥ saṃgatim āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Aha! This very argument has arrived at our main subject!

children.text: yadā hi citir evaiṣā sarvataḥ saṃkucatsthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: For when this very <s>citi</s> (consciousness) is in a state of contracting everywhere,
progressively from the means of enjoyment, from the objects of enjoyment, from the body, from the senses,

children.text: bhogād bhoktus tathā śūnyā mahāpralayabhāg iva //
children.translated_text: from enjoyment, from the enjoyer — likewise becoming void, as if partaking of the great dissolution —
this state of the nature of <s>Rudra</s> arises, since it is the state of destruction (<s>saṃhāra</s>).

children.text: sadyojātaś ca yad rudraḥ puruṣaś ceśvarātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: And <s>Sadyojāta</s> is also <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s> is also of the nature of <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: śrīmān sadāśivo deva īśānaś ceti gīyate /
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the Lord, is sung as <s>Īśāna</s>;

children.text: viṣṇur vāmaḥ kajy aghora iti caitad bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> [is known as] <s>Vāma</s>, and <s>Aghora</s> — this [fivefold division] will be [explained].
Because each one [of these five], possessing all powers internally,
expands — these are called <s>Brahmans</s> (the five sacred utterances), due to their greatness and their expanding the universe.
Since in the aspect of the predominance of the other powers [within each],
each one individually has a connection with the fivefold causation of <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest.

children.text: saiva śāstreṣu bhedena teṣu teṣu pratanyate /
children.translated_text: That very [fivefold nature] is variously extended in different scriptures;

children.text: ataś ca sadyojāte 'smin mukhyā raudradaśā sthitā //
children.translated_text: thus in this <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the principal state is that of <s>Rudra</s>.
And that [state], though in the form of contraction,
will become an expansion of consciousness, because the <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> aspects, being absorbed,
forcibly subordinate [everything]. The state beginning with 'the non-existence of objects' has <s>Rudra</s> as its presiding deity —
so was formulated by the glorious <s>Utpala</s> (master <s>Utpaladeva</s>) as 'differentiated objects of cognition.'
Though [the universe] has arisen, insofar as it has undergone contraction in the mere essence of differentiation,
therefore the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and the experienced (<s>bhogya</s>) clearly interchange here.

children.text: ajātam iva tad viśvam atra sadyo 'vabhāsate /
children.translated_text: That universe appears here as though unborn;
hence [this is called] the stage of <s>Sadyojāta</s> (the 'just-born'), whose essence is the cognition of the void.

children.text: tataḥ śūnyapadasyāntar yāvat sa ca vivikṣati /
children.translated_text: Then, insofar as he, within the stage of the void,

children.text: devas tāvat svayaṃ bodhe viśvaṃ procchalati sthitam //
children.translated_text: wishes to manifest — to that extent, the Lord, in [his own] awareness, [causes] the universe, which is [already] present, to surge forth.
This expanding <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) of the Lord knows [the universe] —
the absorption of both [experiencer and experienced] in the luminous ground of the expanding consciousness is thus established.

children.text: saṃvidaḥ śūnyarūpāyā vikāso viśvam eva tat /
children.translated_text: The expansion of consciousness in the form of the void is the universe itself;
for just as one who is immersed in the fullness of deep sleep's repose
cognizes those various aspects of houses, markets, and the like — called the state of dream —

children.text: ata eva na sā sṛṣṭiḥ sthitir eva tu sā tathā //
children.translated_text: for that very reason, that is not a [new] creation, but rather a maintenance [of what already exists].
For with respect to previously created entities, it is merely a cognition;

children.text: tathā ca jāgrato rūpāt svapno bhedena jāyate //
children.translated_text: and thus, from the state of waking, dream arises as a differentiation.
However, the states of waking and the rest each have multiple sub-divisions;
therefore it is appropriate that [even dream] appears in the form of creation.

children.text: ato nijavibodhena tān bhāvān vyāpnuvan vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Hence, the Lord, pervading those entities through his own awareness,

children.text: etais tyājayate tāṃ svām audāsīnyadaśāṃ vibhuḥ //
children.translated_text: through them causes the abandonment of his own state of indifference.
This is the unfolding of the <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge); those entities that belong to the state of its cognition
attain fullness through the radiance of [the power's] expanding nature.
The supreme contraction indeed occurs at the stage of <s>Sadyojāta</s>,

children.text: yad eṣāṃ svasvarūpasya niṣṭhā naiva sma jāyate //
children.translated_text: since [in that stage] the establishment of each [entity's] own true nature simply does not arise.
Without ascending to consciousness, how can the determination be made
of [states like] being and non-being, inert and non-inert, 'not-blue' and 'blue,' and so forth?
As the master <s>Utpala</s> (teacher <s>Utpaladeva</s>) said: 'Just as of being and non-being, so
of the inert and the non-inert — there is certainly no distinction of their own nature [apart from consciousness].'
Therefore, releasing the state of self and other through the surging forth of the flood of awareness,
scattering everywhere the beautiful bliss of the infusion of consciousness,
wishing to appropriate the universe — which is of the single body of consciousness — into [his own] consciousness-self,
through the emission of [his] own power of awareness, that Lord is called <s>Vāma</s>.
Although he, through the predominance of his own power of awareness,
bestows upon entities their own form — nevertheless, in ultimate reality,

children.text: svīkartum icchan saṃhāram eṣāṃ kalpayate bhidaḥ /
children.translated_text: wishing to reappropriate [them], he projects differentiation in them for the purpose of [their eventual] dissolution;
therefore, in the establishment of differentiation, he is the supreme Lord [called] <s>Vāma</s>.
Here, knowledge that flows forth from auspiciousness extends;

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ socyate teṣāṃ bhinnānāṃ svīkriyaiva yā //
children.translated_text: their 'auspiciousness' (<s>saubhāgya</s>) is said to be the very reappropriation of differentiated [entities].
And of the diverse entities that are limbs of experience, through his own power,
from the vision of the play of his own curiosity (<s>kautuka</s>) — consciousness itself surges forth.
That very [consciousness], through its inherent passion, colors the universe;

children.text: vyakto hi rañjayed viśvaṃ vyaktiś cāsya svarūpataḥ //
children.translated_text: for one who is manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) indeed colors the universe, and his manifestation is from his own nature.
That very surged-forth state, the arising of the flood of the desire to appropriate —
he abides for a moment in the totality of its rays' essence, with undivided awareness.

children.text: kiṃ nākarṣati kiṃ naiṣa ca bhāvayati yogavit /
children.translated_text: What does this knower of <s>yoga</s> not attract? What does he not bring into being?

children.text: tata evocyate śāstre nārakto rañjayed iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said in scripture: 'One who is not colored [by passion] cannot color [the world].'
[One should be] established in desire, situated in the midst of desire, enveloped by the goad of desire;

children.text: kāmena sādhayet kāmān kāmaṃ kāmeṣu yojayet //
children.translated_text: through desire one should accomplish desires; one should unite desire with desires.
Desire is the will to reappropriate; through the conjunction of veiling that [will],

children.text: viśvaṃ sādhayate kāmī kāmatattvam idaṃ yataḥ //
children.translated_text: the desirer accomplishes the universe — for this is the reality of <s>Kāma</s> (desire).

children.text: tathā hi parame svātmany adhyāsya sthairyam añjasā /
children.translated_text: For thus, having directly established firmness in [one's] own supreme Self,
through the process of concealing the expanding facets of awareness surging from that —
the universe, subordinated to the goad of desire, appears as a servant.
And by this very reasoning of inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) accomplishment, through [one's] own arising,

children.text: prāṇaḥ puryaṣṭakaṃ dehaṃ vyāpya viśvaṃ prakarṣati /
children.translated_text: <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), pervading the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), the [gross] body, and the universe, extends [its power].
Because of the manifestation of that reality, the reality of <s>Kāma</s> (desire),

children.text: siddhacakreṣv idaṃ gopyaṃ kiṃ vā na prakaṭīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: this is to be kept secret in the circles of <s>Siddhas</s> (adepts) — or rather, it has not been made manifest [before].
Having issued forth from the bliss of the void, the Lord, whose nature is the surging forth [of consciousness],
proceeds by expanding his own powers;

children.text: yatrāsya pravivikṣāsti yataś ca prāvṛtad vibhuḥ //
children.translated_text: wherever there is his desire to enter, and from wherever the Lord has extended —

children.text: sarvāḥ śaktīr asau bhāvaḥ svātmany udrecya vartate /
children.translated_text: that entity exists by elevating all powers within its own self;

children.text: tataś cidātmako devo nyagbhūta iva bhāsate //
children.translated_text: hence the consciousness-natured Lord appears as if subordinated [to the entity].
But these [powers] — <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening-forth), <s>icchā</s> (will), <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), and <s>kriyā</s> (action) — shine forth as arisen;
therefore, although he appears endowed with a tetrad [of powers],
nevertheless, how can there be any enumeration of his powers in reality?
Since herein lies the art of uprooting the aspect of the differentiation of entities.
Established therein, the practice transcends the domain of the ordinary world.
Due to the variety of infinite powers, even here [at this level], practices like <s>uccāṭana</s> (expulsion) and the rest [are possible].

children.text: saṃhāralīlābhūyiṣṭhā api tās tāḥ kriyāḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those various practices, though predominantly of the play of dissolution, are [firmly] established.

children.text: tad itthaṃ jñānaśaktyante bhāvānāṃ vapuṣi sthite //
children.translated_text: Thus, when [entities] abide in the body [constituted by] the <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge) at its culmination,
then the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action), being the ultimate [stage], dissolves them with care.
Just as the most subtle power called <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening-forth), at the outermost limit,
appears as if in a gross form due to the coarseness of the entities to be created —
so too this <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action), within which entities have been absorbed (<s>nimeṣita</s>),
resting in its own nature, unfolds as if it were complete.

children.text: nanv asty eva kriyā yasyāṃ bhedaḥ pratyavabhāsate //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But there is indeed an action in which differentiation is manifest —

children.text: maivaṃ sarvā kriyā bhedaṃ praty uta prāg vyapohati /
children.translated_text: [how can action dissolve difference?]' Not so — all action rather eliminates differentiation before [producing its result].
For in the domain of differentiation, [the components] firewood, flame, and rice

children.text: ta eva pākāviṣṭatve bhedaṃ projjhanti sādaram /
children.translated_text: — those very same, when subjected to cooking, lovingly abandon their differentiation.

children.text: yadi bhinnasvarūpās te pākaikyaṃ tat kathaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: If they were of essentially different natures, how could the unity of cooking arise?

children.text: bhinnaṃ svarūpam aṅgānāṃ na hi yuktyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: An [essentially] different nature of the components simply cannot be justified by reason.

children.text: nanu pāko na kaś cit sa yat tan nānāsvarūpakam //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But cooking is nothing [in itself]; that which has manifold forms
— burning, moistening, drying, and the like — is called cooking;

children.text: bhinnā eva kriyāḥ sarvāḥ phalam ekaṃ prati sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: all these are distinct actions, [but since they are] directed toward a single result,

children.text: pāka ity ucyate nānyā kriyā nāmāsti kācana /
children.translated_text: they are called cooking — there is no other [single] action by that name.'

children.text: etad eva kathaṃ bahvya ekaṃ phalam abhīpsitam //
children.translated_text: Reply: How is it that these many [actions], directed toward a single desired result,

children.text: kathaṃ saṃpādayeyus tāḥ. pūrvoktād eva hetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: can bring it about? — precisely from the cause stated before.
Objection: 'Just as a single cognition is clearly produced

children.text: janyate jñānam ekaṃ tat tathaivātra bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: by the eye, the lamp, the object, and mental attention — so too it will be here.'
Reply: This one, whose body has become muddied by wallowing in muck,
runs toward a mirage's waters in the desert, desiring to bathe!

children.text: bhinnasvarūpād yady ekam asti vastv iti saṃbhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: If it is possible that a single entity exists from things of different natures,
then differentiation through difference of cause is not ultimately real.

children.text: atha bhinnasvarūpaṃ tad ekaṃ cety upagamyate //
children.translated_text: But if that [entity] is accepted as being of different nature and yet one,

children.text: svabhāvabhedo bhedāyety etat tyaktaṃ vrataṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: then [the principle that] 'difference of nature leads to difference' — that vow would be abandoned.

children.text: nanv itthaṃ sā kriyā mā bhūd ekā kāṣṭhādi kārakam //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Very well, let there be no such [single] action; let the firewood and the rest, as agents,

children.text: phalaṃ janayatām evam apy astu na hi naḥ kṣatiḥ /
children.translated_text: simply produce the result — even so, there is no harm to our [position].'

children.text: kriyā hi nāma nāsmākam anyā śaktis tv asau yataḥ //
children.translated_text: Reply: For us, what is called 'action' is nothing other than a power; since
a power, through the configuration of the result, is identical with the entity itself — without differentiation.

children.text: sā ca śaktir vibhor eva sa ca viśvātmavigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that power belongs to the Lord alone, and he is of the form of the entire universe;
he is not [truly] differentiated through the distinction of result and agent.
Even though within his own undifferentiated self, the Lord thus manifests differentiation —

children.text: kriyāśaktir iti proktā yayā kartā maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: [this] is called <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action), by which the doer is <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).

children.text: nanu yat paśavaḥ kuryuḥ kathaṃ tad upapadyatām //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But what the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) do — how is that justified?

children.text: te hi bhedaikajīvatvāt kuryur bhedavatīṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: For they, whose very life consists of differentiation alone, would perform action that is [itself] differentiated.'

children.text: alam etena paśavaḥ kathaṃ kuryur iti sphuṭam //
children.translated_text: Reply: Enough of this! 'How can bound souls do [anything]?' is itself self-evident;
that very argument is self-refuting, like [the existence of] a barren woman's son.

children.text: na hi kumbhakṛtaḥ kvāpi kadācit kartṛtā bhavet //
children.translated_text: For the pot, made by [the potter, could] never anywhere at any time have agency
if it is not identical with the maker [called] <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).

children.text: nanu kiṃ svit kulālena kumbho 'pi kriyate tataḥ //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But then, is the pot also made by the potter?

children.text: īśasya viśvakartṛtve kiṃ paṭe 'pi na kartṛtā /
children.translated_text: If the Lord is the maker of everything, does he not also have agency over cloth?'

children.text: yady evaṃ tat kulālena paṭo 'pi kriyate na kim //
children.translated_text: Reply: If so, then is cloth also made by the potter? Is it not?

children.text: nanv evaṃ sati no kartā ko 'py anya iti karmaṇām /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Well then, there is no other doer of actions —

children.text: śubhāśubhānāṃ svaphalaṃ kartuṃ kaṃ prati hetutā //
children.translated_text: with regard to auspicious and inauspicious [actions], toward whom would there be causality for [the production of] their respective fruits?'

children.text: evam evaitad āyuṣmaṃs tathāhy evaṃ vijānatām /
children.translated_text: Reply: Exactly so, O long-lived one! For thus, for those who know in this way,

children.text: na kiṃ cana phalaṃ kvāpi śubhāśubhasamudbhavam //
children.translated_text: there is nowhere any fruit arising from auspicious or inauspicious [action].

children.text: itthaṃ ye tu na jānanti bhuñjate te 'vipaścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: But those who do not know thus — they, the unwise, do experience [such fruits];

children.text: tad eva karmasaṃjñaṃ tu malam ajñānamūlakam //
children.translated_text: that very [experience], called 'karma' (action), is the impurity (<s>mala</s>) rooted in ignorance.
It is precisely by accepting this [position] that some [thinkers],
[asserting] mere awareness (<s>saṃvittimātra</s>), consider [the Self] to be a non-agent, from the impossibility of agency.

children.text: citsvarūpādhikaṃ hy asya yat tat kartṛtvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: For what is called his agency, being [something] additional to his nature as consciousness,
would impose inertness upon him — due to the unwanted consequence of an excess of consciousness [being needed].
Objection [from Sāṃkhya]: 'The agency of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is figuratively attributed to the <s>Puruṣa</s> (soul).'
Reply: This is sung in vain at home by those who have departed from the path of logic.
For figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) does not attain the true nature of a thing;
it is merely a designation — let it be devoid of real substance to that extent.
Even with the figurative designation of fire, a human being
does not dispel the cold arising from hailstone spray, glacial winds, and snowfall.

children.text: draṣṭuḥ puṃsaś ca na draṣṭrī prakṛtiḥ parigīyate /
children.translated_text: And <s>Prakṛti</s> is not proclaimed to be the seer of the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the observer;
nor is there any other poor [entity] to serve as the figurative recipient of the attribution of agency.
Moreover, what purpose would arise for him from the conventional usage of agency?
