A [mere] designation is not capable of transforming a [real] thing.
As for those knowers of method who have accepted the Self as agent —

children.text: te 'pi praśnam imaṃ tāvad asmākaṃ pratibhārpitam //
children.translated_text: even they should first receive this question, presented with [our] reasoning:
'Is the agency — of the kind well-established in the world through connection with action,
whose nature is vibration (<s>spanda</s>) — possible in the Lord who is devoid of vibration?'

children.text: nanu jñānaṃ cikīrṣā ca yatnaś ceti guṇatrayam /
children.translated_text: Objection [from Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika]: 'The triad of qualities — knowledge, desire, and effort —

children.text: samavaiti yad atrāsya tat kartṛtvam udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: which inhere [in the Self] — that is declared to be his agency.'
Reply: In this way the intellect of those of childish understanding would be duped by deceivers!

children.text: dārakā api vā vidyur na saṃvedanavarjitāḥ //
children.translated_text: Even children, not devoid of awareness, would know [better].

children.text: tatra jñānaṃ na kartṛtvaṃ sarvatrāsty eva tad yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, knowledge is not agency, since it exists everywhere;

children.text: icchāyatnāv api prāyaḥ saṃstaḥ sarvasya sarvataḥ //
children.translated_text: and desire and effort too are generally always present in everyone in all situations.
A potter whose mind is distressed by the absence of a house,

children.text: jānann icchan sayatno 'pi kiṃ kuryān nātmano gṛham //
children.translated_text: though he knows, desires, and strives — why can he not make a house for himself?

children.text: nanu kartuṃ na jānāti tataḥ kartuṃ na cecchati /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'He does not know how to make [a house]; therefore he does not desire to make one;

children.text: tasmāt kartuṃ na yatate tad gṛhaṃ kurutāṃ kathaṃ //
children.translated_text: therefore he does not strive to make one — so how would he make that house?'

children.text: kartum ity eva yad rūpaṃ jñānādīnāṃ viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Reply: The qualifier 'to make' that modifies knowledge and the rest —

children.text: karotes tatra ko 'rthaḥ syād yadi saspandatā kila //
children.translated_text: what meaning would 'making' have there, if not vibration (<s>spandatā</s>)?

children.text: tadāsau spandituṃ vetti prepsatīti bhaved vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the statement would be: 'He knows how to vibrate, and wishes [to do so]' —

children.text: tac ca svātmagataṃ nāsya spanditaṃ vaibhavodbhavāt //
children.translated_text: and that [vibration] pertains to his own self, not to his vibrating [external things], since it arises from [his own] power.

children.text: anyad aspanditaṃ jñānaṃ śarvasyāpi na saṃbhavet /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even for <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), non-vibrating knowledge would not be possible.
And 'possessing knowledge, desire, and effort' is said to be his instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).
Of the Self, 'to make' — therefore, in the analysis of this meaning,
'he knows, he desires, he strives — to know, to strive, to desire' —

children.text: pratyekam iti yo 'rthaḥ sa kartuṃ vettīti śabditaḥ /
children.translated_text: the meaning of each individually [is reducible to] what is expressed as 'he knows how to make';

children.text: cikīrṣitṛtvaṃ caitat syān na kartṛtvaṃ punar bhavet //
children.translated_text: this would be 'one-who-desires-to-do-ness,' but never agency proper.
If this were [accepted as agency], then there would be an equality of mental acts
with acts of speech and body. Or how would agency be reached through acts of speech and body?

children.text: mānasāny api karmāṇi kathaṃ tasyeti gīyatām /
children.translated_text: How can even mental actions belong to that [Self]? Let it be stated.
When the three qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) belonging to that [Self] exist, regarding actions arising from mind, speech, and body —

children.text: karmaṇāṃ saṃciter eṣa karmabhāgīti cen nanu /
children.translated_text: if [one says] this [Self] is a sharer in <s>karma</s> due to the accumulation of actions,

children.text: upacāro 'yam evaṃ syāt sa cāvastv iti varṇitam //
children.translated_text: this would be merely a figurative usage, and that has been described as unreal.
Moreover, when qualities belonging to other substances such as the greatness of the Self and so forth are present,

children.text: tāni santīti kiṃ so 'pi kartṛtvāyatano bhavet //
children.translated_text: if those [actions] exist, would that [substance] too become a locus of agency?

children.text: na cāstv ity upagantavyaṃ muktāv api hi tad bhavet /
children.translated_text: Nor should it be accepted that [the Self] does not exist, for that would apply even in liberation;
since the same rule applies when the qualities of other selves are present.
Therefore, the destruction of what has been done and the accrual of what has not been done would apply to [all] selves.
Moreover, if the Lord, who everywhere requires intelligent beings [as instruments],
were made the efficient cause for effects that require a particular arrangement —
and when [the effect] is filled by its own respective parts of proximate and other causes in combination,

children.text: kam aṃśaṃ kumbhakārādeḥ prātuṃ bhavatu hetutā /
children.translated_text: what portion could be left for the potter and the like to occupy as causality?

children.text: na hi so 'sty aṃśaleśo 'pi sarvakartari yaṃ prati //
children.translated_text: For there is not even the slightest portion, regarding the maker of all, for which

children.text: na jñānecchāyatnam asti kartṛtvaṃ nānyad ity api /
children.translated_text: knowledge, will, and effort do not exist; and agency is nothing other [than these].

children.text: tasmān nānyasya kartṛtvaṃ kadācid api saṃbhavet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the agency of another could never be possible.
They know sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>) as the agency [even] of the Lord over lords.

children.text: tad itthaṃ parameśānāṃ bhede bhede 'pi vātmanām //
children.translated_text: Thus, for the supreme Lords, whether in difference or [even for] selves —
actions do not by their own nature give rise to bondage.

children.text: tasmād idam amuṣmāt syāt karmaṇo vā śubhāśubham //
children.translated_text: Therefore, "this [action] would arise from that, or the auspicious and inauspicious from <s>karma</s>" —
that sovereignty belongs to none other than the Supreme Lord.

children.text: nirṇītam etad anyatra mayaiva vitataṃ yataḥ //
children.translated_text: This has been determined by me elsewhere extensively, since

children.text: tad alaṃ prakṛtaṃ brūmaḥ kriyāśaktir iyaṃ parā /
children.translated_text: enough — let us speak of the matter at hand. This supreme power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>)
is proclaimed as the <s>Aghora</s> [aspect] of the Lord, from that very [source].
Hence the graciousness (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>) of this [power] toward entities, in their refuge in <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: yato 'ñjasaiva mārgo 'yaṃ yā kriyā ca na sātmikā //
children.translated_text: for this path is direct, and that action which is not self-natured —

children.text: nanu nātra sthitāḥ kecid bhāvā ye śivatāśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: now, there are no entities established here that are agents dependent on <s>Śiva</s>;
truly so, but one being instructed thus should understand:
the Lord of lords (<s>devadeva</s>) is free from the path of the fabrication of place, time, action, and agent,
and likewise his <s>Śakti</s>, who has the form of the universe.
That universe too, free from the stain of the limiting power (<s>kalā</s>) of time and the like,
abides in non-difference from <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: tatsvātantryāt svatantraṃ tat svātmani procchalat sthitam /
children.translated_text: Through that [Bhairava's] sovereignty, it is sovereign, abiding as arising in its own Self;
from wherever it shines, from there too, expelled from the possession of <s>Śiva</s>, [it appears as] set.
Therefore, this supreme [power] has the form of the gracious (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) [and] <s>aghora</s>;
as will be stated: "In the circle of beings, bestowing the fruit of the abode of <s>Śiva</s>,
the supreme <s>Aghora</s> powers of <s>Śiva</s> are proclaimed by the knowers of that."
Elsewhere too, the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>) of <s>Śiva</s>, when operating in bound souls (<s>paśu</s>),
is binding; [but] when abiding in its own path, known [properly], it bestows <s>siddhi</s> (attainment).
The expansion that is proclaimed from <s>a</s> to <s>ha</s> —
that very [expansion], having taken recourse to vowellessness from the abode of <s>bindu</s>,
is this bursting forth of the power of action — the entire garland of phonemes (<s>varṇamālikā</s>),
which, having gathered [all] into the self-awareness of "I" (<s>aham</s>),
abides [thus]. From that, the flash of the full, supreme I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇa-parāhaṃkāra</s>),
which consumes the multitude of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) from <s>Ananta</s> down to <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),
which has absorbed into the cave of its own womb the throng of the moving and unmoving world,
which has swallowed the collection of individuals within the self-awareness of its own consciousness —
insofar as it has flashed forth, [it has done so] through the nature of the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>),
whose state is constituted by innumerable varieties beyond ordinary knowledge,
whose nature is the differentiation of gentle and fierce [aspects] such as the pacification of infinite effects,
and whose firm abiding is made manifest by the majesty of its own absorption —
through propriety, [these powers,] though of various forms, belong to the splendor of <s>Bhairava</s>,
variegated by the repetition of empty, full, both, and becoming [states],
devoted solely to the absorption of their own portions called the universe, which are of the nature of <s>Śākta</s>,
directed toward the uprooting of entities long established in the world and time,
these powers, through their own expansion, spreading forth each its own cluster of rays,
from the resort of the reality of the truth of intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>),
excluding the left-hand conduct (<s>vāmācāra</s>) arising from the world, as is appropriate,
produce the scriptures that have attained completeness.
Whatever practice first arose, in the domain that transcends the world —
that very same [practice], here, in the state of absorbed difference, becomes [scripture].
This complete great creation (<s>mahāsṛṣṭi</s>) of the Supreme Lord is established here,
in which the aspects of dissolution and creation are situated in the middle, within the universe.

children.text: sā cādyā sṛṣṭir ity eva naiva vaktuṃ bhavet kṣamam //
children.translated_text: And it would not be proper to call that the "first" creation at all,
for in a reality devoid of place and time, how could firstness and the like arise?
This is the waking state — that primary [state] which partakes of the stage of opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>).
This is <s>Brahmā</s>, seated on the lotus of the awakening of the aspect of his own power.

children.text: tā etāḥ sauśivād rūpāt prabhṛti brāhmam antataḥ //
children.translated_text: Beginning from the <s>Sauśiva</s> (pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>) form, and ending with the <s>Brāhma</s> (pertaining to <s>Brahmā</s>) form,
these powers of the Lord of consciousness burst forth.

children.text: etāvān eva devo 'yam iti yady api śakyate //
children.translated_text: Although it is possible to say "The Lord is just this much,"
this cannot be said due to the immeasurability of the Great Lord whose form is consciousness.
Within the fifteen [stanzas on] awakening (<s>Prabodhapañcadaśikā</s>), I have clearly stated:
"Limited illumination is said to be the characteristic of the insentient;

children.text: jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate //
children.translated_text: awareness is distinct from the insentient, since it is not limited."
Nevertheless, the Lord himself, of such nature, free from measurement,
through the connection of his own sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>), making himself into the moving and the unmoving —
through <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Ajāta</s> faces, arisen and wishing to arise,

children.text: ekakaiḥ ṣaḍbhir, ekena trikeṇa, dvyātmakais tribhiḥ //
children.translated_text: singly in groups of six, in one triad, and in three pairs —
there arises the varied condition of the ten divisions of <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore, from the diverse modes of consciousness, due to the force of intermixture,
variegated knowledges of difference have been produced even in what is called <s>Śiva</s>.
When there is the conjunction of the left and right in the three faces,
then, through the states of future, present, and past, each [face] becomes a power;
when the six become three, there is the <s>Rudra</s> division — thus established in eighteen ways.

children.text: ekaikaṃ pañcavaktraṃ ca vaktraṃ yasmāt pragīyate /
children.translated_text: Since each face is proclaimed as five-faced,
therefore, through the divisions of the ten-and-eighteen-differentiated [system], there is innumerability.
Variegated by the knowledge and action appropriate to each, as previously stated —

children.text: nirṇīyante yatas teṣu tena no punaruktatā //
children.translated_text: since they are determined in those [contexts], there is no redundancy here.

children.text: anyānya eva bodho hi samācāraḥ kriyākramaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the awareness, the practice, and the sequence of action are indeed different in each case;

children.text: tatra tatra tathā proktaḥ sarvas tu śivadhāmagaḥ //
children.translated_text: each is proclaimed as such in its own place, but all lead to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
Just as all drops of water find rest in the great ocean,
so all knowledges and actions [find rest] in the ocean of consciousness, in <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: mitam api jalaṃ bhūmau sūryāṃśubhiḥ kila pīyate /
tad api ca punar vṛṣṭidvāraiḥ prayāti mahārṇavam /
children.translated_text: yet that too, through the doors of rain, proceeds again to the great ocean.
Even a limited amount of water on the earth is drunk up by the rays of the sun;

children.text: jagati nikhilaṃ jñānaṃ karma sphuṭaṃ kim api svayaṃ /
kim api ca paraiḥ pāramparyāc chivārṇasi majjati //
children.translated_text: and some through others in succession — merges into the ocean of <s>Śiva</s>.
In the world, all knowledge and action — some clearly by oneself,

children.text: yac cānte dakṣiṇe hārdaṃ liṅgaṃ hṛt paramaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: And what at the end, on the right [side], is the heart-<s>liṅga</s>, considered the supreme heart —
that too, having absorbed within itself all emitted entities, is exceedingly full.
And through the absorption of the portion of the light of <s>māyā</s> that produces the sense of difference,
it is dark, bearing the form of darkness, due to being the agent of universal dissolution.
Therefore, in the <s>Vijñānaśāstra</s> (Scripture of Consciousness), it has been stated by the Great Lord:

children.text: līnaṃ mūrdhni viyat sarvam ityādi timiraṃ vibhoḥ //
children.translated_text: "All space is absorbed at the crown" and so forth — the darkness of the all-pervading Lord.
Thus, in the deep night, when the dark fortnight has arrived, for a long time
one should meditate on the <s>Bhairava</s> form — difficult to penetrate for those who [merely] meditate.

children.text: uktaṃ ca yatra svar duḥkhaṃ tamo vādvayasaṃvṛte /
children.translated_text: And it is said: "Where heaven is suffering, where darkness envelops both [heaven and earth],
there is no connection with ignorance and <s>karma</s>, because of the vision of the state beyond dependence."

children.text: tad atra timirākāre bhairavīye vapuṣy alam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in this body of <s>Bhairava</s> having the form of darkness, enough —
the fourfold face shines by being absorbed within.
Wishing to arise, it is arisen; wishing to conceal, it is concealed.
Then, simultaneously, differentiated in this way, [becoming] sixteenfold,

children.text: dakṣe vaisargike hārde svatantre ca śive viśat /
children.translated_text: it enters into the right, the <s>visarga</s>-related, the heart, and the sovereign <s>Śiva</s>.
The scripture called <s>Bhairava</s>, consisting of eight times eight, [arises] simultaneously.
Thus the <s>tantra</s> stands threefold, called <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Bhairava</s>.
For in reality, this existence of knowledge bursts forth in just three ways:
through difference, through difference-and-non-difference, and through complete non-difference.

children.text: tathā ca mukhyāḥ śāmbhavyas tisra icchādiśaktayaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus the principal <s>Śāmbhava</s> powers are three: <s>icchā</s> (will) and the others.
But therein, through elaboration, there is the conjunction of the five powers and so forth.

children.text: itthaṃ madhye vibhinnaṃ tat trikam eva paraṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: Thus, differentiated in the middle, that supreme <s>trika</s> (triad) and likewise
the scripture are established in our <s>guru's</s> house through the tradition of lineage.
Therefore, precisely because of the proximity of the left and right scriptures,
at the edge of the stream, at the periphery of the support, the <s>Kaulika</s> [tradition] bursts forth.
And even beyond that, full with the absorption of all conditions of entities,
<s>Bhairava</s>, whose activity is nourished by the fluidity (<s>drava</s>) arising from the supreme truth,
in those [faces] of <s>Īśāna</s>, left, and right, the triad of powers in sequence,
having gathered in [all] from the <s>Aparā</s> (lower) up to the edge of the <s>Parā</s> (supreme), abides.
and that which produces the clarity of that, and also that infinite [power];
That [<s>Bhairava</s>] manifests the division of difference;
in reality, they have declared it to be <s>Triśiras</s> (Three-headed) alone.
and the form of the Supreme Lord that is devouring —
The upper, left, and other <s>tantras</s> and <s>kulas</s>
are established in this stream, for the removal of the contraction of difference.
The meaning of the <s>Trika</s>, established in three ways, is the subject of the supreme light;
this very [meaning] has been set forth by the Supreme Lord as "the Moon of Knowledge" (<s>Jñānacandra</s>).
That very total meaning of scripture, having resorted to the activity of the supreme speech (<s>parāvāk</s>),
is without the distinctions of expressed and expressor and the like that have not yet arisen.
But afterwards, in the power of action, which is very subtle, whose nature has flashed forth
through the predominance of the aspect of the power of knowledge, in the wealth of sovereignty called <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
in the lower level of <s>Paśyantī</s> and <s>Madhyamā</s> [speech], through the connection with the tracing of murmured utterance,
it operates in the form of words and sentences, having the form of phonemes.
Therefore, in the <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s> (Scripture of the Autonomous), it is stated: "The Lord <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself
has composed the <s>tantra</s> with sentences of prior and subsequent words."
And thus it is stated there too, in the <s>Suśivāvaraṇa</s> section:
"The <s>Suśivāvaraṇa</s> is first; therein <s>Sadāśiva</s> should be known,
conjoined with the ten <s>Śiva</s> [forms], accompanied by the eighteen <s>Rudra</s> [forms];
the jurisdiction is in the <s>Īśa</s> principle, while the desire for that is in the <s>Sauśiva</s>;
in the enclosure, from <s>bindu</s>, in the realm of enjoyment, from the glory of the all-pervading Lord;
the supreme triad of the knowledge called <s>Bhairava</s> is in the <s>Śakti</s> principle."
Therefore, the position is stated above <s>Īśvara</s> [and] below the stage of <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
as the <s>Suśivāvaraṇa</s> in the glorious <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s>.
After that, in those divisions of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, sufficiently
established in the <s>māyīya</s> (illusory) course — the <s>Śiva</s>-named [division] is taught by the <s>Śivas</s>,

children.text: bhedo rudraiś ca rudrākhya iti prāpto vicitratām /
children.translated_text: and the <s>Rudra</s>-named by the <s>Rudras</s> — thus [the teaching] has attained variety.
Then, from the successive radiant bursting forth of the essence of the arising power of action,
having resorted to the <s>Vaikharī</s> (gross speech) of the <s>māyīya</s> level, which encompasses all objects,
the meanings of scripture, consisting of phonemes, words, and sentences, [become] within the domain of the world.
Having resorted to those various <s>tantra</s>-descents, they operate.

children.text: tena prathamato yāvan māyīyāṃ vaikharīṃ darīm //
children.translated_text: Therefore, as long as this meaning of scripture, constructed from <s>māyīya</s> phonemes,
has not arrived at the <s>māyīya Vaikharī</s> cave,
it is internally characterized by the supreme speech (<s>parāvāk</s>), whose sole [nature is] the awakening of essence,
refined by the sacramental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) rooted in natural, unartificial absorption in the supreme,
the meaning of scripture, ending in the worldly, is in the thirty-seventh, in the supreme Lord.

children.text: tatrāsatāṃ hi bhāvānāṃ kvāpi nāsty eva satyatā /
children.translated_text: For indeed, the reality of entities that are non-existent — that never exists anywhere.
In a master whose nature is overwhelmed by insolence, whence comes discipline?
Therefore, the meaning of all scriptures abides as having the nature of the supreme reality.
Therefore, these <s>Vedas</s> and the like too, [though] <s>māyīya</s> portions of teachings,
shine forth from the power of the sun of <s>Bhairava</s> alone, not from anything else.

children.text: na hi saṃvidvimarśāt syād anyat kvāpy eva kāraṇam //
children.translated_text: For there is never any cause whatsoever other than the self-awareness of consciousness (<s>saṃvidvimarśa</s>).

children.text: saṃvinnāthasya saṃvit syāt saṃvid eva tathā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: The consciousness of the Lord of consciousness is [itself] consciousness; for consciousness is thus [ultimate];

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ceti tathātva upacāryate //
children.translated_text: cause and effect — these are figuratively spoken of as being such.
For in the transformation of an entity, [which] gradually [assumes] extended properties,
at the beginning and end, consciousness alone appears as the form.

children.text: saṃvic ca kālakalanāṃ saheta yadi tat sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: And if consciousness were to endure the fragmentation of time, then clearly
we would enjoy fragments of space cut by sharpened swords!
Therefore, all scriptures, because of non-departure from the form of consciousness —
Because of the self-luminosity of consciousness, [all things] are in reality self-luminous.

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ pṛthag jātu vācakād vyavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: And the denoted (<s>vācya</s>) never stands apart from the denoting [word] (<s>vācaka</s>);
for, through [consciousness's] autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), the very act of denoting, [being] that which will become the denoted —
sometimes the denoting aspect appears with the denoted swallowed into its own form;
sometimes it shines as expressing a universal [meaning];
sometimes it is specified by a particular qualifier, near or infinite,
and shines forth with an overflowing of the denoted aspect [having] a manifest form.
Therefore, sometimes the orientation toward the object, sometimes the orientation toward the [word's] own form,
sometimes the intention to express a meaning, and somewhere a state pervaded by aesthetic relish (<s>rasa</s>) —
these diverse [conditions] of words are observed, because of the non-departure from the nature of consciousness;
that [consciousness] glitters with the variegated sparkle of consciousness — what is surprising?
is here, due to its clarity, the illuminator of both itself and other.
Thus, the word (<s>śabda</s>), non-different from the <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness) that is <s>Śiva</s>,
anything else [is called <s>pramāṇa</s>] only through figurative usage. For indeed:
That alone is the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — mere reflective awareness whose essence is <s>cit</s> (consciousness);
This consciousness (<s>saṃvitti</s>) which is of the nature of self-luminosity — that is the ultimate [reality];
that is called <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), from which the entire universe is established.
And this [consciousness] does not transcend its own nature, which is <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective awareness);

children.text: vimarśo 'syāḥ paro bhogaḥ pūrṇaḥ paśyanty udāhṛtā //
children.translated_text: its <s>vimarśa</s> is the supreme experience (<s>bhoga</s>), complete — it is called <s>Paśyantī</s>.

children.text: parāparā saiva devī mānam ity avadhāryatām /
children.translated_text: <s>Parāparā</s> — that very <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) is the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>) — let this be understood,
wherein the knowable (<s>meya</s>), reaching the lower aspect (<s>aparāṃśa</s>), is established through identity [with consciousness].

children.text: na hi bhinnena mānena meyasya syād vyavastitiḥ /
children.translated_text: For the establishment of the knowable cannot occur through a means of knowledge that is separate [from it];

children.text: na hi haṃsasya śuklatve kākaḥ śvetatvam arhati //
children.translated_text: just as a crow does not deserve whiteness from the whiteness of a swan.

children.text: etad eva tathā cāha guruḥ śaṅkaranandanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this very [point] the teacher, the son of <s>Śaṅkara</s> [i.e., <s>Utpaladeva</s>], has stated thus:

children.text: na mānatvāt tato 'nyatvān na bādhād asthiteḥ sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Not by being a means of knowledge, [for] then it would be other [than the object]; not by sublation; not establishment from non-establishment.'
'By properties that are inseparable from <s>Prakāśa</s> (light/consciousness), which are of fixed nature with regard to existence —

children.text: dharmair bhāvo bahirbhāvān na bhāvaḥ siddhim ṛcchati //
children.translated_text: an entity does not attain establishment through externality from those properties — [therefore,] there is no external entity.'
Therefore, the very nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvittikā</s>) is the knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>), and the knowable (<s>prameya</s>);
it shines forth from its very nature, grasping self-luminosity.
And this [consciousness], beautiful with the reflective awareness of the <s>mantra</s>-form words and names residing within —
is, from itself alone, the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), independent, due to the absence of anything other.
Its various names, in many modes,
were fashioned by the [various] proponents, arisen from its very grace.
And thus, what is proclaimed as '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' (direct perception), established by the stamp of the circle of sense-faculties

children.text: pratyakṣam iti yad gītaṃ tat tāvat pravivicyate //
children.translated_text: beginning with the eye — that is now examined.
If the sense-faculties (<s>akṣas</s>) have their establishment apart from consciousness,
then there could be no unity of [the sense-faculty] with the object as means of knowledge — just as with an external pot and the like.

children.text: nanv ātmanaś cakṣurādi karaṇaṃ na ghaṭādikam /
children.translated_text: 'But the eye and the like are instruments of the self, not pots and the like!'

children.text: tasmāt tenaiva bhāvānāṃ mānaṃ na tu ghaṭādibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is through [the self] alone that there is knowledge of entities, not through pots and the like.
But for this [self], which is held to be all-pervading, its conjunction [with the senses being] non-specific,
and there being no distinction of materiality between the eye and the like and pots and the like —
whence could there be a fixed fulfillment of the self's need for instruments?
'A specific conjunction alone is the basis for instrumentality.'
The specificity [arises] through those particular actions described as <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit).
This very [response], whose nature is the semblance of reasoning devoid of [genuine] logical force,
deceives the naive while [itself] being bent on flight [from the real issue].
And that which, arising from the all-pervading self that is conjoined with all the senses,

children.text: yugapaj jñaptim ācchettuṃ mano nāma nigadyate /
children.translated_text: is called '<s>manas</s>' (mind) — in order to cut [i.e., organize] simultaneous cognition —
regarding that too, we say: first, it is the self alone that is conjoined with the mind;

children.text: tatrāpy ātmamanoyogaṃ kaḥ kuryād iti carcyatām /
children.translated_text: and regarding that too — who effects the conjunction of self and mind? — let this be deliberated.

children.text: vyāpakatvād asau syāc cet sarvair eva mano vrajet //
children.translated_text: If it be [said] that this [conjunction happens] because of [the self's] pervasiveness — then the mind would be conjoined with everyone;

children.text: ekasya jāte saṃyoge sarvaḥ sarvajñatām iyāt /
children.translated_text: and when the conjunction occurs for one [self], every [self] would attain omniscience.
If the inner [mind] as superintendent requires the eye and other senses —
then the superintendence of objects [occurs only] through the path of that portion of the senses.
Illuminated through contact with the subtle portion superintended by the senses,
let one single atom of the external object — a pot and the like — appear.
But if the mental superintendence has now arisen over the sense-domain,
then what arises is its very capacity over its own domain.
Then, the eye-rays, emerging from the most subtle aperture,

children.text: viśvavartini bhāvaughe na pramāṃ kurvate kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: why do they not produce valid cognition of the totality of entities abiding in the universe?
'The senses apprehend entities situated in a suitable location' — enough!
What indeed is this 'suitability' of location? — let it be examined.

children.text: yatrasthasya bhaved vittiḥ sa deśo yogya ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'That location where cognition would arise for the one situated [there] — that location is called suitable.'

children.text: kutrasthasya bhaved vittir iti kiṃ vā na darśyate /
children.translated_text: 'And in what location would cognition arise for the one situated [there]?' — is this not to be shown?
These self-proclaimed logicians, devoid of the presentation of [valid] reasoning —

children.text: pūrvam eva kathaṃ tūṣṇīṃ nātiṣṭhan kiṃ vikatthanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: why did they not remain silent from the very beginning? What use are their boasts?
And for this self, whose purposive intention is barren [of independent power],
how would this conjunction with the network of mind and senses not be incoherent?
If then the purposive intention of this [self] arises toward an object —
[we ask:] what purposive intention could there be toward the unknown? And if known, what is the use of conjunction with the senses?
If [the intention is directed] toward what has been previously known and is being remembered — [then] the purposive intender [must have already known it];
one thing is the purposive intender, and the effort arises toward another [object].
Objects dependent upon the senses of eye and the like, connected to the self conjoined with the mind —
having bypassed the senses of eye and the like which have become proximate [means],
how do they extend the status of knower to the self itself?
'But the knower-status is produced by knowledge; knowledge inheres in the self;
therefore, how could the suspicion of knower-status [arise] for anything else?'

children.text: etad eva vayaṃ brūmo jñānaṃ tatraiva vai kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is exactly what we say: whence indeed is knowledge there [in the self, as you conceive it]?
Blinded by bias toward his own position, he gave that very [circular] answer out of fear.
'Just as the mind is called the cause for the conjunction of sense and self,
so let another cause be stated for the conjunction of self and mind.'
And if so, there would be an infinite regress — and that would undermine the very foundation.
If, however, the conjunction of mind and self is accepted as eternal —
then the sleeping, the intoxicated, the unconscious, and the unfortunate would always be knowers!

children.text: na caitad bhavatāṃ jñānam abhīṣṭaṃ śākyaśiṣyavat //
children.translated_text: Nor is this your [desired] kind of knowledge — [you would be] like disciples of the <s>Śākyas</s> (Buddhists).
Therefore, how can '<s>pratyakṣatā</s>' (directness/perception) [be established] from the sphere of the sense-faculties?
Now, let the examination of each of these [faculties] be set forth.
Therein, the mind [is held to be] atomic, eternal, [capable of cognizing] all objects, fast, light, and non-material —

children.text: manas tac cāpi naiveha yuktisiddhatvam aśnute //
children.translated_text: but even that does not attain logical establishment here.

children.text: aṇu cec chīgrasaṃcāri mano yad viṣayān muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: If the mind is atomic and moves swiftly, and rapidly
touches objects — then at that very moment, the body would become a corpse.
Even if there is conjunction of the mind while it is in the body, then, through the [inherence of] knowledge precisely there,

children.text: ekāṇumātraṃ jīvaḥ syāc chiṣṭaṃ syād ghaṭakuḍyavat //
children.translated_text: the <s>jīva</s> (soul) would be of one atom's measure [only], and the rest [of the body] would be like a pot or a wall.

children.text: atha svāntena yogaś cej jātaḥ kvāpy ātmagocare /
children.translated_text: If, however, the conjunction with the mind has occurred somewhere in the domain of the self [which is all-pervading] —

children.text: tad vibhor ātmano jñānaṃ samavāyīti mātṛtā //
children.translated_text: then, [since] the self is all-pervading, knowledge is inherent [in it] — and so the status of knower

children.text: jāteti sarvadehasthaṃ jīvanaṃ kiṃ na siddhyati /
children.translated_text: has arisen [already] — why does animation throughout the entire body not obtain?

children.text: enayaiva na kiṃ yuktyā ghaṭāder jīvanaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: By this very reasoning, would not animation of pots and the like also occur?

children.text: vibhāv ātmani jātaṃ hi jñānaṃ tatraikadeśataḥ /
children.translated_text: For if knowledge has arisen in the all-pervading self, [it would be] there in one particular location only;

children.text: dehamātre punaḥ svānte bhavet sāvayavā sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: but again, in the mind — which is only body-sized — there would be a composite [extended] existence.
If the mind were all-pervading, there would be simultaneous cognition of everything;

children.text: nitye ca manasi jñānaṃ sarvadaiva bhavet tataḥ //
children.translated_text: and if the mind were eternal, knowledge would always exist — therefore [this is absurd].
Even the state of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) would arise [only] when conjoined with knowledge;
and in liberation there is no conjunction of self and mind — this is most wondrous!

children.text: kiṃ hi vyāpakatā mokṣe svātmano vinirudhyate /
children.translated_text: For is the pervasiveness of the self suppressed in liberation?

children.text: abhautikaṃ cet sarvārthaṃ kathaṃkāraṃ mano bhavet //
children.translated_text: And if [the mind is] non-material, [yet capable of cognizing] all objects — how would such a mind exist?
It is because of the skill in manifesting [specific] qualified objects

children.text: taijasatvam abhīṣṭaṃ hi tan mano bhautikaṃ na kim //
children.translated_text: that the fiery nature of the eye is desired — then is the mind not material?

children.text: sarvarthatve ca manasaḥ kim anyair akṣaḍambaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: And if the mind [cognizes] all objects, what need is there for the pageantry of other senses?

children.text: nanu bāhye 'sya viṣaye prāg asty akṣopayogitā //
children.translated_text: 'But for external objects, there is first the utility of the senses!'
'For what is seen by the senses, the mind's state follows afterwards.'

children.text: atrocyate yathaiva prāg indriyeṇa na gṛhyate //
children.translated_text: To this we reply: just as what is not previously grasped by the sense —

children.text: tac cet svalakṣaṇaṃ paścād anuyantr iti kā kathā /
children.translated_text: how can there be talk of that [mind] subsequently apprehending its unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)?

children.text: atha sāmānyamātraṃ tad gṛhītaṃ prāk tadindriyaiḥ //
children.translated_text: If what was grasped previously by the senses was mere universals —
and if the determination of the particular was then [achieved] by the mind residing in the particular —
since [the mind] does not [grasp the particular] — why would the mind's grasping of universals occur
without the grasping of the particular? Where [is the logic in that]?
And if [the mind] grasps universals, its [alleged] all-object-ness is undermined —
being barren of the grasping of particulars, by the removal of the word 'all.'

children.text: āśugāmitvam etasya yac coktaṃ tatra vastuni //
children.translated_text: And regarding the swiftness of this [mind] that was stated — concerning the actual thing:
when one's own hand is right in front, when a pot is somewhat far away,

children.text: atidūre ca mervādau kathaṃ tulyaiva gantṛtā //
children.translated_text: and when <s>Meru</s> and the like are very far away — how can the travel be equal?
For even of swift-moving things, previously [known to have] such a nature —
a difference is perceived between near and far.
And how would a non-material, subtle [mind] grasp a mountain and the like?
'The manifestation of a like thing is effected by a like thing.'

children.text: nanv astu prākṛtī buddhis tato 'haṃkṛt tato manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But let there be <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) whose nature is <s>prakṛti</s>, then <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), then <s>manas</s> (mind)' —

children.text: ittham apy aṇutā naiva manasaḥ saṃprasiddhyati //
children.translated_text: even in this way, the atomicity of the mind is not at all established.
The previously stated refutations stand by [its] pervasiveness — enough.

children.text: itthaṃ mano na yuktyaṃśair mānasāvarjanāya naḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, the mind, by [its] logical aspects, is not [sufficient] for our conviction of mental [perception]
of the sort desired by the others whose view is deluded by duality.
That power which belongs to <s>Prakāśa</s> (the Light), the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>),

children.text: yā śaktis tan manas tv astu svasvātantryopakalpitam /
children.translated_text: which partakes of thus-appearance — let that be [called] 'mind,' fashioned by its own freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>).

children.text: yatra śrotraṃ nabhas tatra sarvaśabdaśrutir bhavet //
children.translated_text: If the ear is space (<s>ākāśa</s>), then wherever there is space, there would be hearing of all sounds;

children.text: cakṣurādyaiś ca sarvatra nirvibandhaṃ yato nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: and with the eye and the like, everywhere — since space is unimpeded.
And the impediment through <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) lacks the support of logical presentation.

children.text: bādhiryādi kathaṃ ca syāt kathaṃ vā taccikitsanam /
children.translated_text: Moreover, how would deafness and the like occur? And how [would there be] its cure?
'Through the destruction of the substratum of the impediment; and the grace [of hearing comes] likewise.'

children.text: akṣaṃ svāvayaveṣv eva x x x samavāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sense-faculty inheres in its own components [of the body]; ... inherent [therein];

children.text: viśeṣeṇa nabho naiva kvāpy āśritam iti sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: but space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is specifically not located in any [particular body-part] — such is the position.
Conjunction, however, ... exists together with the entity;
through the grace and destruction of that [conjunction], let there be modification accordingly.

children.text: yad anugrahas tad anugrahaḥ sa tadāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is grace, that is grace, and that is its substratum —
this verbal construction of one's own appears to us to be entirely hollow.
The grace of the senses operates through the substratum — this is clear;

children.text: abhidhatsva ka eteṣām āśrayo 'stv iti codite //
children.translated_text: declare then: what is the substratum of these [senses]? — when asked [thus],

children.text: yad anugrahayogo 'sya sa evāśraya ity ayam /
children.translated_text: 'That whose conjunction with grace [is operative] — that very thing is the substratum' — this
reasoning, resting upon mutual dependence, does not transcend circularity.

children.text: vāyuprakṛti yac coktaṃ sparśanaṃ tad vivicyate /
children.translated_text: And the tactile sense, which is said to be of the nature of wind (<s>vāyu</s>) — that is [now] examined.

children.text: vāyor vegavatī tāvad aniruddhā sthitiḥ sthitā //
children.translated_text: Wind's unrestricted state [of movement] is established as having velocity;

children.text: dehadeśe tataḥ sparśaḥ na kuḍya iti kaḥ kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore, touch [occurs] in the body-region but not in a wall — what is the logic of this?

children.text: cakṣuś ca taijasaṃ tejaḥ prasṛtaṃ bāhyagocare //
children.translated_text: And the eye, which is fiery — fire, spreading to the external domain,

children.text: arthān rūpapradhānāṃś ca vettīty etan nirūpyate /
children.translated_text: cognizes objects predominantly of the nature of form — this is [now] examined.

children.text: adṛśyaṃ yadi tat tejaḥ preryate manasā katham //
children.translated_text: If that fire is invisible, how is it directed by the mind?

children.text: preraṇaṃ na hy avijñānaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For direction of something unknown is never tenable.

children.text: indriyeṇa na ca jñātaṃ kadācic cākṣuṣaṃ mahaḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor has the ocular light ever been cognized by a sense-faculty.
Nor is your mind independent with regard to what is not cognized by a sense-faculty.

children.text: apreritaṃ ca tat paśyet sarvataḥ sarvathā sadā //
children.translated_text: And if undirected, that [ocular light] would see everything, everywhere, always —

children.text: āsamañjasyam eva syāt pravṛttau vā nivartane /
children.translated_text: and there would be incoherence whether in activity or in cessation.

children.text: kiṃ ca golakasaṃsthānaṃ tāvac ca yadi tan mahaḥ //
children.translated_text: Moreover, if that light is restricted to the configuration of the eyeball,

children.text: tāvatas tadgatasyaiva grahaḥ syān nānyataḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: then grasping would occur only of what is within that [sphere], not from anywhere else.
And conversely, even when the eyeball is closed,

children.text: unmīlite vā sarvatra vastuni grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: or when it is open — grasping of everything would occur.
And when the eye is opened and the ray-circle has spread forth,
there is no folding up of it, like a cloth, when the eye is closed;

children.text: tato nimīlitākṣasya vastudṛṣṭir na kiṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: therefore, would there not be perception of objects for one whose eyes are closed?
Moreover, in bright sunshine, for one whose eyes are closed,
there is the appearance of variegated light — and for one whose pair of eyes is pressed as well.

children.text: yogināṃ bindudṛg dhvānte kathaṃ tad vā bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How would the perception of a luminous point (<s>bindu</s>) by <s>yogins</s> in darkness be [explained]?

children.text: bhaved unmīlite 'py akṣṇi na vastugrahaṇaṃ kvacit //
children.translated_text: Even when the eye is open, there may not be any grasping of objects whatsoever
[when] the mind's superintendence is [withdrawn] — and [the eye has] an extension greater than an atom.

children.text: dīpāpekṣā ca yāmuṣya sāpi kiṃ na vibādhyate //
children.translated_text: And the dependence on a lamp that this [eye] has — is that not also refuted?
The light of a lamp is beneficial to [the perception of things by] one's own inner self, eye, and objects.

children.text: na pratyekaṃ manovṛtteḥ saṃskāras tena ced bhavet //
children.translated_text: If there were an impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) from each individual mental activity through [the lamp],
then, when one merely imagines a lamp, there should be the apprehension of form at night.

children.text: ātmanaḥ saṃskriyā cet syāt tasya sarvagatatvataḥ //
children.translated_text: If the impression pertains to the Self — since the Self is all-pervading,

children.text: sarvadā rūpasaṃvit syāt saṃyogaḥ saṃskriyā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: there would always be the cognition of form. Since conjunction [is supposed to be] the impression,
what other impression can be spoken of for one who is formless and eternal?
If [the lamp] assists the eye, then when the flame is situated at the place of the eye,
a form located within the [field of] light would never appear.
Objection: 'But that group of rays from the eyes goes to the place of the object to be known.'

children.text: hanta tatraiva vijñānam ātmadeśe na kiṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: Well then, cognition [would arise] right there [at the object's location]; why would it not arise at the place of the Self?
Since the Self is right there by virtue of being all-pervading, and since the instrument [the eye] is right there —

children.text: tasmād bhogāśrayo deho jīvann iti vṛthoktayaḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore, the statements 'the body is the locus of experience' and 'it is alive' are pointless.
If it is established that the rays of the eyes have the capacity to travel,
then on an unobstructed forest path, clearly, beginning from one's own hand,
how could the perception of the sun, moon, and such things arise?
For, even with speed, the stated difference [in time between near and far perception] would be for one traveling far and not far.
When that [object] is concealed by [the absence of] lamp-light and eye-light, how is there cognition?

children.text: śuddha eva bhaved bhāve tābhyāṃ vyāmalatājuṣi //
children.translated_text: The cognition should be pure in a state that partakes of purity through those two.

children.text: andhatvaṃ tac cikitsā ca na yuktāśrayadūṣaṇā /
children.translated_text: Blindness and its treatment — [these] are not [meant] to refute [our] established position.

children.text: rasanā ca jalātmā cet taj jalaṃ srutimadyataḥ //
children.translated_text: And if the tongue is of the nature of water, [then since] that water flows down,

children.text: tataḥ sthairyaṃ kathaṃ tasya kā ca nānārasaprathā /
children.translated_text: how then [is there] its stability? And what [explains] the manifestation of various tastes?
If it [the tongue] has a single taste, then due to the position of the tongue having one taste,

children.text: na syād ekarasajñaptir yathā pittabhare sati /
children.translated_text: there could be no cognition of a single taste — just as when there is an excess of bile,

children.text: tiktā rasanavṛttir no mādhuryaṃ viditaṃ kṣamā //
children.translated_text: the activity of the tongue [reports] bitterness, and is not capable of knowing sweetness.

children.text: nanu pittagataṃ taiktyaṃ na tv evaṃ rasanāgatam /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'The bitterness belongs to the bile, not to the tongue in that way.'
Then the bile and the [sweet substance] — both traversing the path of the tongue equally —
there should be simultaneous cognition pertaining to both bitterness and sweetness.

children.text: nīrasā rasanā cet sā rasābhivyañjikā kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: If the tongue is tasteless, how then can it be a revealer of tastes?

children.text: svabhāvād iti ced asyāḥ ko 'yam āmbhasatāgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'by its nature' — then what is this insistence on its being aqueous?

children.text: ghrāṇaṃ ca pārthivaṃ tasya kāṭhinyaṃ kiṃ na dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: And if the organ of smell is earthy, why is its hardness not perceived?

children.text: nanu gandhaguṇodreki kiṃ sa gandho na bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Because the quality of smell is predominant [in it] — does that smell not manifest?'
There is no such valid cognition regarding the organ having a manifest smell.
The mind, which is odorless and not of the nature of earth, is capable of grasping smell —

children.text: asty eva bhavatāṃ tena nānumā tādṛśā kṣamā //
children.translated_text: this is accepted even by you. Therefore, such an inference is not valid.
Hence, the aggregate of sense-organs as material elements is not tenable.
But if [the sense-organs] belong to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (the ego-principle), then [there would be] pervasiveness and non-differentiation,
and contradiction with being dependent on the body; and there would be no standing as instruments.

children.text: vāgādi yac ca karmākṣapañcakaṃ tad vivicyatām //
children.translated_text: Now let the five organs of action — speech and the rest — be examined.
From the navel to the crown of the head, that which is born from the impact of breath —

children.text: viśeṣaḥ ko 'pi vāgātmā sa tādṛg iha kathyate //
children.translated_text: some particular [capacity] that is the essence of speech — that is spoken of here as being of such nature.

children.text: tasya kāryaṃ bhavec chabdaḥ kartā ko 'tra vicāryatām /
children.translated_text: Its effect would be sound. Let it be examined: who is the agent here?
The Self does not have agency, because even if [agency were granted], due to its all-pervasiveness,

children.text: mayā proccārite śabde tvaṃ vaktā kiṃ na jāyase /
children.translated_text: when I produce a sound, why do you not become the speaker?
This fault [applies] even to <s>Prakṛti</s> (Nature) as the agent — [she being] devoid of agency.

children.text: karaṇasya sthitir nāsti tulye vāgindriye sati /
children.translated_text: There is no standing [for it] as an instrument, since the organ of speech [being all-pervading] is equal [everywhere].
And how does the [distinction between] indistinct and clear states arise in sounds?
And how [is there] the difference among sounds in whispering, murmuring, memory, and the like?

children.text: prayatnāc cet prayatno 'pi yady utpattis tataḥ katham //
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'through effort' — if effort too [is produced], then how from that

children.text: viśeṣo jāyate hy anyo na hy anyaguṇasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: does a different particular arise? For the production of a quality [different from its cause] is impossible.
By the lesser and greater degree of effort, by which [differentiation] is effected —
and the organ of the hand, which grasps — whence comes grasping by the mouth and the like?

children.text: grahaṇaṃ ca kim ucyeta svīkāro yadi saṃmataḥ //
children.translated_text: And what would be called 'grasping' if 'taking possession' (<s>svīkāra</s>) is what is accepted?

children.text: asvasya svasya karaṇaṃ svīkāra iti bhaṇyate /
children.translated_text: Making what is not one's own into one's own — that is said to be 'taking possession.'

children.text: svaśabdaś cātmavācī cet tatrātmā prakṛtir yadi //
children.translated_text: And if the word 'sva' (own) denotes the Self — if <s>Prakṛti</s> is the Self there,

children.text: tan nāsty aprākṛtaṃ kiṃcid ity asvatatvaṃ kathaṃ kila /
children.translated_text: then nothing is non-natural — so how could there be a state of 'not being one's own'?

children.text: ahaṅkāro 'py athātmā syān nāhaṃkārī kṛtir ghaṭe //
children.translated_text: If <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) is the Self — there is no ego-relation [possible] with a pot.
'This is mine' — by this very objection [the position] is refuted.

children.text: ahaṃkārasya saṃbandhi sarvam eva hi tat svakam //
children.translated_text: For everything that is related to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is indeed 'one's own.'

children.text: ātmano vyāpakasyāsti na svaṃ nāsvaṃ ca kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: For the all-pervading Self, nothing is either 'own' or 'not own.'
Likewise, this same force of reasoning applies equally to the organ of the foot.

children.text: deśād deśāntaraprāptyā gamanaṃ ca yad ucyate /
children.translated_text: And what is called 'movement' — the reaching from one place to another —
is established merely by the absence of taking-possession, being of the nature of relinquishing.

children.text: svīkāro dūṣitaś caiṣa svīkārāṃśo 'pi yo gatau /
children.translated_text: And this 'taking-possession' has been refuted; even the aspect of taking-possession in movement —
for that, the organ of the hand would be the fitting instrument, not the one called 'foot.'

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ hi sāṃkāryam evaṃ kāryeṣu jāyate /
children.translated_text: For the co-effect of sense-organs in their respective effects arises in this way.
Therefore, by those who know the great method, in the ultimate doctrine,
a vast array of genuine statements has been proclaimed to negate movement.

children.text: gataṃ na gamyate tāvad agataṃ naiva gamyate //
children.translated_text: 'What has gone is not being gone to; what has not gone is certainly not being gone to;
that which is free from both gone and not-gone does not exist' — and so forth, in their own doctrine.
And the organ of excretion is not merely an orifice; through the sequence of abdominal air,

children.text: utsargaḥ kila sāṃkāryaṃ tena syād iyatī sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: excretion [occurs] as a co-effect. By this much alone is its standing [established].

children.text: upastham indriyaṃ yac ca tasya kāryaṃ nigadyate //
children.translated_text: And the organ called <s>upastha</s> (generative organ) — its effect is stated [to be procreation].
[The argument] 'it ceases' — such validity of inference is not proper.

children.text: tadbhedavādināṃ tāvad dve māne naiva saṃgate //
children.translated_text: For the proponents of its [i.e., consciousness's] differentiation, the two means of knowledge are indeed not compatible.
But from sound and the like, through inference, it is ascertained by the wise.
Therefore, this very self-awareness, established through its self-luminous nature,
shines with the expansions of knower, means of knowledge, object of knowledge, and so forth.
the moonlight that accompanies the splitting open of night-lily petals —
The upwelling of the ocean, consisting of the play of dense waves,

children.text: vikāso yaḥ seyaṃ jagati vividhā kalpanakalā //
children.translated_text: is this very diverse art of construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) in the world.
the unfolding of supreme consciousness, through the interplay of objects, means, and knowers,
Therefore, this is light itself, fully charged with variegated power;
it shines by itself in a variegated form, everywhere and in all things.
Therefore, this [consciousness], whose appearance is fully manifest, through the path of the world-form and the like,
by virtue of its own power-aspect called <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), receives the designation 'direct perception.'

children.text: tathā hi devadevāṃśas tat samunmīlanaṃ dṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus: the aspect of the god of gods — that opening of vision;
the vibration of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) — its one-pointedness; existence — the collection of its properties;

children.text: ityādi sarvaṃ yad bhāti tat pratyakṣam iti sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: and so forth — all that appears is clearly direct perception.
But herein, the [analytical] approach through [categories of] agent-aspect, object-aspect, instrument-nature, and so forth does not [apply].

children.text: nanv asāv asti pāścātye vaikalpikapathe tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But that [distinction] exists in the subsequent, conceptual path.' Therefore —

children.text: yato dehaghaṭābhāso sphuṭaḥ paścāt tu so 'sphuṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: when the appearance of body, pot, and such is clear at first but then becomes unclear,
that very [appearance], in its concealed form, [becomes one with] the pure aspect of self-awareness;
then from that [arises again] the appearance of body, pot, and such — even there this same path [operates].
Up to the appearance of myriads of existential modes of thousands of bodies —

children.text: tatrāpi ca purā paścān na tu tādṛkprathā yadi //
children.translated_text: even there, [there is] before and after; but if there is no such manifestation,
when [awareness] attains the path of reflective awareness (<s>āmarśa</s>), it is variegated as clear and unclear.
To that extent, this is one and the same, of the nature of clearly manifest essential being.
[This] arrives [as] the light of <s>Śiva</s>.
......... this is not truly variegated in reality;
the variety is discussed due to the entry of what is not of that nature into it.
But the entry of what is not of that nature into the light of <s>Śiva</s> is not tenable.

children.text: yadi vā kathitanyāyabalāt kvāpi na citratā //
children.translated_text: Or [alternatively], by the force of the stated reasoning, there is nowhere any real variety.
However, the appearance as variety gives rise to the state of variety.
Thus, this <s>Caitra</s> [individual] of ours, being like the variegated, is of such nature.
Enough of this <s>Maitra</s>-doctrine! He who sees me, the seer of reality,

children.text: paśyan paśyati yaḥ so 'yaṃ samādhau pariniṣṭhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: seeing, sees — he is this one, well-established in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption).

children.text: prāk tv eṣa janmakoṭīṣu tattattāpādy abhuṅkta vai /
children.translated_text: But previously, through myriads of births, he experienced various sufferings and the like.
Even one who has arrived on this path through meditation, conduct, and such practices will be liberated.
He too, another partaker of liberation — thus, of inconclusive arising —

children.text: prakāśa eka evāyaṃ yaś cirān na vibhidyate //
children.translated_text: this light is one alone, which is never split for eternity.

children.text: ata eva hi bhedo 'sti na kaścid yo maheśvaram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no difference whatsoever that could
bind the non-dual Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), beautiful with the bliss of light.
Place, time, form, knowledge, property, limiting adjunct, interiority, and so forth —

children.text: saṃmatā bhedakatvena bhānti cet sā vibhā tathā //
children.translated_text: accepted as differentiators — if they shine, that is the radiance as such;

children.text: na ced vibhaiva sā tādṛk tad advaitam idaṃ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: if they do not, that radiance is simply such — then this non-duality is clear.

children.text: bheda ity eṣa śabdas tu kevalaṃ pratibhojjhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: The word 'difference' is merely abandoned by intuitive awareness.
Or, let there be the construction of difference, sprouting from intuitive awareness;
by the method stated, it will be well-established right there [within non-duality].

children.text: ayaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭaś cāyaṃ tāv anyonyavibhedinau /
children.translated_text: 'This is a pot, and this is cloth — these two are mutually different,
and different from other knowing subjects, and also different from me' —
thus this light is one, being of the nature of reflective awareness (<s>āmarśa</s>).

children.text: nanv evaṃ pakṣapāto 'yam advaitaṃ bhavatāṃ katham //
children.translated_text: Objection: 'But if so, this is partisanship — how is yours non-duality?'

children.text: bhedo 'py astu sa āhatya kiṃ nāma na viṣahyate /
children.translated_text: Reply: Let difference exist too — taken altogether, what exactly is not tolerated?
This is [like] the promotion of song and music in assemblies of the deaf!
For non-duality is not asserted by us through the obstruction of the entry of duality.

children.text: tvatpakṣopagamo hy eṣa syād dvayaṃ taddhi susphuṭam //
children.translated_text: For that adoption of your position — that would itself be duality, clearly.

children.text: idaṃ dvaitam idaṃ neti tad idaṃ ca dvayādvayam /
children.translated_text: 'This is duality, this is not' — that [assertion] is itself both dual and non-dual.

children.text: iti yatra samaṃ bhāti tad advayam udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: That in which [both] shine equally — that is called non-duality.

children.text: nanv ittham astu bhedo 'pi na vayaṃ śabdakāmukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Well then, let difference exist too — we are not lovers of mere words.'

children.text: astv asau na hi no heyam ādeyaṃ vā yathātra vaḥ //
children.translated_text: Let it be — for nothing is to be rejected or accepted by us, as [it is] for you.
If you embrace the position that is all-beneficent,
then you would take refuge in the supreme non-dual vision — that great shelter.
This principle will be [discussed] in the eighteenth chapter.

children.text: yat tad ante paraprāpyaṃ tad astu paramārthataḥ //
children.translated_text: What is attainable as the supreme [goal] at the end — let that be the ultimate reality.

children.text: atra ye na hi viśrāntās te mitāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are not at rest here — they, having resorted to limited consciousness,
are in every way afflicted by the confusions arising from birth and death.

children.text: tasmāt sa eka evāsau prakāśaḥ parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that light alone is the Supreme Lord —
it shines as direct perception, by that very light.

children.text: tatra tā dṛṣṭayaḥ sarvā mahānadya ivārṇave /
children.translated_text: Therein, all those [philosophical] views, like great rivers in the ocean,
inevitably enter — [and] those that have not entered do not attain the state of having fulfilled their purpose.
For thus, the aggregate of the means [of knowledge] — born of form, light, mind, and sense —
together with the knower and the known, or also without them in various ways,

children.text: jñātaṃ ca gamayen mānaṃ na cāpi ujjhati mānatām /
children.translated_text: conveys what is known through the means of knowledge and yet does not abandon the nature of being a means of knowledge.
This investigation into the section on direct perception is now established.
Moreover, since a means of knowledge grasps what is not [previously] known — ever new —

children.text: bhairavecchāvaśād etad viśvaṃ bhāti tathā tathā //
children.translated_text: [this is] because this universe shines in such-and-such a way by the will of <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: vastu pradarśayan mānaṃ pravṛttiṃ vidadhat sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Displaying the object, clearly producing activity,
the means of knowledge brings one to that very object, through the conjunction of its appearing thus.

children.text: sad apy ekāntato nedaṃ nāsac cetyādisaṃvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This is not exclusively existent, nor non-existent' — such cognitions

children.text: bhānty eva paramārthena tad anekāntadṛk sphuṭā //
children.translated_text: shine in the ultimate sense. Therefore, the multi-perspectival view (<s>anekānta</s>) is clearly [valid].
all existences have the nature of one existence.
One existence has the nature of all existences;
is fitting — and is also stated in the revered <s>Sāra</s>-scripture.
This Jain (<s>arhat</s>) doctrine, in our true vision,

children.text: idaṃ mānaṃ meyaṃ tad idam iti saṃkhyāṃ kalayituṃ
svarūpaṃ vā śaktaḥ ka iva jagatīty etad api sat /
children.translated_text: or [to know] its own nature — who indeed is capable [of determining] what the world [truly is]? Even this much is [merely] existent.'
'This is the means of knowledge, that is the object to be known — thus to construct enumeration,

children.text: yatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvād apara iha kaḥ kiṃ prakurutām //
children.translated_text: for apart from silence, what other could do what here?
This is the view of the Lord of Speech, O blessed one, beautiful with the bliss of consciousness —

children.text: ahetor bhāne syād yadi na tanudikkālaniyamas
tato hetor īdṛṅ niyama iti kasyaiṣa mahimā /
children.translated_text: then, from a cause, there is such-and-such regulation — whose glory is this?
If there were manifestation without a cause, there would be no regulation of body, direction, time;

children.text: svabhāvo 'yaṃ hetor atha vivṛtakaṇṭhaṃ katham asau
na bhāvasyaivokto yamayati pare kena hi paraḥ //
children.translated_text: not openly declared to be [the nature] of the existent itself? For who else regulates the other?
If this is the nature of the cause — then how is that [nature]

children.text: nirukto viśvātmā jagati nikhile jṛmbhata iti /
children.translated_text: the etymological explanation: the universal Self unfolds in the entire world.
And by its nature, this Self is <s>Paramaśiva</s> (Supreme <s>Śiva</s>) — so says the <s>āgama</s> (scripture);

children.text: dharādeś cānanyo bhavatu tad iyaṃ bhūtacititā

children.translated_text: it is barren [of birth and death], free from the calamity of death and birth through directions and time.
And let it be non-different from earth and the rest — then this is the consciousness of [all] beings;

children.text: tad asyāyaṃ lokas tadanu paraloko 'py ayam it
grahaḥ kasmād dhetoḥ spṛśati na hi taṃ kālakalanā /
children.translated_text: from what cause does this apprehension [arise]? For the measurement of time does not touch him.
Therefore, [the notion] 'this is his world, then this is the other world too' —
splendid with all the defilements and bonds reduced to ashes of becoming.
Then, the glory of the supreme bliss of the joyful essence of happiness, surging forth through autonomy,
concerning the domain of all <s>tattvas</s> (realities).
The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view is now discussed here at greater length,
and they arise from a cause that is most subtle.
The earth and the rest are clearly perceived,
engaged in the grasping of that [sense-data], [is posited];
And again, an external instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of tenfold nature,
is the mirror of pleasure, pain, and bewilderment.
the threefold internal cause of this [instrument]
and being inert and differentiated,
requires another, higher root-cause;
that [root-cause] is called here the 'night' (<s>Prakṛti</s>), the object of experience (<s>bhogya</s>).
That which is of such a nature, being precisely the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
does not mutually attain experiencer-hood [with the experienced].
And the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>), whose nature is dependence,
is impossible, since their properties are contradictory.
A single entity having both the form of the experienced and the experiencer
by virtue of its consciousness-nature, [even] the mind
Therefore the experiencer is nothing but the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>);
enter the state of experiencer, which involves differentiation?
[which is a] pervader, omnipresent — how could the Lord
one that partakes of a contracted existence.
Therefore he should resort to a state fashioned by his own self-mastery (<s>vaśitva</s>),
is held to be his innate impurity (<s>mala</s>).
This [contraction], from the absence of any other cause such as [external] art and the like,
this very [being] is designated as the <s>puruṣa</s> (individual soul).
It appears in three forms; under its dominion
as its necessary concomitant, his covering (<s>kañcuka</s>)
Under the compulsion of the state of dependence [inherent] in being an experiencer,
<s>rāga</s> (attachment), and <s>niyati</s> (fixity) — these are named [as the coverings].
shines forth [in the forms] thus: <s>kāla</s> (time), limited agency (<s>kalā</s>),

children.text: svaṃ rūpaṃ vivṛṇoty alaṃ nijabalāt tacchuddhavitsaṃbhavaḥ /

children.translated_text: But if this Self, through the unobstructed covering of his own complete autonomy, fully reveals his own form by his own power — that is the arising of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>).

children.text: kartṛtvaṃ kila kāryavargam akhilaṃ bodhe nidhāya svake
paśyann īśvaratāṃ vrajed aham idaṃ sarvaṃ sadety uddhuraḥ //

children.translated_text: Agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) [arises when], having deposited the entire array of effects within his own awareness, seeing [them thus], he attains lordship, [thinking] 'I am all this, being' — exalted.

children.text: jñeye bhedatirodhitāṃ nijacitau yasmāt sa saṃpaśyati /

children.translated_text: Knowership (<s>jñātṛtva</s>) [arises when], seeing in the clearly shining knowable [object] the gaze that has flashed forth within the heart, he perceives the concealment of difference within his own consciousness;
therefore, the cognition of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) — in which 'I' and 'this' have impetuously attained unity-in-difference — would reveal the <s>Sadāśiva</s> state.
to that extent, being of surpassing activity,
So long as all the knowable, the entirety of effects, remains absorbed within awareness,
its [the knowable's] emergence appears as if it abandons its own form.
within the mass of the flames of awareness,

children.text: bhavet prākkakṣyāyām api sa samakāntis tad adhunā /

children.translated_text: This 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃbhāva</s>) — it has dissolved [in awareness], yet is not truly dissolved; even in the prior stage it was of equal splendor; but now,

children.text: tad eṣā śāktī bhūriṣir iti svasiddhātmani parā //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>Śākta</s> level, the supreme, established in the self-proven Self, rich in [infinite] forms.
in the predominance of the 'I'-aspect, the method [of manifestation] is unlimited in the outpouring of entities —
It desires [to manifest] when the 'this'-aspect dissolves — [yet] there, due to the connection of prior and subsequent forms, it dissolves [further];
this entire level is called <s>Śākta</s> (pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>), being painted with the assemblage of variegated consciousnesses.
assumes each and every level;
In each <s>tattva</s>, the God of gods, by his own will,
the glorious <s>Bhairava</s> is thus explained in scripture.
of one complete Self, whose nature is complete consciousness —
through its divisions as mild, moderate, and intensely supreme.
This [doctrine of] the 'vision of <s>śaktipāta</s>' (descent of grace) is now explained,
which is [nothing but] the Self's seeing of its own true nature.
And through the mutual sub-divisions of those [grades],

children.text: nanu kiṃ kadācid ayam īśvaro nijarūpaṃ prakāśayati pūrṇacitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Does this Lord — who is complete consciousness — sometimes reveal his own form,

children.text: kiṃ vā kadācid atha saṃvṛṇute nirhetuko hi niyamaḥ kila kaḥ //
children.translated_text: and sometimes conceal it? For what rule could be without a cause?'
there is no other cause for these determinations.
It has been said here before: the infinite [Lord] —
whose nature is the manifold and variegated manifestation [of all things].
Even in worldly [matters], it is that very <s>Maheśa</s> (Great Lord),
The mounting of the waves' mansions of the ocean of consciousness [constitutes revelation];
From his autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) — we shall not now elaborate any further answer.

children.text: śāntis tasyās tadanu tad ayaṃ bandhanāmnāpadiṣṭas

children.translated_text: by that very [autonomy], when the taste [of one's true nature] is thus regained — that is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), of the form [previously] stated.
the stilling of those [waves] — that is designated by the name 'bondage';

children.text: sadā kadācid adhunā tadetyādi ca saṃvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Always,' 'sometime,' 'now,' 'that,' and the like — these
are the conceptual play of time, manifested through the autonomy of consciousness.

children.text: na ca kālakalābhiḥ sa spṛśyate parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: And the supreme Lord is not touched by the divisions of time;

children.text: na hi tāsāṃ svatantrāsti sthitis tatkalpanāṃ vinā //
children.translated_text: for those [time-divisions] have no independent existence apart from being projected [by him].

children.text: tena svasṛṣṭe bhāvāṃśe svarūpātmany api sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this appearance of dependence — in the aspect of entities self-created,
and even in [what is] one's own essential nature — is manifested by the Lord himself.
The autonomous supreme Lord projects dependence;

children.text: svātantrye pāratantrye ca nānyal lakṣaṇam ucyate //
children.translated_text: no other defining characteristic is stated for autonomy and dependence [than this].

children.text: paricchinnaprakāśo hi jaḍas tenātra yaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that which is of limited illumination is inert; one who exists here [as such] —
if this very limiter were itself limited, then clearly

children.text: tad asya rūpagrahaṇe na prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
children.translated_text: illumination would not illuminate in the apprehension of its own form.

children.text: tathā hi bāhyo bhāvāṃśaḥ svayaṃ naiṣa prakāśate //
children.translated_text: For the external aspect of entities does not by itself shine forth;

children.text: jñānam arthaprakāśātma tac cānābhātam eva hi /
children.translated_text: knowledge is that whose nature is the illumination of objects — and that [knowledge itself] is indeed unmanifest;

children.text: tasyāpi samavāyy ātmā naiva bhāti svarūpataḥ //
children.translated_text: even its inherent Self (<s>samavāyin ātmā</s>) does not shine forth from its own nature;
its instrument — the eye and the rest — also does not shine forth;
and illumination from light and the like does not appear apart from cognition.

children.text: nanu jātaṃ yadi jñānam arthasyāsau prakāśatā /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'If cognition has arisen, that [cognition] is the illumination of the object —

children.text: śaktir dharmo yadi prāptaṃ sārvajñyaṃ viśvamaṇḍale //
children.translated_text: if [that illumination is] a power, a property — then omniscience is established throughout the entire universe.'
Reply: If that something called 'illumination' is something else [from the object],
then it is nowhere found among the measured, the measurer, and the means of measurement.

children.text: tataś cāprakaṭaṃ viśvaṃ sarvadaiva bhaved idam /
children.translated_text: And then this universe would always be unmanifest.

children.text: aprakāśasya bhāvasya yadi ca syād prakāśanam //
children.translated_text: But if a non-luminous entity were to become luminous,
to that extent its own nature would be diminished, because of the loss [of its prior nature].

children.text: jñānotpattiś ca bhāvasya svarūpasthasya cet prathā //
children.translated_text: And if the arising of knowledge is the manifestation of an entity abiding in its own nature,

children.text: aviśiṣṭe svarūpasthabhāve viśvasya sā na kim /
children.translated_text: then since the entity abiding in its own nature is undifferentiated, why would that [manifestation] not apply to the whole universe?
Therefore, the illumination of the universe is established in the limiter [i.e., consciousness],
differentiated into various forms arisen from the manifestation of its own autonomy.

children.text: paricchedaka itthaṃ cet paricchedyo bhavet tataḥ //
children.translated_text: If the limiter is thus [himself] limited, then
an infinite regress will ensue, destructive of the very foundation.
Therefore he, being unlimited, is called the limiter;

children.text: akālpyas tena śāstreṣu tan na kālasya gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: he is inconceivable — therefore [his nature] is not within the domain of time.
Therefore, the property of being a knowable (<s>vedya</s>) is predicated of time [rather than of him].

children.text: yadi kālaś ca mātāraṃ paricchindyāt tato dhruvam /
children.translated_text: If time were to limit the measurer [consciousness], then surely
the existence of time would seek its fulfillment as attached to the measurer.

children.text: na ca mātrantaraṃ kiṃcit saṃbhaved anavasthiteḥ /
children.translated_text: And no other measurer is possible, due to infinite regress;
and if one assumes [another measurer] to eliminate that [regress], that measurer would be free from the divisions of time.

children.text: ya eva tu paricchedyo mātā tallagna eva cet /
children.translated_text: But if the very one who is the measured is the measurer, and if time is attached to him,

children.text: sa kālo mātṛmeyatve tarhy ekasya kathaṃ tava //
children.translated_text: then how can one [entity] be both measurer and measured in your [system]?

children.text: bhedavāde hi bhavatāṃ niṣṭhitā matir īdṛśī /
children.translated_text: For in the doctrine of difference [held by] you all, such is the settled conclusion.

children.text: abhedavādināṃ nas tu naiva kāpy astu khaṇḍanā //
children.translated_text: But for us, proponents of non-difference, there is no refutation whatsoever.

children.text: viśvaṃ mātṛmayaṃ yeṣāṃ mātā viśvamayas tathā /
children.translated_text: Those for whom the universe is constituted by the measurer, and the measurer by the universe —
that supreme Lord is not [caught] in the mire of the net of time-divisions.
The illumination of the power of consciousness [merely] assumes the appearance of impurity (<s>mālinya</s>);
therefore, when it is concealed and thereafter becomes manifest again,
this is the very unfolding of that [consciousness], which designates [the appearance of] 'such-ness' (<s>tathātva</s>).
A certain fashioning of his, whose nature is the self-reflection of his own nature —
[occurs] in which the Self considers itself worthy of union with <s>Śiva</s>,
since, through the conjunction of variety, it considers itself thus.
Therefore, the ninefold arrangement of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) has been stated here;

children.text: anyathā neśvarasyāsti rāgo dveṣo 'tha vā kvacit //
children.translated_text: otherwise, the Lord has neither attachment nor aversion anywhere,

children.text: yena kvāpy eṣa niyatāṃ svāṃ śaktiṃ pātayed vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: by which he would let his power descend in a fixed manner upon anyone.
And thus, this <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) of the Great Lord is without external cause.
Therefore, [the assertion] that the power descends due to: the cessation of attachment, the equilibrium of <s>karma</s>, the preponderance of merit,

children.text: malapākāt suhṛdyogād bhakter bhāvāc ca sevanāt //
children.translated_text: the ripening of impurity (<s>mala</s>), the company of the good, devotion, disposition, and practice,
the breaking forth of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), the maturation of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
the destruction of false knowledge, the renunciation of action, the abandonment of desire,

children.text: sāmyāc cittasya sā śaktiḥ patatīti yad ucyate /
children.translated_text: the equanimity of mind — [the assertion] that the power descends [due to these causes]
is false.
Objection: 'But even there, from the search for yet another cause,
the possibility of infinite regress and its impossibility [must be considered];
and from the occurrence of [fallacies like] mutual dependence, vicious circle, and the like.'

children.text: asmiṃs tu pakṣe sarveṣāṃ pravādānām api sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Reply: In this [our] position, the standing of all [other] doctrines too

children.text: yuktā sarvaṃsahe pakṣe na kiṃcit kila duṣyati //
