children.translated_text: is justified; in the position that sustains all, nothing whatsoever is faulty.
by the wise themselves; therefore,
The reasoning therein can be applied
for the verbosity of [doing so] in the text would be futile.
a separate demonstration is not given here —

children.text: śivaśaktiṃ na ca tāṃ vinā bhavet /
children.translated_text: <s>śivaśakti</s> (power of <s>Śiva</s>); for without it
Therefore, they have arrived at the unconditioned
in rival scriptures are in vain.
the state of liberation [cannot exist]; hence the discussions of liberation
perform investigation [to determine worthiness]' —
'At the time of <s>śaktipāta</s>, O Lord, you never
in various places in his own treatise.
so formulated the glorious master <s>Utpala</s> (<s>Utpaladeva</s>)

children.text: tasyaiva hi prasādena bhaktir utpādyate nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: For it is by his grace alone that devotion is produced in human beings,
through which, with minds absorbed in his nature, they attain the supreme accomplishment.
Thus, in <s>Purāṇas</s>, scriptures, and the like, that <s>pārameśvarī</s> (supreme) power
is declared to be entirely independent; for if it were dependent, there would be non-lordship.
Only by those whose vision is sluggish, obscured by the blindness of the doctrine of difference,
[is] the impossibility of its fixed occurrence somewhere [asserted],
endlessly pondering — 'from the ripening of the equilibrium of <s>karma</s>, impurity, and the like' —
the self is wearied in vain in such webs of [supposed] causes.
Their grasping at [supports like] <s>kuśa</s>-grass and <s>kāśa</s>-grass is of no help to them.
Therefore, he alone, nourished by the sovereignty of his own autonomy of such a kind,
manifests as 'then,' 'thus,' 'in that way,' and the like — through [infinite] variety.
Thus, the entry of all [philosophical] views

children.text: anupraveśa ity anyair alaṃ vā yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: into this very supreme Lord [is established] — enough of other displays of reasoning!
Thus, the God of gods has here declared his own essential nature.
Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the means of knowledge there, the foremost of all means of knowledge.

children.text: ekam evedṛśaṃ mānam iti kecit prapedire //
children.translated_text: Some have maintained that this alone — of such a nature — is the [only valid] means of knowledge.

children.text: dhūmād agnir iti prāyas tasyaivaitad vijṛṃbhitam /
children.translated_text: 'Fire from smoke' — this is generally just a manifestation of that very [direct perception].
Just as, regarding a pot, the cognizer, established through the seeing of the prior portion,
licking [i.e., reaching toward] meaning in the form of clear and unclear aspects,

children.text: sphuṭām eva matiṃ matvā pratyakṣatvaṃ prapadyate //
children.translated_text: knowing [the cognition] to be clear, attains the status of direct perception,

children.text: na cānumānam antyāṃśe saṃvid ekaiva sā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: so too in the final portion [of inference], it is not inference, since it is one and the same cognition.
The manifestation of fire, which resides within the perceptual awareness of smoke,
is likewise — a single cognition arises, reaching toward the object;

children.text: tāvaty āṃśe sphuṭākārā pratyakṣam iti bhāṣyatām //
children.translated_text: insofar as it is of clear form regarding that portion — let it be called direct perception.
Just as the variety of gems and the like [is perceived] — so too, from the presence of latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
in [the interaction of] the eye, the self, the mind, illumination, the object, and the like within cognition —
in cognition, [what is] direct perception shines forth clearly;
likewise, from the presence of the contact with the ground of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of such a kind,
at the end, that very cognition, having the form of smoke-and-fire, [arises].

children.text: yathā ca dṛḍhasaṃskārāḥ sollekhāḥ sapadi svayam //
children.translated_text: And just as those of firm latent impressions, with their traces [activated], spontaneously
perceive the true nature of gems and the like — with obstructions overcome —
so too, those who are hungry, with firm determination,
quickly grasp food and the like for consumption — due to the non-interruption of pervasion and the like.

children.text: tena pratyuktam eva syād yad āhuḥ parikalpanam //
children.translated_text: By this, the reply is already given to what they call 'conceptual construction' (<s>parikalpanam</s>):
'The cognition of pervasion, whose nature is invariable concomitance, practiced [through experience]' —

children.text: kiṃ hi tatkalpanāvyāptivitter iti na manmahe //
children.translated_text: 'what indeed is the conceptual construction of that pervasion-cognition?' — we do not think so.

children.text: āśūtpattivaśād asyā na khalv asty upalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Due to the swiftness of its arising, there is indeed no distinguishing mark [that separates it from perception];

children.text: anumīyata evaṃ sā tad eva parikalpanam //
children.translated_text: 'It is inferred' — that itself is [mere] conceptual construction.

children.text: aho svapakṣapātāndhāḥ svam apy upagataṃ muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas! Blinded by partiality for their own position, even what they themselves have accepted
these [logicians] who fancy themselves reasoners have begun to forget, again and again!
For in your view, all cognition is momentary,
illuminating its object merely through [the act of] arising.

children.text: na kṣaṇāc cāparaṃ kiṃcid āśubhāvitvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: And nothing other than 'momentary' is called 'swift-arising';

children.text: tat sarvam āśubhāvy eva vijñānam iti tattvataḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore, in truth, all cognition is indeed swift-arising.
Then 'absence of a distinguishing mark' would apply to all categories of entities everywhere;
but if [some cognition] pertains to a longer duration, for those of unbroken vision —

children.text: jñātaṃ tenāpi tarhy artho janmamātreṇa bhāsyate /
children.translated_text: then by that [criterion] too, the object shines forth merely through [the cognition's] birth;
and that which is clear regarding the object merely by virtue of arising —
how would its quicker or more stable mode of being bring about a [real] difference?

children.text: yat tat kila grahāpekṣaṃ svaprakāśam athāpi sat //
children.translated_text: That [cognition] which indeed requires apprehension, yet is self-luminous —
elsewhere it assumes the role of a means, like lightning, a lamp, and the like;
and even there, the condition of being slow or quick in duration appears as differentiation.

children.text: na ca kvāpy anumāneṣu vyāptyāder grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: And nowhere in inferences can there be an apprehension of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) and the like;
it becomes progressively clearer, by which it is observed.
Moreover, in the sequential cognition-series of smoke and the like, being clearly
arisen, how could it produce the appearance of a single entity?
If the final connecting cognition (<s>anusandhāna</s>) will do so,

children.text: tad api prāksthasaṃvittisamaṃ bhinnaṃ kathaṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: that too, being different from the prior cognition just as [those prior ones are from each other], how could it?
If by that [final cognition] the prior chain of cognitions is traced —

children.text: tad asan na hi saṃdhānaṃ naṣṭāyām upapadyate //
children.translated_text: that [chain] being non-existent, a connection cannot be established when [the object] has perished.

children.text: atha smaraṇam eveha saṃdhānaṃ saṃvidāṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If memory itself were the connection of cognitions here,

children.text: tad apy anubhavābhāve kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: that too, in the absence of [prior] experience — how could it possibly arise?

children.text: na ca jñāneṣv anubhavo yujyate saṃvidaḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: And the experience of a cognition within consciousness is not possible anywhere;
for it is your view that a pair of cognitions does not exist simultaneously.
The nature of knower-and-known is observed in things that exist simultaneously,
but not in mutually contradictory things that arise in the form of prior and subsequent.
Therefore, even the cognition that has the prior appearance of following pervasion —
even there, this perception-knowledge is non-sequential.
Just as one suddenly awakened from deep sleep, with vision just opening,
[thinks] "it is perception" — in order to remove the dimness of the aspect of entities,
while performing eye-rubbing and the like, does not think
"I am inferring entities" — so too let it be understood here.
And just as one whose vision has not recovered from the dense delusion of deep sleep

children.text: svātmānam atha tatsthānaṃ vismaraty eva tat kṣaṇaṃ //
children.translated_text: forgets at that very moment both himself and his place —
then, with pure vision awakened through the gathering of effort,
thinking "I am that very one" — in the ultimate sense, of consciousness —
therein, everywhere, this Lord, <s>Bhairava</s>, whose nature is consciousness,

children.text: svātantryāt svaṃ vapur yāvad gūhate vivṛṇoti ca //
children.translated_text: through sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>), insofar as he conceals and reveals his own form —
to that extent, ignorance and knowledge of this [Self] arise.

children.text: tac ca sphuṭatayā sarvapratyakṣam iti manyatām //
children.translated_text: And let that, through clarity, be considered as completely direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).
And when the word "pot" is heard, the cognition of broad-bottomed, round-bellied, and so forth —
therein too indeed, the remembering of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) and the like is of such a nature,
just as in the examination of gems, one's own clear cognition
abides, being illuminated by assemblages of other cognitions.
Then, through the connection with the final, clear cognition that has been awakened,
the true nature of the gem shines forth — not through the use of other cognitions [as independent means].
Those [other cognitions] have assumed causality merely for the awakening of that [final cognition];
for when that very [cognition] is in conjunction with appearance, those [others] have no utility.
From the example of the knowledge of children and conjurers, of such a kind, by itself,
even in verbal cognition indeed, there is a single clear cognition of illumination.

children.text: atas tathāvidhe śabde śrute yat samanantaram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in a word of such kind, when heard, immediately afterwards,
in the appearance of the meaning — this is the extent of such cognition:
the meaning abides therein to that extent, like the prior and subsequent parts of a pot.

children.text: nanv asau ghaṭa ekaḥ syād avayavyātmakas tathā //
children.translated_text: Now, that pot would be one, having the nature of a whole (<s>avayavin</s>), likewise;

children.text: na tu śabdārthayor aikyaṃ tat kathaṃ sāmyam īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: but there is no unity of word and meaning — how then can such a comparison [hold]?
Ah! One whose eyes are clouded by the darkness of habitual apprehension of difference —
even when the collyrium of correct reasoning is applied, has not attained clear vision.
The blessed Lord, this <s>Bhairava</s>, who is non-different, [assumes] the state of enjoyed and enjoyer
within his own Self, always connected — [he is] of complete form.

children.text: iti prasādhite pūrvaṃ kaḥ praśnasyāsya saṃbhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: Since this has been established before, what possibility is there for this question?

children.text: tad evam upamānādāv api mānāntare sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Thus, even in analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) and other means of knowledge, clearly,
it is the form of the direct perception of consciousness alone that appears everywhere.
Even a blind person, perceiving the respective forms through touch, sound, and the like,

children.text: sphuṭatām eva tāṃ tāvat saṃvetti sa tathāvidhām //
children.translated_text: cognizes that very clarity to just that extent, of such a nature.
Likewise, those who are blind from birth, through form, touch, and the like, conceive

children.text: sphuṭam eva hi bhāvāṃśaṃ teṣāṃ nājñātadhīḥ kvacit //
children.translated_text: clearly indeed a portion of the entity; their cognition is never of the unknown.
"This [woman] is a pool of beauty, a cluster of creepers in the garden of youth" —
thus is a person blind from birth delighted, through the touching of her limbs.

children.text: aho nu sadalaṃkāraṃ gāyatīti jaḍo janaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ah, how beautifully adorned she sings!" — thus an insensitive person,
merely by seeing the face of the singer, is satisfied to that extent.
Thus, perception alone, without a rival, bursts forth.

children.text: tad asya phalacintādi kartuṃ prastūyate manāk //
children.translated_text: Now, the consideration of its fruit and so forth is slightly introduced.
That very knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) is of the nature of the essence of self-awareness (<s>parimarśa</s>);

children.text: tasmād bhedakathā naiva phalaṃ prati susaṃgatā //
children.translated_text: therefore, talk of difference is not at all well-connected regarding the fruit.

children.text: hānādidhīḥ phalaṃ vāstu tasyā apy atha bhāsanāt /
children.translated_text: Let the cognition of avoidance and the like be the fruit; but even of that, because of its appearing,
or rather, because consciousness is in the ultimate sense self-luminous —
that alone is the fruit at the conclusion — firmly established everywhere.

children.text: hlādādikaṃ phalaṃ mukhyaṃ yat sarvatreha gīyate //
children.translated_text: The principal fruit that is proclaimed everywhere here is delight (<s>hlāda</s>) and the like;
that comes to rest in its own self-experience, in the [Self] that is full.

children.text: tad evam idam adhyakṣaṃ sarvataḥ pravijṛmbhate //
children.translated_text: Thus, this direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) bursts forth on all sides.
For one established in the practice of this — what <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) does not arise?
Through the inclination produced by the Vedic [teachings] spoken by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, from <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) and so forth,
from afar, auditory knowledge soon begins to operate.
Even in a mentally perceived aspect of an entity, the arising of clear functioning is indeed sufficient;
when seized by the force of self-awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), what wonder if it arises?
And thus it is stated in the <s>Spandaśāstra</s> (Scripture of Vibration): "Even when the mind is attentive,
it shines forth even more clearly" — enough with extensive elaborations.

children.text: itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ viśvaṃ yat parameśituḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, this entire universe is indeed direct perception of the Supreme Lord;

children.text: tat tato 'py avibhinnasya mātṛvargasya tat tathā /
children.translated_text: and therefore, for the group of knowers who are non-different from that, it is likewise so.
And there is no mixing up of cognitions, because of the mode of appearing as such.
Even in the sameness of perception, there is no equality of the cognitions of pot and non-pot.
Thus, this perception alone, without a rival, bursts forth.

children.text: tato na bhidyate cārthaḥ pratyakṣādvaitam īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the object is not differentiated [from consciousness]; such is this non-duality of perception.
This [doctrine of] non-duality of perception is stated
by <s>Ācārya Narasiṃha</s>, with an intellect perfected in the skill of synthesis (<s>sandhānakalikā</s>).
The validity of inference as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) in all things is stated by some.
For the Lord is omniscient, of non-conceptual nature;
and though he is of the nature of direct perception, he does not come into ordinary usage.
How could conceptual (<s>vikalpa</s>) usage [exist] in the non-conceptual?
And all this usage is carried out through <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptualization).

children.text: sa eva cānumānaṃ syāt tasyaitāḥ parikalpanāḥ /
children.translated_text: That itself would be inference, and these are its fabrications:
the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), the property of the subject (<s>dharma</s>), the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), and the cognition of that — all of them.

children.text: vastutas tv eka evāsau pratyayaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
children.translated_text: But in reality, that cognition is one alone, and is ultimate.

children.text: nanv adhyakṣaviyoge syād anumānaṃ kathaṃ yataḥ //
children.translated_text: Now, in the absence of direct perception, how could there be inference, since
it is grounded in the invariable connection ascertained by that very direct perception?

children.text: satyaṃ kiṃtu ya eko 'sau devaḥ sarvajñatāspadam //
children.translated_text: True, but that one Lord who is the locus of omniscience —
through the force of his possession (<s>āveśa</s>), this <s>vyāpti</s> is fashioned in awareness.
Otherwise, the knowledge of fire-and-smoke and their absence and the like,
whose nature is positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), would not [be established] even in hundreds of ages.

children.text: ata eva hi mukhyasya mānasya sadṛśatvataḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, precisely because of the similarity to the primary <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge),
inference is said to be the prompting of conventional activity.
Thus, these <s>pramāṇas</s> everywhere subsist on the consciousness of the Lord;
they arrive at the state of being means of knowledge [only thus], and not otherwise.
For this multitude of beings is ignorant — how, without settling in that [Lord's consciousness],

children.text: jñasvarūpatvam āpnoti tad vinā mātṛtā kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: could it attain the nature of a knower? Without that, how could there be the status of a means of knowledge?

children.text: tasmād saṃvidi yogo 'sya sa ca nānena durlabhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, his connection with consciousness — and that is not difficult for him.

children.text: vastuto hi na kaś cit sa savinnātho hy asau tathā /
children.translated_text: For in reality, no one is [separate from] that; for he is indeed the Lord of consciousness.
Thus, the thesis whose functioning is subsumed under the direct perception of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) —

children.text: sāpekṣaṃ paratantre ca pāśavaṃ mānam ucyate /
children.translated_text: the dependent <s>pramāṇa</s> of those in bondage (<s>paśu</s>) is said to be conditioned.
"This creature is ignorant, not sovereign over its own pleasure and pain;

children.text: īśvaraprerito yātīty ata eva munir jagau /
children.translated_text: impelled by the Lord, it goes" — thus indeed the sage (<s>muni</s>) has sung.
Thus, the sole validity of inference, dependent on the Lord,
has been determined by the <s>guru</s> named <s>Lolaṭa</s>, and is accepted by the world.
Another, having adopted his [view], says: "True, the consciousness of direct perception

children.text: vyavahāre 'sti mānatvam anumā tu kathaṃ pramā /
children.translated_text: has validity in conventional activity; but how is inference a valid means of knowledge?
In inference, which is easily subject to deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>), once established,
who indeed, being in the position of an examiner, would rest in confidence?
And positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), which is the presence in similar and dissimilar instances —
when first observed, at that time alone, they do not produce certainty.
And those who would remove [uncertainty] through the fault of the property of the thesis and the like —
they would purify a heap of dung with heaps of dust particles!
Therefore, this [inference] is merely doubt, established as a component of activity;
that very [doubt], because of appearing as difference, is designated as <s>māyā</s> (illusion).

children.text: māyeva ca paśūnāṃ syān mānaṃ māyācidātakam //
children.translated_text: And <s>māyā</s> itself would be the <s>pramāṇa</s> of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) — a means of knowledge woven of <s>māyā</s> and consciousness.
Or [it is] reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), whose nature is the supposition of the condition of one alternative;
because of the preponderance of benefit and harm, [it is] capable of prompting activity or cessation.

children.text: prabhaviṣṇuḥ sa eveti kim anyair mānaḍambaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: That alone is capable [of prompting action] — what need of other pompous means of knowledge?

children.text: pramātā śiva evaiko yasyedaṃ svāṅgam īdrśam //
children.translated_text: The knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) is <s>Śiva</s> alone, whose body of this kind
appears as the measurable everywhere, consisting of certainty.
Every other bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), dwelling in the midst of the darkness of doubt,
is tinged with consciousness that is like the flash of lightning —
finding certainty as one or another among the two alternatives and the reality of the other —

children.text: vindāna eva labhate nātra rūḍhiṃ kathaṃ cana /
children.translated_text: never attains firm establishment here.

children.text: tad evaṃ tarkataḥ sarvo vyavahāra iti sthitam //
children.translated_text: Thus, all conventional activity is from reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) — this is established.

children.text: aśuddha saiva vidyeyam iti mānaṃ vidhīyatām /
children.translated_text: Let that impure knowledge itself be constituted as a means of knowledge.

children.text: aśuddhir iyatī tasyā yad vastv ananusāritā //
children.translated_text: Its impurity is this much: that reality is not followed [by it].

children.text: anye tv anarthino nāsti pravṛttir iti niścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But others, firmly convinced that there is no activity without purpose,

children.text: arthitvam eva sacivam ity evaṃ paryacūcudan //
children.translated_text: [say:] "purposefulness itself is the minister [of activity]" — thus they have argued.
Some who know [only] the non-self thus declare attachment (<s>rāga</s>) to be the means of knowledge.

children.text: anye tv āhuḥ saṃśayo 'pi na nāmāniścite gaje //
children.translated_text: Others say: "Even doubt, when an elephant is uncertain,

children.text: śaktatve sati jāyeta rāgo vāpi pravṛttaye /
children.translated_text: if there is capacity, would give rise to attachment also, for activity."

children.text: tataḥ svāṃ kartṛtām īṣad ālocya janatāḥ sadā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, people, slightly considering their own agency, always

children.text: pravartanta itītthaṃ syāt kalāyā eva jṛmbhitam /
children.translated_text: engage in activity — this would thus be the bursting forth of <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) alone.

children.text: tenārthaḥ sa tathā vāstu mā vābhūt svātmanas tayā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, whether that meaning be so or not, through that [kalā],
considering [his own] agency, this [being] engages in activity everywhere.

children.text: anye tv āhur anādir yo vyavahāraḥ kriyātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: Others say: "The beginningless conventional activity whose nature is action —
that <s>niyati</s> (destiny) itself is established as the propeller of the universe.
And that itself is called <s>āgama</s> (tradition) — the sequence of the conduct of the elders.
From that, this entire determination of <s>dharma</s> and the like [arises]."
Neither from perception nor from inference — mostly deceptive —
does the intellect of those possessing the disposition of examination arrive at confidence.

children.text: annaṃ kṣudhaṃ śamayate tṛṣaṃ vārīti bālakāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Food appeases hunger; water [appeases] thirst" — children,
having ascertained this from another source, are without any doubt as to the truth of that.
Even regarding other matters such as sacrifice and the like, because of instruction from that same [tradition],
examiners obtain proper certainty from what is called <s>āgama</s> (tradition).

children.text: tathā ca munir āhedaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpam iti dvaye //
children.translated_text: And thus the sage (<s>muni</s>) has said: "Regarding the pair — this is merit (<s>puṇya</s>), this is sin (<s>pāpa</s>) —
the purpose of scripture is limited; [but] there is no [such limitation to] the purpose of <s>āgama</s> (tradition)."
For <s>āgama</s> is not merely this collection of books and texts;
it is simply the beginningless, well-known [tradition] called the <s>Vedas</s> and so forth.

children.text: kiṃ tu prasiddhir evāsau sā ca śabdasvarūpiṇī //
children.translated_text: Rather, it is that very well-known usage (<s>prasiddhi</s>), and that is of the nature of speech,

children.text: yā sarvadarśaneṣv eva na jātv āyāty apohyatām /
children.translated_text: which in all philosophical systems (<s>darśanas</s>) never comes to be refuted.

children.text: chāgaiś caityo jaṭā bhasma bhikṣā daṇḍaḥ kamaṇḍaluḥ //
children.translated_text: Goats for the <s>caitya</s> (shrine), matted hair, ashes, begging, staff, water-pot,
net, heated stone, plucking of beard, hair, and body-hair,
fire, fuel, laying of bricks, household life —
apart from the sequence of well-known usage of all these words and the like,
what other means is there for the understanding of the meaning actually established and [the meaning] other than that?

children.text: ittham āgama evāyaṃ pramāṇam iti dhīdhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>āgama</s> alone is a valid means of knowledge — so say the wise;

children.text: uktaṃ satyaiva vāg aiśī prasiddhir avigānataḥ //
children.translated_text: it is said: "The divine speech itself is well-known usage, without deviation."
Whether the well-known <s>āgama</s> in the world is accompanied by reasoning or otherwise,

children.text: vidyāyām apy avidyāyāṃ pramāṇam iti tat sthitam //
children.translated_text: both in knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and in ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), it is established as a valid means of knowledge.
The validity of <s>niyati</s> (destiny), for those dwelling in the glorious [world of] beings —

children.text: anye tv āhur viśeṣo 'yaṃ kālo nāmābhivartate //
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: this distinction called time (<s>kāla</s>) proceeds;
that which has the nature of manifest existence proceeds as the present,
while the aspect whose manifest nature has passed is then of the nature of non-manifestation --

children.text: bhūtaḥ kāraṇakḷptyā tu bhāvy asau parikalpyate /
children.translated_text: the past. By the construction of causality, that [time] is conceived as the future.

children.text: sa cāyaṃ na svatantro 'sti kaś cid anyonyasaṃśrayāt //
children.translated_text: And this [time] is not independent in any way, due to mutual dependence,
due to infinite regress, due to the observation of reversal of form,
due to the absence of fixity in determinate quantity, and due to dependence on both the subject (<s>mātṛ</s>) and object (<s>meya</s>),
due to separation from the unconditioned manifestation of that form,
due to the impossibility of its nature being one or many, permanent or impermanent,
due to the unity of one <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjunct) with one [entity], and due to the concealment of the <s>upādhi</s> as well,
due to the uselessness of time in [explaining] difference within action itself,
due to mutual dependence when produced by that, and due to infinite regress when produced by another,
due to the occurrence of conditioned difference being unreal, because of its non-substantiality,
due to the impossibility of the effect, and due to the uselessness of a single [time],
and because consciousness, having been granted manifestness, is eternally present.
From the dissolution of past and future, and therefore from the dissolution of the present too,

children.text: cinnātha eva devo 'sau kālam ābhāsayaty alam //
children.translated_text: the Lord who is the essence of consciousness alone manifests time fully.
Therefore, this worldly existence (<s>saṃsṛti</s>) of the one whose nature is consciousness is called the manifestation of time;
pregnant with its own self-manifestation, it is of the nature of existence and non-existence in entities, while in its own
form it is abidance; the efflorescence of subjectivity (<s>pramātṛtva</s>) is what is spoken of.

children.text: idaṃ na yad ahaṃ cāhaṃ yan nedam idam apy adaḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is not what I am, and I am what is not this; this too is that

children.text: yan nedam iti citreyam abhāva[ābhāsa]syaiva mānatā /
children.translated_text: which is not this" -- such is this variegated cognizing capacity of the [self-]manifestation of non-being.

children.text: parā pramātṛtā yāsau śuddhā tasyāṃ pṛthaksthiti //
children.translated_text: The supreme subjectivity (<s>pramātṛtā</s>), which is pure -- in that, the separate abidance

children.text: na mānam astīty atrāṃśe kiṃ tayā praviviktayā /
children.translated_text: "there is no cognition" -- in this aspect, what use is that isolated [state]?

children.text: yas tu sāṃsāriko mātṛbhāvaḥ sarvo 'yam īdṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: But the worldly subject-state (<s>mātṛbhāva</s>), all of it is of this nature:
therein, the cognizing capacity of that [consciousness] is by the grace of time (<s>kāla</s>).
For indeed, He is complete, bearing the nature of the self of everything in all ways;

children.text: kva mātā kva ca vā mānaṃ kva ca meyo 'vatiṣṭhatām /
children.translated_text: where is the subject, where the means of cognition, and where might the object abide?

children.text: mātrādīnāṃ hi satyatve na syād āpekṣikī sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: For if the subject and the rest were [independently] real, there would be no relational existence;

children.text: meyād eva ca mātrāder bhāvo jātu prakalpate /
children.translated_text: the existence of the subject and the rest is only ever constructed from the object alone,
either from the non-attainment of each other's form, or from the disconnection even when attained,
and from the absurd consequence everywhere [of omniscience], and from the connection with omniscience and the like,
and from the non-simultaneous manifestation of those that are unhelpful to reality,
in the subjectivity and the like generated by another object -- because from something other than that,
its existence abides precisely as un-arisen, in the same manner.

children.text: tasmād pūrṇaś cidātmāsau śivaḥ svāṃśaṃ vikhaṇḍayan /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the complete one, whose self is consciousness, <s>Śiva</s>, fragmenting His own portion,
the aspect of difference [characterized by] 'not I,' would also construct 'this.'
The completeness with respect to everything other than that, [He recognizes as] 'I am' in the self to that extent;

children.text: tato 'nyato 'pi saṃhartā jāyate nāham ity api //
children.translated_text: then from what is other than that too, the withdrawer arises, [characterized by] 'not I' as well.

children.text: ubhau tau idam aṃśau cāpy apohati parasparam /
children.translated_text: Those two 'this'-aspects mutually negate each other,

children.text: buddhistham idam aṃśaṃ svaṃ svāham aṃśe tirodadhat //
children.translated_text: concealing the 'this'-aspect established in intellect within its own 'I'-aspect,
it abides without dissolving it, like a pot covered by a cloth.

children.text: tad eva buddhisaṃsthāt tu samayāgrathitād atho //
children.translated_text: That very same [consciousness], however, from [the 'this'] established in intellect, from the knot of convention, and then
from the internal aggregation of 'this,' negating the 'I'-aspect,
from the 'I'-aspect's negation of the flood of 'this,' from the inner 'I,'
from the negation of one's own 'I,' the manifestation of negation of other 'I's --
the six deities (<s>ṣaḍdevatāḥ</s>), whose form is void, depending on which [consciousness] operates.

children.text: tad evedam iti jñānaṃ vikalpa iti gīyate /
children.translated_text: That knowledge which is 'this is that very thing' is called <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction);

children.text: sa kālaḥ kalyate yena viśvaṃ nijakalodayāt //
children.translated_text: that is time (<s>kāla</s>), by which the universe is impelled from the arising of its own <s>kalā</s> (creative power).

children.text: tad atrāṃśe ya eṣo 'sti bhāsāṃśaḥ svaprakāśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now in this aspect, that which is the aspect of manifestation (<s>bhāsa</s>), self-luminous,
in the form of being, it is of the nature of enlivening everything;

children.text: na mātāsau na vā mānaṃ na ca meyaṃ nirucyate /
children.translated_text: it is neither the subject (<s>mātā</s>), nor the means of cognition (<s>māna</s>), nor is it called the object (<s>meya</s>).

children.text: yas tv asau śūnyatāyogād abhāvo rudradaivataḥ //
children.translated_text: But that which, through connection with voidness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), is non-being, having <s>Rudra</s> as its deity,

children.text: sa eva mānatām eti yadyogān mātṛtābhāvi[va]taḥ /
children.translated_text: that very [consciousness] attains the status of means of cognition (<s>mānatā</s>), from whose connection [arises] subjectivity (<s>mātṛtā</s>);

children.text: mānāc ca pṛthaṅmeyam ity evam upapāditam //
children.translated_text: and from the means of cognition, a separate object -- thus it has been established.

children.text: itthaṃ kālasya mānatvaṃ pratipede 'tra kaiś cana /
children.translated_text: In this way, the status of time as means of cognition has been accepted here by some,
who are devotees at the feet of the guru known as the illustrious <s>Bhavatī</s>.
Thus, in the conscious being (<s>puṃs</s>) who is fragrant with the glory of the properties of consciousness,
that which has been taught as the sixfold [group] called <s>kañcuka</s> (covering), which bestows subjectivity --

children.text: tad ekaikasya mānatvaṃ ke cana pratipedire /
children.translated_text: some have accepted the cognizing capacity of each one [of the six] individually;
others think that one [kañcuka is primary] while all the rest serve as its auxiliaries.

children.text: anye kadāpi kasyāpi kathaṃcit kva canetyādi /
children.translated_text: Others [say] sometimes of one, somehow, somewhere, and so on;
others [say] of two [kañcukas together]; others by the arrangement of two triads.
Others [say it is] through mutual assistance; yet others [say it is] through mutual awakening.
But others consider <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), whose nature is the equilibrium of <s>guṇas</s>,
to be the primary means of cognition, from the observation of sleep, intoxication, fainting, and the like.

children.text: sa yatraiva pramātāyaṃ yataḥ supta iva sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: That [<s>Prakṛti</s>] wherein this cognizing subject abides as if asleep --
that itself is his subjectivity, because of the non-apprehension of means and object.
Because of the unchangeability of each other even in such a state of sleep,
merely this <s>Prakṛti</s> considers 'I know.'

children.text: tatra mukhyaṃ tu yan mānaṃ yatpuṃsaivānudarśanam //
children.translated_text: The principal means of cognition therein is that which is the direct perception of the conscious being (<s>puṃs</s>) itself,
and that is pure, without modification, devoid of the nature of being and non-being.
Thus some maintain, relying on the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [interpretation of] the coverings (<s>kañcuka</s>);
they are knowledge-seekers in the house of the guru named <s>Vayyābhidhāna</s>.
Others declare the ground of intellect (<s>dhībhūmi</s>) alone, which is colored by seer and seen,
to be the means of valid knowledge; some [say it is] the collection of [mental] functions (<s>vṛtti</s>);
others know the aggregate of properties (<s>dharma</s>), enumerated as eight beginning with <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: anye 'haṃkāram evāhuḥ kecid dhiyam atho manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Others declare it to be <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) alone; some [say] intellect, others mind;

children.text: kecid tritayam evedaṃ samaṃ sarvatra manvate //
children.translated_text: some consider this triad to be equally [operative] everywhere.
Others have accepted each one of the ten sense-faculties (<s>indriya</s>);
some [say] all of these [operate] everywhere in an undifferentiated manner.

children.text: andhasyāpi hi tat kiṃcidrūpāyatanam asti yat /
children.translated_text: For even a blind person has some basis for the visual domain (<s>rūpāyatana</s>),
[just as] a modification [of function occurs in] one who has only one ear or sense of touch, through the stable presence of other faculties.
'The dawn has broken, adorned with the expanse of sky free from clouds' --

children.text: ity ākarṇya parāṃ tūṣṭiṃ yāty andho haimane dine //
children.translated_text: hearing this, a blind person experiences supreme satisfaction on a winter day.
Even though he infers the pleasure born of protection from cold,
nevertheless, his self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) does not fail to manifest form.
Others have accepted the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) as the means of cognition,
from the rule that the ray of the eye is without [physical] contact, and so on.
The invisibility of the eye and the rest is thus well established;
but invisibility to a <s>yogin</s> is never established.

children.text: anye tu sthūlabhūtānāṃ jyotiṣāṃ mānatāṃ jaguḥ /
children.translated_text: Others have declared the gross elements and luminaries to be the means of cognition;
yet others have accepted even the object of cognition (<s>meya</s>) as having the status of means of valid knowledge.

children.text: yato bhavati mātṛtvaṃ tatpramāṇam iti sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: That from which subjectivity arises -- that is the means of valid knowledge, such is the position;

children.text: tadghaṭādyaiś ca yat tasmāt te 'pi mānam iti smṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: and through pots and the like, from that -- therefore they too are regarded as means of cognition.
Worldly usage, however, does not follow reality;
for it is mostly figurative, being constructed from mere desire.

children.text: kathaṃ jānāsi bhoḥ so 'haṃ jānāmīti ca coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'How do you know, sir?' When challenged, 'I know,'
he says, 'I know by means of this pot that has been seen.'

children.text: tasmān meye 'pi mānatvaṃ na hi nāma na laukikam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the status of means of cognition even in the object is indeed not non-worldly [i.e., is accepted in common parlance];
when the doctrine of non-difference is fundamental, even contradiction is not a fault.

children.text: ye tu pramāṇam āhus tatsāmagrīṃ tair api sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Those who call the aggregate [of conditions] the means of valid knowledge -- by them too, clearly,

children.text: arthāder mānatābhīṣṭā sā saṅghe 'py anyathā kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: the status of means of cognition is desired for the object and the rest; how could it be otherwise even in the aggregate?
Others, however, [accept] the cognizing capacity of every differentiation of determinate quantity,

children.text: kramoditāṃ hi sarvatra kvacic cāpy akramoditām //
children.translated_text: arising in sequence everywhere, and in some cases arising without sequence,
in some cases beautiful with the fullness of devouring both sequence and non-sequence --
they maintain [this]; their view is indicated here merely in outline.
First, through connection with the object, which flashes forth instantaneously,
concealed everywhere by the intention of seeing another purpose,
subjectivity [arises] last -- therein, the expansion of the visual [faculty];
then brilliant within with the expansion of mind, ego-intellect group;
then the splendor of the efflorescence of awareness purified by the <s>puṃs</s> (conscious being);
then, in sequence, the nights of time (<s>kāla</s>), <s>kalā</s>, <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>niyati</s> (necessity), and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: anyathā vā samaṃ vāpi dvandvayogena vā triśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or otherwise, simultaneously, or in pairs, or in threes,
or in every way, with groups of four or five, even at the level of <s>Āṇava</s> (the atomic);
non-existence, agency, attachment, proof, reasoning, and doubt --
these indeed arise there too, variegated by their respective sequences.
Behind that, there is that non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>) [cognition], which manifests pure sovereignty;
<s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) attains the status of means of cognition at the final stage of cognition.
Then, in the resort of the glorious knowledge-power and will-power of <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
that subject attains fullness, resting blissfully in the path (<s>adhva</s>) up to <s>Śakti</s>.
Thus, since complete subjectivity (<s>pramātṛtva</s>) manifests,
born from the separation from the concealment of any one portion of that --
the modes of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), through differences in manifestness and otherness, have gone to innumerability.

children.text: ata eva hy ajānānaiḥ śivaśāstroditāṃ sthitim //
children.translated_text: Therefore indeed, by those who do not know the position taught in the <s>Śiva</s> scriptures,
in manifest and non-manifest awarenesses, in the domain of memory and non-memory and the like,
in deep sleep and the like, in rapidity -- because of the impossibility of reasoning, reflection, and the like --
attention of the mind, <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), the construction of unseen [forces] such as <s>dharma</s> --

children.text: ity ete hi sphuṭaṃ śabdā nātra ko 'rthas tatri ... mā //
children.translated_text: these words are indeed clear; what meaning is there in that... [text corrupt].
And when the means of cognition of each successively higher group of principles has been ascertained,
the aspect of the lower principles takes on the status of object (<s>meya</s>).

children.text: na cātrāsti kramaḥ kaś cid vyavadhāne hi saṃbhavāt /
children.translated_text: And there is no [fixed] sequence here, for there is possibility even with gaps;

children.text: na hi vidyā na bauddhī tām ālocayati saṃvidam //
children.translated_text: for it is not that <s>Vidyā</s> does not illumine that awareness which is of the intellectual [level].
For <s>Vidyā</s> is declared to be the discriminator, resting upon the back of intellect;
the external sense-faculty, whose body is light, is of the nature of apprehension;
they call the mind the organ of conception (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), and <s>ahaṅkṛti</s> (ego-sense) the claimant,

children.text: niścetrīṃ ca dhiyaṃ tatra vidyāṃ cāpi vivecikām //
children.translated_text: and intellect (<s>dhī</s>) the determiner; and therein, <s>Vidyā</s> too is the discriminator;
therein also, <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is the coloring agent, <s>kalā</s> is the revealer of capacity,

children.text: kālaṃ vyavacchit kartāraṃ niyatiṃ ca niyāmikāṃ //
children.translated_text: <s>kāla</s> (time) is the divider, and <s>niyati</s> (necessity) is the regulator,
the reflector, the manifester of commonality with other subjects,
the reflector upon the forms and non-forms of the sphere of the graspable and its grasper,
<s>Māyā</s> is the cause of the disturbance of the fall from the enjoyment of completeness,
<s>Sadvidyā</s> (true knowledge) is the bestower of rest in completeness, of the nature of the auspicious <s>Śiva</s>,
the reflector upon the essential nature of the aspect filled with knowledge,
<s>Icchāśakti</s> (power of will) is the manifester of the fullness of the subject-aspect --
depending on [all] these, this complete subject-state expands.
First illumination and apprehension, then conception and claiming,
after that determination and observation, then the pair of discrimination and non-attachment,
agency, stability, delimitation, manifestation of commonality,
reflection on diversity, non-disturbance, apprehension of the complete object,
awareness of complete subjectivity, and the state of <s>Bhairavī</s> itself --
thus, in sixteen ways, as long as [consciousness] illuminates what is filled with objectivity,
that moon of consciousness (<s>vijñānacandra</s>) is said to abide with twice-eight <s>kalās</s> (phases).
<s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassed) is the first position; then <s>Ānanda</s> (Bliss), <s>Icchā</s> (Will), <s>Īśana</s> (Sovereignty);
<s>Udaya</s> (Arising), <s>Ūnatā</s> (Insufficiency), and <s>Āveśa</s> (Possession) -- thus the sixfold [group] is established.
From <s>Anuttara</s> beginning, up to <s>Jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge), it is thus;
but <s>Icchā</s> (Will) itself, established through <s>Īśana</s> (Sovereignty), [becomes] <s>Kriyāśakti</s> (power of action),
grasping a trace of the aspect of the abidance of light, it has attained the state of sixteen.
The <s>Icchā</s> and the rest -- from the conjunction of the prior <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>Ānanda</s> --
through the contact with those initial ones, [form] the four conjunct phonemes (<s>saṃdhyakṣara</s>).
Then, from the attainment of self-awareness, the state beginning with <s>bindu</s> [arises];
then, in the form of the aspect filled with the entire arrangement,

children.text: visargaḥ kila śākto 'sau vikṣepa iti yaḥ smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Visarga</s> (emission) indeed -- that is said to be the <s>Śākta</s> projection;
the separation of <s>visarga</s> itself is the seventeenth <s>kalā</s>;
sometimes that very [kalā] is the eighteenth, through the connection with renewed agitation.
Of <s>Anuttara</s>, of the <s>a</s>-phoneme, which has the form of the Supreme <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: akulasya parā yeyaṃ kaulikī śāktir uttamā //
children.translated_text: of <s>Akula</s> -- this supreme <s>Kaulikī Śakti</s> (power of the <s>Kula</s>) is the highest.

children.text: sa evāyaṃ visargas tu tasmāj jātam idaṃ jagat ṝü /
children.translated_text: This very <s>visarga</s> is that from which this universe has arisen.
Its capacity for agitation, the arising of the <s>kalā</s> of agitation,
from the state of fullness of agitation -- the diminishment of the sequence of that <s>Akula</s>;
thus, arisen from the oscillation of self-reflection whose nature is the essence of the sixfold --
because of having the nature of <s>Anuttara</s>, it is the expansion of the first one alone.

children.text: sa eva bhagavān antar nityaṃ prasphuradātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: That very Lord, eternally scintillating within,
He whose middle power is full, replete with the flood of all entities residing within,
beautiful with the joy of the universe arising from the agitation of his own will —
he ever shines forth, beautiful with the savor of complete creative emission.

children.text: śivaśaktyoḥ sa saṃghaṭṭaḥ sneha ity abhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: That union (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is called 'love' (<s>sneha</s>).
To gain entry into this very state of complete <s>visarga</s> (creative emission),
they practice the tradition of licking (<s>lehana</s>), churning (<s>manthana</s>), and so forth.

children.text: tathā hi madhyamāṃ nāḍīm adhiṣṭhāyākhilaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: For thus, having presided over the central channel (<s>madhyamā nāḍī</s>), [that] supreme radiance animates the entire body
from the midst of the agitated nectar (<s>amṛta</s>).
It would attain the state of creative emission; it reaches the rapture (<s>camatkṛti</s>) of bliss.

children.text: apūrṇā kevalaṃ sā tu pūrṇā tu bhagavanmayī //
children.translated_text: But that [emission] is merely incomplete; the complete one, however, is pervaded by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
Therefore, this one <s>visarga</s>-power (<s>vaisargikī śakti</s>) alone unfolds.
The <s>visarga</s> itself, agitated, [becomes] doubled in intensity through effort —

children.text: hakāro nāma viśveṣāṃ vyañjanānāṃ prasūtikṛt ṝü /
children.translated_text: the letter <s>ha</s> is the progenitor of all consonants.

children.text: sa eva ca punarbinduyogāt svām eva bhūmikām //
children.translated_text: And that very [<s>ha</s>], again, through union with the <s>bindu</s> (dot), resorts to its own
unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>) ground — that is regarded here as the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃbhāva</s>).
Here, from the vowel <s>a</s> arises the group called <s>ka</s>, and from <s>i</s> arises another;
then indeed, from the vowel <s>ṛ</s>, through the condition of the shadow of the <s>repha</s>-portion,
the <s>ṭa</s>-group [arises]; and then from that very [source], through the sequence of the shadow-condition from <s>dharā</s> (earth),

children.text: tavargas tatparaḥ paścād uvarṇādyaralāś ca vaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>ta</s>-group follows that; then, from the vowel <s>u</s> and so forth, [come] <s>ya</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>la</s>, and <s>va</s>;

children.text: ivarṇavargāc covarṇāt krameṇety ata eva hi //
children.translated_text: and from the <s>i</s>-vowel group and from <s>o</s>-vowel, in sequence — therefore indeed

children.text: antaḥsthā ity aśītāś ca ivarṇād dviprabhedaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: the semivowels (<s>antaḥstha</s>) and the sibilants, from the <s>i</s>-vowel, in its twofold division.
The origin of <s>śa</s>, <s>ṣa</s>, and <s>sa</s> is from the conjunction with the portion of pure conditioning.

children.text: icchāyā eva viśvo hi prasavo bahudhā sthitaḥ ṝü /
children.translated_text: For the entire emanation of the universe is the manifold production of will (<s>icchā</s>) alone.

children.text: ata eva hi sasthānabhāvo yuktatvam arhati //
children.translated_text: Therefore indeed, the state of being co-located [with the source] is fitting.
Since this coagulated state of the living being, having the nature of the womb (<s>yoni</s>),
that very [state] is here declared to be the power of the unsurpassed Lord (<s>anuttaradeva</s>).
Therein, the semivowel principles [are arranged] according to the sequence of stages of supreme speech (<s>parāvāk</s>);

children.text: avarge śivatattvaṃ tu kādau hānte śivāntakam //
children.translated_text: in the <s>a</s>-group is the <s>Śiva</s>-principle, and from the <s>ka</s>-group to the <s>ha</s>-ending, [extends the range] ending in <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus, this <s>saṃpuṭayoga</s> (union of encompassment) has been explained as the meaning of the thirtieth [verse].

children.text: evaṃ pūrṇānavacchinnā ciddevī syād yadi sphuṭam //
children.translated_text: If the Goddess of consciousness (<s>ciddevī</s>) were thus full and undivided, clearly,

children.text: sarvam asyāṃ bhaved eṣā sarvatra ca tathā bhavet ṝü /
children.translated_text: everything would exist in her, and she would exist in everything.

children.text: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati //
children.translated_text: 'He who sees me everywhere and sees everything in me —

children.text: tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa mametyapi tan muniḥ /
children.translated_text: I am not lost to him, nor is he lost to me' — thus the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]
spoke through the words of <s>Arjuna</s>'s teacher, here and there.

children.text: saṃvidātmā hi vicchinno yadi syāt sarvabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: For if consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), whose nature is the self, were severed from all entities,
it would be merely an entity [like any other], like a pot with its own particular characteristic.
And thus, from the loss of consciousness's nature as consciousness, it would perish.

children.text: palāyate hi cit sā ced vyavacicchedayiṣyate //
children.translated_text: For if that consciousness were to flee when one attempts to delimit it,
[it would be] like the shadow of one's own head in the sequence of stepping on one's own feet.

children.text: yac ca sarvaṃ mayi proktaṃ na paśyati mahājanaḥ //
children.translated_text: And as for 'everything in me' — the great ones do not perceive [this].
Because of being situated in the midst of everything, they are established in me to that extent.
Thus, because of not being established in [mere] luminosity, [for one] who partakes of equality with non-existence,
it is indeed destruction — so the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) declared, by both paths.

children.text: eṣa vastukramas tāvad yo 'yaṃ saṃpuṭa ucyate //
children.translated_text: This is the order of reality, insofar as what is called the <s>saṃpuṭa</s> (encompassment).
Then, from that very [encompassment], in the abode and seat pervaded by the entire course of the paths (<s>adhvan</s>),

children.text: saṃvid ādheyatāṃ prāptā punar ādhāratāṃ gatā //
children.translated_text: consciousness, having attained the status of the contained, again attains the status of the container.
And it has been stated in the unsurpassed sacrifice (<s>anuttara yāga</s>): 'Again, the seat;
then —'
But here, for those who wish to enter, the Sage (<s>Muni</s>),

children.text: ūcivān bhagavān eva viśvaṃ tan nānyatheti yat /
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, spoke according to the sequence of instruction — that the universe is just that and not otherwise.
The autonomy of undivided consciousness shines on the path of differentiation;
this arrangement of the instructed and the instructor is made manifest.

children.text: svātmaiva hi gurur devaḥ para ity abhimanyate //
children.translated_text: For one's own self is indeed the guru and the lord, [but] it is imagined as 'another'.
The sentences uttered by oneself are imagined as spoken by another.

children.text: pratipādyaṃ ca yad vastu yena ca pratipādyate //
children.translated_text: And the object to be conveyed and that by which it is conveyed —
all of that is indeed of the nature of the self, yet it is imagined as differentiated.
Just as a dull being, in the state of dream, [experiencing] the succession of instructions,
hearing them, imagines them to be spoken by another —
so too, this entire empirical activity is of the womb of waking.

children.text: ko bhedaḥ svapnajāgratsu tarhi syād iti cet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one asks], 'What difference then would there be between dream and waking?' —

children.text: bhaṇiṣyate 'tha vā nāthe svatantre kin na bhāṣitam //
children.translated_text: that will be stated [later]; or rather, for the autonomous Lord, what has not been spoken?
Thus, through the sequence of instruction itself, [there is] the distinction of injunction and restatement.

children.text: sarvaṃ devo 'tha vā devaḥ sarvam ity ekam eva hi //
children.translated_text: 'Everything is God' or 'God is everything' — this is indeed one and the same.
In reality, like 'jar' and 'pot' (<s>kumbha</s>/<s>ghaṭa</s>), the universe is merely a matter of synonyms.

children.text: vācya eṣāṃ tvam eveti tac chrīnārāyaṇo 'bhyadhāt //
children.translated_text: 'The referent of these [terms] is you alone' — thus <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s> declared.
But if there is non-difference, how can there be a construction of injunction and restatement?

children.text: yo danturaḥ sa caitro 'yam iti danturam āditaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'He who has protruding teeth is this <s>Caitra</s>' — [here] the protruding teeth first

children.text: anūdya caitra ityaṃśo yadi nāma vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: having been restated, the portion '<s>Caitra</s>' is, so to speak, newly enjoined.

children.text: tad danturo 'nyaś caitrāc caitraś cānyas tataḥ katham //
children.translated_text: But then the protruding-teethed one would be different from <s>Caitra</s>, and <s>Caitra</s> different from him — how?

children.text: ghaṭaś caitra itīdṛkṣā na syād vidhyanuvādatā /
children.translated_text: 'The pot is <s>Caitra</s>' — such a thing would not be an instance of injunction and restatement.

children.text: tasmād ya eva caitro 'sau sa dantura iti sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the established position is: he who is <s>Caitra</s>, he is the one with protruding teeth.
The real [distinction of] injunction arises merely from [the sequence of] cognition, [as does that] of injunction and restatement —
'This tree (<s>pādapa</s>) is a ground-grower (<s>bhūruha</s>)' — it is employed [thus];
with respect to those who stand in the position of a synonym not [yet] known.

children.text: maheśvaraḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat tv iti //
children.translated_text: '<s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) is all this universe' — likewise.
'A jar (<s>kumbha</s>) is a pot (<s>ghaṭa</s>)' — so too it is stated;

children.text: itthaṃ saṃpuṭayogena paripūrṇā hi yā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the <s>saṃpuṭayoga</s> (union of encompassment), the state that is perfectly full,
in which hundreds of aspects of dissolution and creation abide within —

children.text: tām eva bhāgaśaḥ ke cid upāsitumanas tayā /
children.translated_text: that very [fullness], some who are intent on worshipping it partially, by means of that [fullness],
through the [series] arising from doubling — one, then four, six, twelve, and so forth —
break it up through various sequences by the differentiated modes of the wheel of consciousness (<s>saṃviccakra</s>).

children.text: ekā saṃvid dvidhā saiva dṛkkriyātmā tridhātha sā //
children.translated_text: Consciousness is one; that same [consciousness] is twofold, as seeing and action; then threefold;
through the accompaniment of the power of opening (<s>pronmeṣa</s>), it is also declared as fourfold.
Through the consciousness-power as established in bliss, it is declared as fivefold.
Sixfold, through the investigation of the exploration of consciousness stated by the six vowels;
up to twelvefold — consciousness in creation and so forth, in the same domain —
singly, through its threefold nature, or in the triad, through its fourfold nature.

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ kalayate saṃvit tatrābhyeti ca raktatām //
children.translated_text: Consciousness projects creation; therein it attains the state of attachment (<s>raktatā</s>);
it projects maintenance and destruction; somewhere it projects doubt;

children.text: tāṃ saṃhṛtya ca bhāvāṃśaṃ saṃhārāt svātmanaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: and having withdrawn that, [it projects] the aspect of existence; and from the withdrawal of itself,
it contemplates its own nature as the withdrawer; within that, regarding merit and demerit,

children.text: na drutaṃ na nirodhaṃ vā svasvātantryeṇa vāñchati //
children.translated_text: it desires neither dissolution nor cessation — by its own autonomy.
Thus, devouring within itself the circle of rays of the aspect of cognition,
it withdraws the suns established in the aspect of the means of knowledge.
Then, having withdrawn the merely-constructed aspect, into the unconstructed heart,
that which transcends even all that, within the uninterrupted splendor,

children.text: nayet tan nayanadvārād viśvaṃ yāvat tathā nayet /
children.translated_text: one should lead [it] through the gate of the eye — whatever of the universe [there is], so should one lead it.
Then one should project creation, and so forth — through the sequence of such practice,
this twelve-spoked wheel (<s>dvādaśāra cakra</s>) ever revolves,
of which these [divisions into] months, zodiac signs, and the like are merely gross [manifestations].
and manifoldly, through various sequences and non-sequences,
Through the power of the sequence-and-non-sequence, in twos, threes,
devouring the knowable, the knowing, the measure, and the knower.
this wheel, as proclaimed, expands —
Because of the resort to the infinite rays and spokes within this wheel,

children.text: cakrabhedo na saṃkhyātuṃ kadācid api śakyate //
children.translated_text: the divisions of the wheel can never be enumerated.
Just as in the feather of a peacock, white, yellow, red, and the like
appear, flashing and closing, even in forms not inherently so —
so too, the Lord of the wheel (<s>cakreśa</s>), fully replete with the subtle consciousnesses that flash open and close within,
shines, variegated with the activity of closing and opening.
That [wheel], through the closing of some [spokes] and the opening of others,
from the one-spoked wheel onward, revolves up to the thousand-spoked.
That [wheel] is innumerable, or mutually harboring one another within,

children.text: na vā tac cakram atha kiṃ vyomaivaikaṃ vijṛmbhate //
children.translated_text: or it is not a wheel at all — but rather, a single sky (<s>vyoman</s>) alone that unfolds.
And that too shines as harboring infinite real wheels within,
or harboring infinite skies — [it is] called the one great sky (<s>mahāvyoman</s>).

children.text: yathā caite meghāḥ punar atha tathā bhānti bahudhā /
children.translated_text: and just as these clouds again appear manifoldly in the same way —
Just as a single sky gleams as white, blue, and red,

children.text: svatantraṃ svākāraiḥ sphurati na ca te ke cana tataḥ //
children.translated_text: and those [forms] are in no way [separate] from it.
so too, the principle of consciousness (<s>saṃvittattva</s>), autonomous, shines forth with its own forms, free from the limitation of enumeration and calculation,
having elucidated this reality,
Thus, my Lord, himself dwelling in the heart,
transmitted through the succession of the lineage of gurus —
assuming wondrous forms,

children.text: tad amutra naye na ye prarūḍhiṃ

children.translated_text: resort to the capacity to realize [it] —
for those who do not attain maturity there, [for those who]
taught the various constructions of <s>maṇḍalas</s>.
for their awakening, the Lord
is joined by its own conventions to those [letters] in sequence —
Just as a child, through written lines in the set of letters,
one is joined to one's own full and priceless splendor.
so too, through <s>mudrās</s>, <s>maṇḍalas</s>, <s>mantras</s>, and <s>tantras</s>,
as distant or near, having adopted a gradation;
Here too, something shines forth solely by his will,
thus, the differentiation within the domain of ritual practice (<s>kriyāpaṭala</s>) is indeed manifold.
yet untouched [by that gradation], established in the state beyond parts —

children.text: itthaṃ pramāṇatābhāgi yat tattvaṃ hi nyarūpyata /
children.translated_text: Thus, that reality which has been elucidated as partaking of the [three] means of knowledge —

children.text: parāparā bhagavatī seyaṃ bhāti tathā tathā //
children.translated_text: the supreme and non-supreme Goddess (<s>Bhagavatī</s>) — she shines in various ways.

children.text: tad atraiva parāṃśo yaḥ sa mātraṃśo 'paraḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, the supreme aspect is the 'measure' (<s>mātra</s>) aspect; the non-supreme, again,

children.text: meyāṃśa iti tat pūrvam evāsmābhiḥ prakāśitam //
children.translated_text: is the 'measurable' (<s>meya</s>) aspect — this has been illuminated by us previously.

children.text: mātraṃśo 'pi pare bhāge bahudhā yat sthitas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: The 'measure' aspect too, insofar as it is situated manifoldly in the supreme portion —
that which is predominantly supreme-and-non-supreme is the <s>Mantreśvara</s>-form.
That which has a predominance of the non-supreme is called <s>Mantra</s>.
And the knower (<s>mātā</s>) who is [equally] supreme and non-supreme, with a predominance of the supreme-and-non-supreme —
he is called <s>Vijñānākala</s>, one whose supreme nature is awakened.
Through a predominance of the non-supreme aspect, that very one is the <s>Pralayākala</s>.

children.text: aparaḥ kila yo mātā sakalaḥ sa tu bhāṣyate /
children.translated_text: The knower who is [entirely] non-supreme is declared to be <s>Sakala</s>.
Through the divisions of supreme, non-supreme, and the rest, his states are also manifold.
When examined, [the system] amply generates innumerable divisions of knowers.
But principally, seven divisions of knowers alone are proclaimed.

children.text: pramāṇāṃśe patanty eva teṣām eva svaśaktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their own powers fall within the aspect of the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>);
we consider that this capacity for operation is precisely what constitutes power (<s>śakti</s>).

children.text: yac ca vyāpriyamāṇatvaṃ karaṇatvaṃ tad eva hi /
children.translated_text: And that which is the state of operating is indeed the state of being an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).
Thus, from the divisions of the possessor-of-power and power, born of the knower and the means of knowledge —
the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is declared to be of fourteen forms.

children.text: mātā mānaṃ ca meyaṃ ca yata ekaṃ prakīrtitam //
children.translated_text: Since the knower, the means of knowledge, and the knowable are proclaimed as one,
therefore [reality is] of fifteen forms as one, fivefold in nature.
And therein, in the division of each one singly, having its own principle-nature,
the infinity of divisions, made through condensation and expansion, is made manifest.
Again, through the sequence of gathering the divisions from water and the rest down to the root,
an even greater flood of variety arises from the sub-divisions of divisions.
principle, fifteen [categories] have been stated.
Thus, from earth onward, up to the <s>Pradhāna</s>

children.text: bhūto na mātā na ca mānarūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: as [that domain] — he is neither [simply] a knower nor of the nature of a means of knowledge.
From <s>Puruṣa</s> to <s>Kalā</s>, the <s>Sakala</s> [knower] has its own nature
In the [spiritual] night, the nature of the <s>Pralayākala</s> would obtain;
Thus, the thirteen-fold nature is here established.
in the stage of <s>Vidyā</s>, the nature pertaining to <s>Mantra</s>.
in the middle, the nature of the <s>Vijñānākala</s>;

children.text: aiśe mantreśavargasthitir atha suśive dhāmni tannāthaniṣṭhā
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca tatra prakaṭayati nijāṃ mātṛmānavyavasthām /
children.translated_text: And each preceding [level] manifests its own arrangement of knower and means of knowledge.
In the lordly [stage], the state of the <s>Mantreśvara</s>-group; then, in the auspicious abode of <s>Śiva</s>, the culmination of their Lord.
But from <s>Mantreśvara</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> downward, the divisions are in the numbers of the three-arrowed [i.e., <s>Kāma</s>, 5], the Sage [i.e., 7], and the three-eyed [i.e., 3].
Therefore, the state of <s>Śiva</s>, self-luminous, ever one, with no other knower, shines forth.
therefore, it does not attain difference or separateness.
And power (<s>śakti</s>) is not different from the possessor of power (<s>śaktimān</s>);
therefore, the essential nature [of the knower] is not [merely] endowed with power [as something separate].
And in the absence of a knower, there is no power;
The luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) that shines without differentiation from the earth-principle —

children.text: sa eva śivanātho 'tra pṛthivī brahma tatparam //
children.translated_text: that very one is <s>Śivanātha</s> here; the earth is <s>Brahman</s>, that supreme [reality].
Those who are prepared to bestow the accomplishments (<s>siddhis</s>) pertaining to the earth-principle,
and who impel [beings] by <s>Śiva</s>'s will — they are the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s>.

children.text: preryamāṇās tu mantreśā mantrās tadvācakāḥ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: But those being impelled — the <s>mantreśas</s> (lords of mantras) [and] <s>mantras</s> are clearly their designators,
having practiced yoga pertaining to the <s>dharā</s> (earth) principle through the <s>Śiva</s> knowledge.
But not those of such views as <s>Pāśupata</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and the like —
who have not attained the fixed abode, who partake of the <s>vijñānakala</s> (pure knower) [level],
who, through the enjoyment of the respective <s>tattvas</s> (principles), have undergone dissolution at the end of the cosmic cycle —
just as those in the state of deep sleep, they are here [called] <s>pralayakevalins</s> (dissolution-liberated souls).

children.text: sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭam eva hi lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: In deep sleep, absorption into the <s>tattvas</s> is clearly observed;
otherwise, whence would there be this much specific association of dreams?

children.text: sauṣuptam api citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Deep sleep too appears as variegated — clear, unclear, and so forth —
from the observation of the variety of memories [such as] 'I slept happily' and the like.
Those mingled with the impurity in the form of the upsurge of <s>māyā</s> and <s>karma</s>,
ascending upon the earth [principle] — these are to be known as <s>sakalas</s> (souls endowed with all impurities) here.
Of this very septenary, in the construction of its respective functions,

children.text: prakṣobho yas tad evoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: the agitation that [occurs] — that is what is spoken of as the septenary of <s>śaktis</s> (powers).
<s>Śiva</s>, of unfallen consciousness-nature, and those three powers of his —
they, by the force of autonomy, have assumed the forms of grasper and graspable.
Through the predominance of the grasper-aspect, and through the springing forth of the graspable-aspect —

children.text: sapta sapteti yat tv ekaṃ jaḍamātraṃ narātmakam //
children.translated_text: [they become] seven and seven. But as for the one that is mere inertness, of the nature of <s>nara</s> (the human) —
its essential nature, therefore threefold, is established for each <s>tattva</s>.

children.text: kiṃ cārthe khalu nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Moreover, in an object to be grasped, indeed the instants — sixteen <s>tuṭis</s> (micro-moments) —
are constructed for each, through the penetration of two-and-a-quarter finger-breadths.
Therein, the first [<s>tuṭi</s>] is of the nature of the essence of supreme non-duality, without distinction.

children.text: antyas tu grāhyatādātmyān na pṛthak pravibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: The last, due to identity with graspability, is not separately discerned.
The penultimate is understood as the grasper of the essential nature of that [object].

children.text: ādyaṃ ca saptakaṃ tatra nirvikalpakatāṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: And the first septenary therein has attained the state of being non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>),
skilled in obscuring [awareness] through the shadow of the gradually opening conceptual aspect.

children.text: tad eva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: That very [septenary] is known to be of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, consisting of the supreme power.
The second septenary therein is of the nature of the supreme-and-non-supreme stage,
called '<s>vikalpa</s>' (conceptual construction) — thus difference is manifested.
In this subtle awareness, those who have set about to measure —

children.text: saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vā vikatthanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: what form they perceive there — what use are boasts about that?

children.text: kramāt tu bhedanyūnatve tuṭīnām api yo mataḥ //
children.translated_text: Progressively, the diminution of difference in the <s>tuṭis</s> that is accepted,
and the diminution of <s>vikalpa</s> — that is the characteristic of the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>).
Just as one who has long suffered pain, and thereafter has attained a state of happiness,
forgets that very pain through the path of resting in happiness —
so too, even when <s>vikalpa</s> has departed, people who are established in cognition,
by the force of resting in [post-conceptual] <s>vikalpa</s>, do not acknowledge that [non-conceptual] state.
the awareness barren of <s>vikalpa</s>, true in the ultimate sense,
Through the diminution of <s>vikalpa</s>,
let the good intellect of those who strive in that attention [recognize this].
attains the manifestness of its nature as consciousness — thus
Attentiveness to the relation between the cognition of graspable and grasper —
this is declared [to be the practice] there, through the connection with the desired fruit.

children.text: ata eva hi tadbhedabāhulyād bhuvanāny api /
children.translated_text: Therefore, due to the multiplicity of their differences, even the worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>)
attain variety — and [yet] transgression [of the system] is not accepted.
This [occurs] both sequentially and non-sequentially, from the prior refutation of time;
and the ultimate reality of direction (<s>diś</s>) is simply not established by reasoning.

children.text: pūrvāparapratītiṃ hi naikā sā kurute tathā /
children.translated_text: For that single [consciousness] does not produce the cognition of before and after in that way.

children.text: upādhibhedo no vastu tat kathaṃ sā prakalpyatām //
children.translated_text: The difference of limiting adjuncts is not [a difference of] substance — so how can it [direction] be constructed?

children.text: yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭa ity ataḥ parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For whatever is superior in qualities to whatever — therefore the Supreme Lord
has spoken [of this], whose sphere of direction and time is fashioned by his own bliss.
Thus, for those who wish to enter into this variegated form of the <s>tattvas</s>,
a threefold [classification] has been described in the [types of] <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), through the difference of means.
The <s>Śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to <s>Śiva</s>) is without means; then comes the means of consciousness (<s>cit</s>);

children.text: jaḍopāyas tv āṇavaḥ syāt sa cāpi bahudhā mataḥ //
children.translated_text: the means of the inert (<s>jaḍa</s>) is the <s>Āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual soul) — and that too is considered manifold.
Even in what is non-inert, through the connection with supreme lordship,
there is the appearance of inertness — of <s>nāḍī</s> (channel), sense-organ, external [objects], and the like. By this, [there is] the status of consciousness as a means.
Therein, the apprehension of external form that occurs by resorting to the activity of the senses —
that [state], which abides as clearly waking, follows [one] again and again.
The construction made by one's own imagination is dream — the opposite of waking.

children.text: layākalasya yo bhogaḥ layakarmavaśān na tu //
children.translated_text: The enjoyment of one in whom the <s>kalā</s> (power of limited action) has dissolved — through the force of the <s>karma</s> of dissolution, but not
stable, due to the state of night — is deep sleep, [characterized by] non-cognition of pleasure and the like.
Of one in whom the <s>kalā</s> of knowledge has [dissolved], through impurity alone, from mere enjoyment,
the differentiated [states], differing from themselves, both inert and non-inert, are willed [into being].
In the fourth [state] (<s>turya</s>), the three — <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantranāthas</s> (lords of mantras), and <s>mantramaheśvaras</s> (great lords of mantras) — are established therein,
insofar as the states are capable of bearing the entry of the <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness aspect,
[and] their own essence draining away, [they become] spontaneously non-differentiated.
In the state beyond the fourth (<s>turyātīta</s>) they will be — thus, in this fifteenfold [schema]:

children.text: yasya yad yad sphuṭaṃ rūpaṃ taj jāgrad iti manyatām //
children.translated_text: whatever form of whatever is clearly manifest — let that be considered 'waking.'

children.text: tad evāsthiram ābhāti svarūpaṃ svapna īdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: That very same form, when it appears unstably — such is dream.

children.text: asphuṭaṃ tu yad ābhāti suptaṃ tat tat puro 'pi yat //
children.translated_text: But what appears unclearly — that is deep sleep; and what [appears] before that too [is the same].
But the connecting thread (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) of the three, by whose force it arises —
that is the fourth (<s>turya</s>), like the thread of a garland — let it be grasped in all [states of] difference.
But that which shines with the upsurge of non-dual experience, melting away all difference —

children.text: turyātītaṃ tu tat prāhur itthaṃ sarvatra yojayet //
children.translated_text: that they call the 'beyond the fourth' (<s>turyātīta</s>). Thus one should apply [this scheme] everywhere.

children.text: layākale hi svaṃ rūpaṃ jāgrattatpūrvavṛtti tu /
children.translated_text: In the <s>layākala</s> (dissolution-limited soul) indeed, its own nature is waking; the prior state thereof
is dream and the rest — the wise one should trace this sequence throughout.
Even in the one Lord alone, who is complete, consciousness is called <s>turyātīta</s>;
bliss is the fourth (<s>turya</s>); will itself is the seed-ground, [which is] the state of deep sleep;

children.text: jñānaṃ tu svapnavṛttitvaṃ kriyā jāgrad iti smṛtā /
children.translated_text: knowledge is the state of dream; action is said to be waking.
Here itself, the designations arising from the stages of yoga — <s>piṇḍastha</s> (established in the body) and the rest —
[and those like] <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious in all directions) and the rest, are constructed by those who know enumeration (<s>prasaṃkhyā</s>).
Since the four forms exist in each one, therefore, in the extended [scheme],
there is fourness in each; then threeness afterward; then oneness.
But the one Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, shining forth in the form of the universe,
is one — conjoined with the state extending from <s>Śiva</s> to <s>sakala</s> (the fully bound soul).
This entire path (<s>adhvan</s>), possessing the mode of non-difference from <s>Bhairava</s>,
appears as partaking of autonomy through his autonomy.
This [path], abiding in the form of the knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), is conceived as the <s>mantrādhvan</s> (path of mantras).
In the form of the means of knowledge (<s>pramā</s>), this is etymologically explained as the <s>varṇādhvan</s> (path of phonemes).
Having attained the form of the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), this goes to [being] the <s>padādhvan</s> (path of words).
Without abandoning the entry into the form of the means of knowledge, [when it attains] the state of the knowable (<s>meya</s>),
proceeding through the connection of construction — [it becomes] the <s>kalādhvan</s> (path of <s>kalās</s>), conjoined with the knower.
In the conjunction of pure knowability, let it be grasped as the <s>tattvādhvan</s> (path of <s>tattvas</s>).
Through the conjunction of being the support for the grossness thereof, it is described as the <s>bhuvanādhvan</s> (path of worlds).

children.text: tathā hi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā /
children.translated_text: For thus, when the state of what is to be expressed is swallowed by the reflective awareness of consciousness,
devoted to the thinking and protecting that depend on the knowledge and action of <s>Śiva</s>,
through the dexterity and playfulness of the entire array of powers,

children.text: mantrādhvā rabhasena drāk prāg udbhūtaḥ śivātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>mantrādhvan</s> (path of mantras), of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, springs forth impetuously at the outset.
[The mantras,] possessing the relishing of rest in the mere springing-forth of consciousness,
of unrestricted powers through the capacity of all designations,
are emitted, functioning from the co-arising object with their own self, down to the earth [principle].
Reflecting upon the corresponding objects within their own self,
in [their] own play of consciousness — they bear a true awareness of the nature of knowledge (<s>pramā</s>).
Children, animals, and other knowing subjects, who do not partake of [linguistic] convention —
even they, resorting to this self-awareness whose essence is unfabricated impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
variously differentiated, attain the variegated state of being knowing subjects.
If conventions attain firm establishment in this unfabricated awareness

children.text: saṃketā yānti cet te 'pi yānty asaṃketavṛttitām //
children.translated_text: of infinite phonemes — then even those [conventions] attain the functioning of non-convention.
