children.text: anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: But without this [natural awareness], all conventions, however many times they are made,
would never come to rest in the mind — through the connection with other conventions,
and from the non-termination [of the regress], and from [the consequence of] undermining the foundation.

children.text: tatrāpi khalu saṃkete bālo vyutpādyatāṃ kutaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even there, in [the establishment of] convention, how would a child be instructed?

children.text: tenānantas tv amāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the infinite, non-illusory (<s>amāyīya</s>) group of phonemes of this kind,
accompanied by the reflective awareness of consciousness, always unfolds.

children.text: tata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire /
children.translated_text: And from that very [source], the illusory (<s>māyīya</s>) phonemes have extended their birth.

children.text: teṣāṃ te khalv amāyīyā vīryam ity avadhāryate //
children.translated_text: For those [illusory phonemes], those non-illusory ones are indeed ascertained to be [their] potency (<s>vīrya</s>).

children.text: tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣv āvṛṇute nijā /
children.translated_text: For thus, when the utterances of another are heard, [if] one's own

children.text: pramā yasya jaḍo nāsau tatrārthe yāti mātṛtām //
children.translated_text: knowledge (<s>pramā</s>) conceals [meaning] — he is not inert, [and yet] regarding that object he attains the status of the knower.

children.text: yasya tu svapramā bodhe praviśed bhedagarbhagā /
children.translated_text: But for one whose own knowledge enters into awakening, carrying difference within —
in his own cluster of illusory (<s>māyīya</s>) phonemes, he attains the status of knowing subject.
And to the extent that the unfabricated form thereof predominates,
to that extent the gradation of aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) is constructed.
But when the predominance thereof is great, [those who are] established in the nature of intuitive insight (<s>pratibhā</s>)
assuredly attain everywhere the excellence of poetic genius and eloquence.

children.text: ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the attainment of the power of speech, the worship of the phonemes [is practiced];

children.text: teṣām eva tatas tena guptā guptena bhāṣitāḥ //
children.translated_text: of those very [phonemes], therefore, by the hidden one [<s>Śiva</s>], the hidden [meanings] are spoken.
Then, so long as the Lord's perpetual repose extends, simultaneously encompassing many
phonemes, well-established in the fulfillment of the enjoyment-aspect —
just so long does this <s>padādhvan</s> (path of words), having resorted to the ground of the knowable,
[constitute] the first sprout in the aggregate of conventional signs that are dead-yet-alive in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: evaṃ prameyatā mātṛbhāvo mānatvam apy atha /
children.translated_text: Thus, the status of the knowable, the knower-state, and also the status of means-of-knowledge
are ascertained of the aggregate of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>.

children.text: tatra sarvaṃ vibhāty etat parameśitari dhruve /
children.translated_text: Therein, all this shines in the fixed Supreme Lord
in the form of a reflection — not as something external, because
in the sky of consciousness that is <s>Śiva</s>, this cognition of body and such,

children.text: bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ bhāti rajjau sarpādikā yathā //
children.translated_text: differentiated, shines for the transmigrating souls — as a snake and the like in a rope.
For the established conclusion of [prior] body and death is the domain of dream;
the assumption of another body after death — of what kind is the [real] arising of a body?
But in dream, from the forcible manifestation of the generic [form] of mere intuitive insight (<s>pratibhā</s>),

children.text: viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante 'pi te tathā //
children.translated_text: the particulars appear — though they are not even intended as such.
Just as certain <s>śālagrāma</s> stones have wondrous patterns in their hearts,
so too the lines within the ground [stretching] from <s>māyā</s> to the end are of consciousness, with wondrous hearts.
Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like conform to the will of that [consciousness];
they are not, by themselves, of the nature of existent or non-existent, cause or non-cause.
When a long-established rule is cut off, [and] from the setting-in-motion [of a new one] —
even when [the rule] is not [yet] established — this <s>Bhairava</s> of the sky of consciousness stands autonomous.
In [that consciousness] which partakes of non-difference from <s>Bhairava</s>, full of sole consciousness —
the non-reflection 'I am thus' is the differentiator in the circle of existents.

children.text: sarvapramāṇair no siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream, no other agent is established by any means of knowledge,
so too let creation be understood as [arising] from autonomous self-awareness.

children.text: cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍann evaṃ hi vetti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who, playing in the garden of the city that is the mind's painting,

children.text: aham eva sthito bhāvair bhūtaiś cinmātrakair iti //
children.translated_text: knows thus: 'I alone exist as states — beings that are mere consciousness' —
thus, the varieties of 'I have been born, I have died' — birth and death —
shine on the wall of the mind, self-constructed, in that which is birthless and deathless.
The state of 'this world and the other world' is merely the cognition of the supreme will.
However, even in the difference of time, <s>kalā</s>, awareness, and place, it is non-different.

children.text: abhaviṣyad ayaṃ sargo mūrtaś cen na tu cinmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If this creation were material, it would have existed [independently]; but it is not — it is made of consciousness.
Then let even a single mountain be discerned from within it [independently of consciousness]!
In the discussion of the support and the supported regarding the group of elements, subtle elements, and the like,
at the end, the power made of consciousness, of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> alone, is the supporter.

children.text: tasmāt pratītir evetthaṃ kartrī sā pratibhā śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, cognition itself is the agent — that intuitive insight (<s>pratibhā</s>) is <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: atra svātmani te tena śaktiḥ sādhārasaṃjñitā //
children.translated_text: Here, that power, in its own self, is called <s>sādhāra</s> (supporting) by him.

children.text: sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāram api naiva pataty adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even what is imagined, without [external] support, does not fall downward —
through its rest in the self-supporting power. Let the universe be reflected upon in this way.
From the firm establishment of this [consciousness] in the form of the dense 'I' and the like — the state of earth and the rest;
until, at the end, 'I am consciousness' — the nature of <s>Bhairava</s> is accomplished.

children.text: maṇāv indrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive /
children.translated_text: Just as blue and the like appear in a rainbow or on a gem — in <s>Śiva</s>,
but in ultimate reality, these have no connection with arising or ceasing.

children.text: deśe kāle 'tra vā sṛṣṭir ity etad asamañjasam /
children.translated_text: 'Creation [occurs] in place, in time, or here' — this is incoherent,

children.text: cidātmano hi devasya sṛṣṭir dikkālayor api //
children.translated_text: for the creation of the Lord who is of the nature of consciousness includes even direction and time.
In the [space of] one-and-a-half cubits to which waking [experience] is ascribed,
and in [the duration of] a watch (<s>prahara</s>), there are separate dreams — imagining diverse directions and times.

children.text: ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcid api manmahe /
children.translated_text: Therefore, we do not consider there to be anything called a 'moment';

children.text: kriyākṣaṇe 'pi hy ekasmin bahvyaḥ santi drutāḥ kriyāḥ //
children.translated_text: for even in a single moment of action, there are many swift actions.
Therefore, those who have accepted the contraction of entities as ending in a moment
are surely, through this pipe [of reasoning], dependent on the view of the void (<s>śūnyadṛṣṭi</s>).

children.text: tad ya eva sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkatuṃ tahtāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, by his autonomy, is able to nullify existing entities
and to make manifest those that do not [yet] exist — that Lord is the supreme Lord.
Thus, the supreme Lord is proclaimed as having the universe as his form;

children.text: na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāder upapannatā //
children.translated_text: but the existence of any separate entity — earth and the rest — is not established.

children.text: uktaṃ caitat puraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate /
children.translated_text: This has been stated before, and so is not investigated further;
and the refutation of external objects has been composed by many others as well.
Objection: 'If so, [then] birth and death, and the connection of action with its fruit —

children.text: kathaṃ syāt kin nu pūrvoktaṃ citsvātantryaṃ suvisṛmtam //
children.translated_text: how would they be possible? Or has the previously stated autonomy of consciousness been forgotten?'

children.text: tathā hi citsvatantreyaṃ yathā bhāsayate tathā /
children.translated_text: Reply: For this consciousness, being autonomous, manifests however it manifests;

children.text: satyaṃ bhāty akhilākāragarbhā sā ceti niścitam //
children.translated_text: truly, it shines forth containing all forms within itself — this is certain.

children.text: ikṣau pratyaṇu mādhuryaṃ yathā sarvātmanā tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as in sugarcane, sweetness pervades every particle in its entirety,
so in each individual atom there abides the state of containing all creation.
But those scholars who dispute about this, not knowing the root-<s>tattva</s> (reality),
are surely engaged in protecting their own fantasy-kingdoms.

children.text: prāṇe khe citi bāhye vā kutrāpīdam iti bhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is it in the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), in the void, in consciousness, or externally?' — this confusion [of theirs]
is a manifestation of the absence of autonomy arising from the fixity of ignorance.
Therefore, the self-reflection of one's own consciousness shines here as 'birth';
but previously, consciousness was not in a form befitting [its own] autonomy.
The prior consciousness itself is here called 'former <s>karma</s>' (action);
the consciousness that overrides that [prior] consciousness is what destroys <s>karma</s>.

children.text: akṛtaṃ ca yathā svapne mayā kṛtam iti sphuret /
children.translated_text: And just as in a dream, 'this was done by me' flashes forth though it was never done,

children.text: phaladā dṛśyate saiva vārtā jāgrati karmaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and that very [cognition] is seen to be fruit-bearing — such is the story of <s>karma</s> in waking too.
And so, if even a single consciousness arises that is of the nature

children.text: yasyaikāpy uttarodeti saṃvit sa phalabhāṅ na hi //
children.translated_text: of scorching the fruits of the mass of prior actions — then he is not a partaker of [those] fruits.
Moreover, through the clear flashing of many other consciousnesses, infamy [becomes] fame,
and more — [it becomes] fruitful, like a seed watered by the waters of a heavenly river.
Thus, <s>karma</s> of little fruit, flashing in a slight cognition,

children.text: asphuran niṣphalaṃ tv eva nyāyaḥ so 'yaṃ svasaṃvidam //
children.translated_text: [and karma] not flashing at all, is indeed fruitless — this is the principle regarding one's own consciousness.
And even therein, the smallness or abundance that are attributed to cognitions —
those belong to the doer of <s>karma</s> through the maturation of his consciousness, partaking of that form.

children.text: yā ca (yasya) saṃvit svayaṃ tādṛkphalagarbhā na jāyate /
children.translated_text: And for one whose consciousness does not itself arise as pregnant with such fruit,
nor through contact with a cognizer who apprehends another's fruit —
even in the consciousness of another cognizer who knows the fruit,
from the construction of yet another cognizer — until the end, that [chain] is something or other, sufficient [to explain it].
One who is awakened, [seeing] creation as imperishable, an unfolder of the power of maintenance,
we know, contracts the constructions of fruit-dependence.

children.text: matsyād amatsyadṛṣṭyeyaṃ sṛṣṭir ity āśayena te /
children.translated_text: 'This creation [goes] from fish to non-fish in [its] vision' — with this intent,
the ancients taught that benefit to others should be performed.
Thus, this so-called benefit is extended even to the dead;
through the offering of <s>piṇḍa</s> (funerary rice-ball) and the like, a further bodily connection is given [to them].

children.text: varaṃ svātmani saṃkleśāḥ paraṃ mā pīḍayan tv iti /
children.translated_text: 'Better that sufferings afflict my own self — let them not torment another' —

children.text: iti kalpitam etasya kṛcchrādes tapasaḥ phalam //
children.translated_text: thus has the fruit of austerity such as <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) and the like been constructed.
Regarding garlic and the like, the inedibility that has been stated — the injunction is of this nature:
let creatures simply accept it as without [external] cause.
Thus, in determining the edibility or inedibility of swans, partridges, and the like,

children.text: yujyeta bhinnabuddhitvam anyathā nna kathaṃ cana //
children.translated_text: the difference of understanding is justified; otherwise, [it is justified] in no way whatsoever.
Thus, in both the seen and the unseen [domains], from the progression of constructed portions and sub-portions,

children.text: phalayogaḥ sa evādya rūḍhaḥ saṃvidbhuvi sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: that very connection with fruit, now matured, abides in the ground of consciousness.

children.text: dehaḥ piṇḍāt pare loke nānyatheti sthitiḥ kṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'The body [arises] from the <s>piṇḍa</s> in the other world, not otherwise' — such is the established [belief];
'The non-connection of beings with each other is what constitutes embodiment' — [is this so?]
And by the multitudes of all scriptures, stakes of doubt have been driven in,
mounted on the ground of the ignorant mind, reaching to the endpoint of fruit-[bearing].
'There is a giver of <s>piṇḍa</s> for me; today I, through the procedure of <s>piṇḍa</s>-offering,
shall obtain the enjoyment of [bodily] limbs — I am well-established with a complete body.'
Through invisible action (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), fashioned by sons, disciples, one's own self, and the like —
'I, possessing a heavenly share, am supremely well-established in enjoyment of pleasures.'

children.text: nāsti me piṇḍadaḥ kaś cit svayaṃ cāsmy atiduṣkṛtī /
children.translated_text: 'There is no giver of <s>piṇḍa</s> for me, and I myself am extremely sinful;

children.text: na me trātāsti kutrāpi patāmi narakārṇave //
children.translated_text: there is no savior for me anywhere — I am falling into the ocean of hell.'

children.text: bhaviṣyati mama trātā kvāpi kāle kathaṃ cana /
children.translated_text: 'Somehow, at some time, there will be a savior for me' —

children.text: ityādiḥ saṃvidāṃ sphāras tathaiva phalati svayam //
children.translated_text: such and similar expansions of cognitions bear fruit just as they are, by themselves.

children.text: tasyās tu piṇḍakartrādir mābhūd atha yathā sphuret /
children.translated_text: But whether the maker of the <s>piṇḍa</s> and the like exists for that [being] or not — however it flashes [in consciousness],

children.text: sa tāvat tatphalaṃ bhuṅkte svasaṃkalpena kalpitam //
children.translated_text: to that extent he experiences that fruit, constructed by his own intention.
But this conviction, firmly bound within the plaster of the thunderbolt of doubt —
the fire of <s>Bhairava</s> alone burns it instantly, root and all.
The fire that exultantly [declares] 'I am <s>Śiva</s> himself' is the incinerator
of the dream-mansion of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), which is the womb of all variegated consciousnesses.
The one deluded by it — whose consciousness is variegated by the consciousness of <s>karma</s> —
considers the manifold <s>saṃsāra</s> to be nothing but [his own] mental construction.
For this reason, a child who has died, being devoid of other latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
becomes a child [again], with deep-rooted impressions of <s>saṃsāra</s> dormant [within].
Those two likewise (?)
until youth is again reached, through the progression of those latent impressions.
Through the consciousness [rooted in] impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), he regards those various
transmigrations as [real]. Some, from the impression of inertness, though having become inert, through the sky-elements and winds,
together with the conjunction of earth and water, attain the nature of flowers and fruits;
when consumed, in the form of semen, [they] again enter the womb —

children.text: yāvad punaḥ punaś citrān saṃsārān abhimanyate /
children.translated_text: as long as, again and again, [the being] regards the manifold <s>saṃsāras</s> [as real],
[it is because] <s>Śiva</s>, perfumed by the latent impressions of his own <s>saṃskāras</s> in that one place alone,
experiences his own hells and the like — enjoyments fashioned by [his own] autonomy.

children.text: kvacid bhūmimayī kvāpi jalātmā kvāpi miśritā //
children.translated_text: Sometimes the [experience] is of the nature of earth, sometimes of water, sometimes mixed —

children.text: evaṃ bhuvanamayy eṣā saṃvid bhāti svarūpataḥ /
children.translated_text: thus this consciousness, consisting of worlds, shines forth from its own nature.
Wherever it is sustained, there alone, from its own impressions, [it experiences]

children.text: vetty anyena na dṛśyas tu sa tv anyān veda cānyathā /
children.translated_text: pleasure and the like — [the being] knows [this] by another [consciousness], though not seen by others; and he knows others differently.

children.text: na deśaḥ paramārthena na ca kālo 'sti kaś cana //
children.translated_text: In ultimate reality, there is no space whatsoever, nor any time.
For in the doctrine of difference, from the space of the sky [being one], everything would be in one place;

children.text: upādher eva deśād bhiddeśasyāpy upādher bhidā //
children.translated_text: if [space-difference depends] on the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) alone, then from the spatial difference of the adjunct, the adjunct too would differ —

children.text: ity anyonyasamāśrityā deśabhedo na kaś cana /
children.translated_text: thus, through mutual dependence, there is no spatial difference whatsoever.
Therefore, only the difference of essential nature is well-suited as the cause of difference;

children.text: sa ca nāsti prakāśaikasvarūpeṣv iti sādhitam /
children.translated_text: and that [difference of nature] does not exist in things whose sole nature is illumination — this has been established.
Those who are deprived of this vision of self-reflective awareness,
are made suspicious by the masses of doubt-producing scriptures [of rival schools], made to conform to those —
through the pseudo-scriptures constructed by the manifold inert creatures fabricated in their own dream,
they are seized by futile doubt, being devoid of awakening.

children.text: yathā prabuddhyante saṃvin nibhṛtāpi ciraṃ sthitā //
children.translated_text: Just as [the latent impressions of] consciousness, though remaining concealed for a long time, come to awakening —
so too, [it is said that] they bear fruit — thus [it is explained] mostly through [the conventional constructs of] mind and the like.
Thus, by [the Lord] who possesses the sovereignty of the autonomy of manifesting diversity,

children.text: kḷptaṃ yad eva tat tasya yāti tanvādirūpatām /
children.translated_text: whatever is fashioned by him assumes the form of body and the rest.
When there is the manifestation of reversal — [the body being] damaged by the manifestation of cold and the like,
afflicted in the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) and the like by contraction, bursting, blows, and the like,
when the wind-wheel of the great machine of the body-bellows goes otherwise —
<s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) disintegrates; thereby the body, which manifests as inert,

children.text: yasmin yāty adhikāre vā jāte prāg vāsanākramāt //
children.translated_text: [passes to] whatever [realm of] jurisdiction arises — or from the succession of prior latent impressions,
there alone he constructs enjoyment, designated as the 'other world';

children.text: pāṣāṇatāṃ vā vetty eṣa punar vā pratibudhyate //
children.translated_text: or he attains the state of a stone — or he awakens again.

children.text: paro 'yaṃ loka iti ca rūḍhyāsya paralokitā /
children.translated_text: 'This is the other world' — through convention, his 'other-worldliness' [is established].
Whatever has been firmly established in his mind here

children.text: tathaivāsya bahir bhāti tatas tatrāpi citratā /
children.translated_text: regarding heaven, liberation, and the like — just so it shines forth externally for him; hence even there, [there is] variety.

children.text: bandho mokṣaḥ sukhaṃ svargo duḥkhaṃ jaḍamayī sthitiḥ //
children.translated_text: Bondage, liberation, happiness, heaven, suffering, the state of inertness —
consciousness itself, being autonomous, in this way shines forth in the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Just as the sense of 'I' pertains to a body endowed with limbs to the extent [of those limbs],
so too the sense of 'I' pertains even to <s>Bhairava</s>, whose form is the entire universe.
A child, even in [what is] empty [of reality], cognizes a ghost as producing real effects;
the variety of objects of meditation, worship, and the like is likewise efficacious in producing real effects.

children.text: mūrto bhinnaḥ samāhūto hitvā bhogān nijān kṣaṇāt //
children.translated_text: 'The embodied, differentiated [deity], when summoned, abandoning his own enjoyments in an instant,

children.text: deva etīti vārtaiṣā vacaneṣv eva śobhate /
children.translated_text: comes as a god' — this account is fitting only in words [i.e., is merely conventional].
But [the deity's] nature as formless and the like — all of this is indeed justified;

children.text: ātmaiva hi tathābhūtas tathā bhāty eva bhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: for the Self itself, having become of such a form, shines forth precisely as differentiated.

children.text: evaṃ svabhāva evaiṣa saṃvido yaḥ sa eva tu //
children.translated_text: Thus, this very nature of consciousness is what it is; and that very [nature]
— insofar as it is seized by differentiation — is explained in scripture as <s>kārmamala</s> (the impurity of action).
But in the conjunction with the ritual of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and other rites, the status of impurity is not extended;
for that [<s>dīkṣā</s>] is a vow for the burning of the entirety of <s>saṃsāra</s> consisting of differentiation.
And <s>dīkṣā</s>, in reality, is of the nature of that true consciousness,

children.text: evaṃ yo veda tattvenety uktaṃ cānuttare naye /
children.translated_text: 'He who thus knows in truth' — so it is said in the <s>Anuttara</s> (supreme) doctrine.
For when such knowledge-union has been attained, and the domain of differentiation has been pacified —

children.text: ātmaiva śiva evaikaḥ ko bandhaḥ kā ca muktatā /
children.translated_text: the Self alone is <s>Śiva</s>, the One — what bondage is there, and what liberation?
But this is stated for the purpose of entering the great consciousness of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).
That <s>dīkṣā</s>, whose nature is ritual action, is for the removal of the impurities of <s>karma</s> and the rest;
regarding actions that are compelled by the force of fixity produced by [one's own] nature,
the enjoyment of this [individual] is made simultaneously through the power of <s>mantra</s>.
For thus, the determinations pertaining to the <s>prāṇa</s>-path, the spatial, temporal, and supra-temporal paths
— the kinds [of existence] are extended for him from earth to <s>Śiva</s>.
Having established therein the jurisdiction for birth, enjoyment, and dissolution,
he is elevated from that [level] and established in another.
and of the disciple, mutually [engaging] —
Thus, of the guru, whose consciousness-self is of established and matured form,
blocks all the prior powers of <s>karma</s>.
for one whose mind is free from <s>karma</s>, <s>dīkṣā</s> occurs effortlessly [and]
and the like is something fashioned by the burden of Śaiva convention;
Even therein, the ritual sequence of rice, sesame, ghee, and <s>caru</s> (oblation-dish)
has not gone to rootlessness, because the operation of differentiation [persists].
even in that clearly established domain, the elaboration of darkness [i.e., ignorance]
the cause of the destruction of merit and the like that produces future <s>saṃsāra</s>;
Even in [the presence of] differentiation, this [ritual differentiation] will again become

children.text: śuddhas tatas tad ata eva hi tattvajālaṃ

children.translated_text: is precisely twofold, through the division of pure and impure.
from that he is purified — and therefore the entire web of <s>tattvas</s> (realities)

children.text: bhāty eva tena bahudhaiṣa kṛtaḥ kriyāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: shines forth; therefore this manifold elaboration of <s>niyati</s> (fixity/cosmic order) has been made,
The pure [domain], studded with three powers, and the <s>Yāmala</s> (paired/tantric) [tradition] —
with the conjunction of greater or lesser enjoyments fashioned accordingly.
through the conceptual construction of the operation of action,
The assemblage of <s>mudrās</s> (seals) and <s>maṇḍalas</s> (sacred circles), anointed with <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>,
wherein all [practices] — <s>yoga</s> and the rest — are fashioned for the bestowal of fruit.
Those who are firmly established in the contraction of the desire for the attainment of the fruit of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation/bliss)
consider unlimitedness itself as the fruit here.

children.text: na hy anantānav/yacchede kāpi yāgādikalpanā anavacchinnavāñchā // 1.1131 //
children.translated_text: For in [the state of] endless non-limitation, there is no construction of sacrifice and the like; the desire [itself] is unlimited.
Those whose vision has transcended all that —
nevertheless, regarding the known reality, which is the beautiful supreme non-dual —
from the autonomy of the nature of consciousness, for some [there remains] the desire for [specific] fruits;

children.text: tāny evoddiśya tat sarvaṃ pūraṇāya dharāditaḥ //
children.translated_text: aiming at those very [fruits], all that [ritual array] — for the sake of fulfillment — from earth
to <s>Śiva</s>, in manifold divisions — is called the <s>dhāraṇā</s> text.

children.text: sphuritam asti na yat kila satyataḥ /
children.translated_text: that has manifested that is not truly [real];
For here, unlike in other doctrines, there is nothing
what indeed could fall into the category of the to-be-rejected?
therefore, for those who partake of the state of the truly real,

children.text: tan nirṇītam anuttaraṃ śivapadaṃ saṃprāptikāmān prati /
children.translated_text: has been determined — the unsurpassed state of <s>Śiva</s>, for those who desire attainment.
Thus, the <s>tattva</s> that shines forth as the final one of the seventeenth chapter

children.text: etat sarvam ihoditaṃ ca jagadānande vipakṣātmakaṃ
bhedaprāṇatayā yato 'tra nikhilo 'py eṣa prapañcaḥ sthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: this entire manifest world abides as having differentiation for its very life-breath.
And all this has been stated here as opposing the universal bliss — [only] because
Second Section
Thus, the Lord <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), established as having the universe for his Self,
is worshipped through <s>dhāraṇās</s> (contemplations), through the sequential practice of knowledge.
The sequence of <s>tattvas</s>, having gone beyond duality — the web of <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and the rest —

children.text: aṣṭādaśe tat paṭale tattvaṃ samyag vibhāvyate //
children.translated_text: that <s>tattva</s> is properly contemplated in the eighteenth chapter.

children.text: prāṇāyāmādikaṃ yatra heyam ity eva varṇyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) and the like are described therein as things to be abandoned.

children.text: na hi tasya parāṃ vittiṃ prati kācid upāyatā //
children.translated_text: For there is no means whatsoever for that [Self] toward the supreme consciousness.

children.text: antaḥ saṃvidi yan nirūḍham abhitas tat prāṇadhīvigrahe

children.translated_text: transferred to the body of breath, mind, and form? Thus, let the method of the practice of <s>abhyāsa</s> (repeated practice) be consistent!
That which is firmly established within consciousness everywhere — how could it be

children.text: ye tv abhyāsapathena saṃvidam imāṃ saṃskartum abhyudyatās
te kiṃ kutra kutaḥ kathaṃ vidadhatām ity atra saṃdihmahe //
children.translated_text: what, where, from what, and how are they accomplishing? — in this we are doubtful.
But those who have undertaken to refine this consciousness through the path of practice —

children.text: abhyāso hi punaḥ punar arthaḥ so 'pi ca dikkālapratibhedāt /
children.translated_text: For <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) is the repetition of an object, and that too, because of the distinction of direction and time,
arising from the conjunction of appearance and other [factors], would be in the path of body, mind, breath, and senses.
Those who desire to speak about the form of <s>Bhairava</s>, which is dense with light alone,
are well established through the repose in the knowledge that has flashed forth just once.

children.text: atraivātaḥ paraṃ proktam aṅgaṃ sarvopakāri yat /
children.translated_text: Therefore, herein, the supreme auxiliary that is helpful to all has been stated:
the <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations) too, ascertained through that very door, would be of such a nature.

children.text: nanv apratiṣṭhe kas tarke samāśvāsaḥ prakalpyatām /
children.translated_text: Now, in reasoning that has no firm ground, what confidence can be fashioned?

children.text: kiṃ vā na bhavatāṃ tādṛg apratiṣṭhāhataṃ vacaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or is not your own statement likewise struck by groundlessness?

children.text: tathā hy āgama evaikaṃ pramāṇam iti niścitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For by those who are certain that <s>āgama</s> (tradition) alone is the one valid means of knowledge,
when there exist multitudes of traditions that contradict each other — how can certainty be reached?
But the well-known acceptance of the multitude (<s>mahājana</s>) is the cause of validity therein.
[Yet] groundlessness [follows], because of the quite possible existence of a multitude opposed to that.
Perception too, in matters of taste and the like, [is subject to] cognitions that are seen to be contradicted;
indeed, it is a receptacle of the infinite regress of ever-subsequent cognitions.

children.text: svasaṃvid api tatraiva bādhiteti kathaṃ kila /
children.translated_text: Self-experience (<s>svasaṃvid</s>) too is contradicted in that very [way] — how then
could this [person], skilled in connecting differences, conduct conventional activity?

children.text: asmākaṃ tv apratiṣṭhānaṃ na kadācit kvacid bhavet /
children.translated_text: But for us, groundlessness never arises anywhere,
for whom the supreme ocean of <s>Bhairava</s> is everywhere complete.

children.text: viśeṣatas tu tarkasya tān praty evāpratiṣṭhatā /
children.translated_text: And the groundlessness of reasoning applies especially to those
who, through the crossing of the ocean of reasoning, have seized the consciousness of the supreme nectar.
For all aspects of reasoning, whose self-experience has not been apprehended,
have not attained <s>Śiva</s> as the ultimate fruit, anywhere.
For the meaning of all scripture is essentially non-difference, [intended] for the attainment of that;

children.text: yas tatrodbhāvito bhedas tatra mūḍhadhiyo ratāḥ //
children.translated_text: the difference that is produced therein — in that, those of deluded intellect are attached.
And reasoning is skilled solely in cutting the logical positions of the doctrine of difference.

children.text: nanv abhede 'pi tarkasya kā cid asty upayogitā //
children.translated_text: But does not reasoning have some utility even in non-difference?

children.text: paramādvayadṛṣṭau ca so 'pi naiva na saṃgataḥ /
children.translated_text: In the vision of the supreme non-duality, that too is not unsuitable.
Therefore, the supreme non-duality (<s>parādvaita</s>), which is of the nature of grace toward the universe —
as its supreme means, he declares the Heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), whose nature is vibration (<s>spandana</s>).
In the Heart, which is composed of awareness, the self-awareness that is the wonder of full consciousness,
simultaneously, swiftly, and forcefully, with the flashing forth of the universe absorbed —
full with the delight of the arising [and] the bliss of the final and initial stages of the apprehension of entities —
that is called the <s>sāmānyaspanda</s> (general vibration), composed of the bliss of the world (<s>jagadānanda</s>).

children.text: sphuraṇaṃ hṛdayasya yat kila prakaṭam idaṃ visargadhāmnaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is indeed the manifest throb of the Heart, from the realm of <s>visarga</s> (emission),

children.text: sad iti pratibhāti yāvatā trikaśaktau viśatīha tāvatā //
children.translated_text: insofar as it appears as "existent" — to that extent it enters into the <s>Trika</s> power here.

children.text: tad idaṃ hṛdayaṃ nirucyate paramaṃ bhairavasaṃvidāmṛtam /
children.translated_text: This Heart is etymologized as the supreme nectar of <s>Bhairava</s>-consciousness,
penetrating the trident of the powers of will (<s>iṣi</s>), vision (<s>dṛk</s>), and action (<s>kṛti</s>); it is then emitted in the supreme abode.

children.text: parame bhagavatparātmani sphuritaṃ viśvam idaṃ cidātmakam /
children.translated_text: In the supreme <s>Bhagavat</s>, the supreme Self, this universe of the nature of consciousness has flashed forth,
penetrating the trident of the three powers; then, through the path of emission in the ground of <s>Śāmbhava</s>,

children.text: tad atho sad iti pragīyate tad idaṃ pūrṇam ihāhamātmakaṃ /
children.translated_text: it is proclaimed below as "existent" — this is complete, of the nature of "I" (<s>aham</s>) here;
the Heart, which is the very throb of the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, always shines forth.
Here, the sequences of creation, dissolution, and maintenance — hundreds, or even thousands of crores —
shine forth with an eternal nature, composed by <s>Hara</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) as causes.

children.text: iha tu puroktād yuktikalāpād yaḥ praviśet sadyo nāśaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: But here, one who from the aforementioned assemblage of reasoning cannot immediately enter, being incapable —
for him, the vibration of the Heart is made manifest through the path of the <s>Śākta</s> means (<s>śāktopāya</s>).
Having attained the path of the Heart through the impulsion of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) situated at the tips of the trident,
intent upon repose in the <s>kalā</s> (phase) of the moon of consciousness situated within that —

children.text: jhaṭity evātha tadbhūmityāgena projjhya tā daśāḥ /
children.translated_text: then, suddenly, through the arrival at that ground, casting off those states
beginning with <s>nirānanda</s> (blisslessness) and so forth, the five [states] situated in the middle of the elements —
one should abandon the prior and ascend to the subsequent, intent upon proper repose,
because the ground that is composed of one's own bliss (<s>nijānanda</s>) follows the peaceful state.
<s>Nirānanda</s> (blisslessness) and <s>parānanda</s> (supreme bliss) are connected with the <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Ajāta</s> [stages];
through the expansion of bliss born from the masses of enjoyment — non-different and differentiated —
a certain state of great bliss (<s>mahānanda</s>), of the nature of left-hand practice (<s>vāmācāra</s>), would flash forth
in the great abode of <s>Bhairava</s>, in the consciousness that has absorbed everything.
The great bliss, having become the bliss of consciousness (<s>cidānanda</s>), operates again and again.
And in this [state], when the <s>trika</s> of right, left, and upper has been fully absorbed —
in the <s>trika</s> whose nature is the gathering of duality and non-duality in every way,

children.text: abhinnā vātha bhinnā vā bhinnābhinnā athāpi vā //
children.translated_text: whether entities are non-different, or different, or different-and-non-different —
conjoined with the fivefold states of bliss beginning with one's own bliss (<s>nijānanda</s>),
they arise, partaking of the unbridled state of the bliss of the world (<s>jagadānanda</s>).
One's own bliss (<s>nijānanda</s>) has its basis solely in the aspect of the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>);
<s>nirānanda</s> is the state [consisting of] repose in mere emptiness.
From repose in the stage of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>), <s>parānanda</s> (supreme bliss) indeed arises abundantly.
But when the knowable is everywhere full through the contact with infinite objects of knowledge,
from the means of knowledge, through the connection with relishing — this is the state [called] <s>mahānanda</s> (great bliss).
When one who is skilled in the apprehension and devouring of the entire multitude of means and objects of knowledge
comes to rest that is exceedingly full, without conditions (<s>nirupādhi</s>),
then indeed [there is] <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss), which is not augmented by the insentient.

children.text: na ca yatra sthitiḥ kāpi vibhaktā jaḍarūpiṇī /
children.translated_text: And where there is no separate state whatsoever that has the form of the insentient,

children.text: yatra ko 'pi vyavacchedo nāsti yad viśvataḥ sphurat //
children.translated_text: where there is no delimitation at all, which flashes forth universally,
which is nourished by the supreme nectar of consciousness that has not been brought [from elsewhere] —
that is the abode of <s>jagadānanda</s> (world-bliss), as our <s>Guru</s> has declared.

children.text: yatrāsti bhāvanādīnāṃ na mukhyā kāpi saṃgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is no primary connection with meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) and the like,
there, repose should be established through the connection with the arising of the Heart (<s>hṛdayoccāra</s>).

children.text: yā tatra samyag viśrāntis tat parādvaitam ucyate /
children.translated_text: The proper repose therein — that is called the supreme non-duality (<s>parādvaita</s>).
Through the employment of the staff of breath (<s>prāṇadaṇḍa</s>), equalized as prior and subsequent,
the ground sprinkled by the palace of the <s>lambikā</s> (palate), supported by the lotus of the fourfold [<s>cakra</s>],
by the <s>yogin</s>, elsewhere than in the [ordinary] person, through the division of bondage and liberation,
through the nature of <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed), operating in the activity of speech,
through the yoga of the dissolution and arising of the supreme I-consciousness of the self-awareness of consciousness,
emptied by the force of <s>udyoga</s> (effort), having the nature of the true twelve <s>kalās</s>,
when the entity is illuminated, filled, and thoroughly investigated by the sun —
by the power of the churning of its absorption, endowed with the <s>kalā</s> called the sixteenfold,
having entered the fire of awakening, properly emitting the <s>kalās</s>,
the four life-giving [<s>kalās</s>], having attained the unchanged state of <s>visarga</s> (emission),
having absorbed within all the principles from <s>ka</s> to <s>kṣa</s>, the infinite, everywhere —
with a [state] delightful through the absence of the self-awareness of the essence of entity-ness of entities,
presiding over the <s>kulanetryā</s> (eye of the <s>kula</s>), fit for the yoga of external emission —
through the state of <s>Rudrayāmala</s> (the union of <s>Rudra</s>), eternally established in that —
the garland of steps of powers ending in consciousness, breath, qualities, and body —
having emitted through <s>visarga</s>, which operates within the womb of vibration (<s>spanda</s>),
embracing the ground of <s>visarga</s>, partaking of the state of the fish-belly,
the supreme <s>kalā</s>, which pervades everything everywhere, which gives life to all,
having penetrated the ground of the trident, connected with the triad of <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels),
expanding and contracting, having gradually assumed unity,
the garland of steps of powers ending in the furrowed brow (<s>bhrūkuṭī</s>), <s>bindu</s>, and <s>nāda</s>,
expanding and contracting like the flux of the she-ass and the submarine mare (<s>vaḍavā</s>),
full with the floods of entities repeatedly dissolving and being emitted,
whose ground is the <s>visarga</s> of the great root-trident unified,
resting in the Heart of <s>Bhairava</s>, adorned by the fullness of all entities,
designated as <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme), achieved through the <s>hevāka</s> of complete filling,
without beginning or end, endowed with inclination toward the universe,
the moonlight of the moon of consciousness in the sky of the Heart's awareness, the mistress of the triad —

children.text: devīṃ prāpya na kiṃ nāma labhate lambhyaty api //
children.translated_text: having attained this <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), what indeed does one not obtain and also cause to be obtained?
Therefore, here, when the supreme [state] exists through means situated in the body of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),

children.text: yadaiṣa pravivikṣuḥ syād yogī tāvad prakampate //
children.translated_text: when this <s>yogin</s> wishes to enter [it], to that extent he trembles —
[he] whose certainty of identity with the body has been practiced over hundreds of previous births,
thinking of the oneness of consciousness and body like water and mud.
He would first enter, to the extent of the sequence of the seizure of his own power,
into the completely full nature of consciousness, free from the <s>māyā</s> called difference.
Sleep comes to him — that [sleep] which produces the loosening of the grip on the body;

children.text: kamprarūpaiva yāvan no rūḍhir jātā parātmani //
children.translated_text: it has the form of trembling, until firm establishment in the supreme Self has arisen.
This is the <s>avyaktaliṅga</s> (unmanifest sign), which is of the nature of individual (<s>nara</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: yatra viśvam idaṃ līnaṃ yad antaḥsthaṃ ca gamyate //
children.translated_text: in which this universe is absorbed, and which is understood as abiding within.
Moreover, this course that has been previously determined as residing in the body —
through the force of its opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), the <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) would attain clarity.
The <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss) of the <s>citta</s>-principle, which possesses the state of special vibration,
from the fullness of the <s>Śākta</s> arising, having absorbed within the supreme essence of <s>mantravīrya</s> (mantra-power) —
this sign (<s>liṅga</s>), which consists of the individual and power, would be manifest or unmanifest;
it is said in scripture to bear the fruit of <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), blossoming with the juice of fruit-production.

children.text: vyaktaliṅgaṃ tad uktaṃ tu yat kevalanarātmakam /
children.translated_text: But the <s>vyaktaliṅga</s> (manifest sign) is said to be that which is solely of the nature of the individual (<s>nara</s>);
this threefold arrangement of difference belongs to a single vibration (<s>spandana</s>).
Those who, deprived of the heart-knowledge of this <s>liṅga</s>, vainly worship

children.text: bāhyasthaliṅgapūjāṃ prayāsamātraṃ phalāya na hi tat syāt //
children.translated_text: the external <s>liṅga</s> — that is mere exertion; it would not serve as a fruit.
That which is manifest, called the self-<s>liṅga</s>, resting upon the human form —
when the external, which is of the nature of non-difference from the body, is full in the universe,
it arises in the ground of great bliss for the <s>yogin</s> who has dissolved [into it];
therefore, the primary <s>liṅga</s> directly comes face-to-face.
One should always abide in this <s>liṅga</s>, intent upon the repose of worship,
which is the Heart of the <s>yoginīs</s>, the temple of supreme bliss,
the temples of the bliss of <s>visarga</s> in the aspect of the seed and womb previously stated,
where the wise discover a certain attainment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>),
where, due to the absence of effort, the entire host of deities
abides in the abode full of bliss, with eternally arisen consciousness as its nature.
That very illumination of the Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, [which is] of contraction and other [expansion] —
even for one whose contraction and expansion do not exist, it shines forth.
Through the stream of bliss arising from the encounter with that completion,
this universe, being sprinkled, abandons its oldness.
Effort toward entry there, being something to be done, produces exertion;

children.text: yataḥ sadodito bhānuḥ kiṃ dīpena vicāryate //
children.translated_text: for when the sun is eternally risen, what is to be considered by [the light of] a lamp?
Whether the <s>yogin</s> abides established in his own Self, in the ground of the vibration of <s>Śiva</s>-consciousness,
or whether he delights in the <s>kula</s> of the <s>yoginīs</s> of the particulars of the flood of external entities —
even in the absence of the pot [i.e., without a specific object], the state that is of the nature of the appearance of the general vibration (<s>sāmānyaspanda</s>),
that supreme <s>Bhairava-mudrā</s>, with inner focus and outer gaze —

children.text: yad āśrayati śaivī sā parā devī tataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: when one resorts to that supreme <s>Devī</s> of <s>Śiva</s>, then again,
in the flood of entities, which is fabricated by the playful sovereignty (<s>svātantrya</s>),
consisting of the efficacy of this and that — through the connection with the relish of the self-awareness of eager intentness —
[he] touches the true ground of <s>Śakti</s>, the special vibration (<s>viśeṣaspanda</s>), and abides.
Presided over by this [supreme] abode, his <s>mantras</s>, in the illumination of that,
attain the quality of sovereignty, even in diverse <s>siddhis</s> (attainments).
One who has attained firm establishment in the activity of abandonment, acceptance, and concealment,
seeing the visible, which shines with the nature of consciousness, through the connection of manifesting all,
from the perspective of the non-different activity, perceiving [everything] from the wonder of consciousness,
having abandoned the timid state — the wretchedness of the desire for the efficacy of objects —
for as long as he abides thus, to that extent the <s>Śāmbhava</s> ground —

children.text: bhairavīm āviśaty eva parāṃ bhūmim ayatnataḥ //
children.translated_text: the supreme ground of <s>Bhairava</s> — he enters effortlessly.
Everything is perceived as possessed of this consciousness;
for consciousness, seized by the nature of light, shines forth.
And it is not that the non-luminous, through a connection with what is to be illuminated, attains luminosity —

children.text: iti vistarataḥ pūrvaṃ prakāśitam idaṃ yataḥ //
children.translated_text: since this has been extensively elucidated before.
One whose entire activity has dissolved through the conjunction with the great daring (<s>mahāsāhasa</s>),
whose mind has become full with the flood of his own massed rays,
thinking of nothing, whose state has abandoned clearly perceived difference —

children.text: yāvad āsīta tāvat tu pūrvoktā eva bhūmayaḥ //
children.translated_text: for as long as he abides thus, to that extent, those very grounds stated before
come face-to-face — the sole causes of burning the mansion of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And the divine aggregate of senses, concealed by the establishment of difference,
whose nature is a mere instrument for the play that nourishes autonomy --

children.text: yadā nimīlanāvandhyas tiṣṭhaty ekaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tadā //
children.translated_text: when it abides for a single moment with closed eyes (<s>nimīlana</s>) without barrenness, then
dissolved by the great flame of awakening arisen through that gateway,
the universe attains repose in the ocean of supreme bliss.
Resting in the savoring of that essence, gratifying the goddesses of awareness (<s>saṃviddevī</s>),
one quickly attains freedom from the terror of death and birth.
For when awareness has reached a state of density, having attained the nature of body, senses, and objects as its own,

children.text: yuktyā tu sā prāptavilīnabhāvāt saṃvidghanaṃ svaṃ vapur eva yāti //
children.translated_text: then, by the method of [recognizing] that the dissolved state has been attained, it goes to its own body which is a mass of consciousness.
By the very method through which the emergence (<s>vyutthiti</s>) of those whose minds are overpowered by external objects
arises -- that very [method leads to] the awareness of <s>Bhairava</s>'s bliss.
By that very [awareness], obtained through the succession of the tradition of the <s>Yoginī</s>'s mouth,
there abides the state of pure consciousness, whose impurities have been shaken off through possession (<s>āveśa</s>).

children.text: vaktram īṣad yadā yogī vikāsayati saṃvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>yogin</s> slightly opens the mouth of awareness,
all [functions] that depend on the movement through the inner wheel of the sense-channels (<s>indriya-nāḍī</s>),
then they attain an expansion that is of the nature of the absence of differentiation of graspable objects, forcibly,
due to the turning toward consciousness; the differentiation of blue, yellow, and the like
-- the difference of the relationship of grasper and graspable -- is immediately shattered.
Through the succession of tradition established in the mouth of the <s>Yoginī</s>,
sealed by the <s>mudrā</s> (seal) that instantly bestows experience,
drowsy with the direct [presence of] <s>Bhairava</s> whose nature is the consciousness that governs all,
that <s>yogin</s>, filled with wonder, attains self-awareness,
an undiminishing state even in the presence of the arising and subsiding of various objects of perception.
Water situated in a pond-hollow does not flow elsewhere;
that which, even with effort, is unable to fill merely that much --
when, however, it becomes filled with relish by the stream of water from the inner gate,
then there would be streams filled with it, flowing in all directions.
Thus, consciousness, opening spontaneously from the impetuosity of self-efflorescence,
illuminating the aspects of entities without distinction, as non-different from its own self,
if it should resort to the domain of closed-eye [absorption] (<s>nimīlana</s>) for even a moment,
then, from the melting of <s>Māyā</s>, the ground of <s>Bhairava</s> shines forth.
The conceptual delimitation that afterwards would display differentiation --
that itself is <s>Māyā</s>, which illuminates the vision of difference for the autonomous one.
For one established in mere opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), that [Māyā] cannot exist, being uprooted.
Thus, what need of much speaking? In the path whose nature is <s>Anuttara</s> (the Unsurpassed),
in reality, no limb of yoga has the status of a means;
for the nature of this [Anuttara] is formless, due to the abandonment of all delimitation.
Even a means is a non-means for it, due to the cessation of [all] approach and activity.
This boat of the body, devoid of exhalation and inhalation,
carries the self across from the domain of the ocean of differentiation.

children.text: nimajjamānam apy etan mano vaiṣayike rase //
children.translated_text: Even this mind, though immersing in the taste of sense-objects,
does not become inwardly wet, like a seamless gourd.

children.text: svaṃ panthānaṃ hayasyeva manaso ye nirundhate //
children.translated_text: Those who block the mind's own path, as one would a horse's --
due to the [mind's] capacity to break through that, it runs along countless wrong paths.

children.text: kiṃsvid etad iti prāyo duḥkhe 'py utkaṇṭhate manaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'What is this?' -- the mind, mostly, feels longing even in suffering;

children.text: sukhād api virajyeta jñānād etad idaṃ [tv iti] /
children.translated_text: it would become dispassionate even from pleasure, through the knowledge 'this is this.'
For thus the guru instructed in many ways in his own scripture:
the activities of the senses, flowing away through indifference and dispassion alone --

children.text: yāvat tu viniyamyante tāvat tāvad vikurvate //
children.translated_text: as long as they are forcibly restrained, so long do they act perversely.
Even what is called <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses) that is applied to the net of senses
-- for one in bondage whose habit is established -- that binding is [like] binding with adamantine plaster.
suffering or pleasure arising therefrom -- free from anxiety,
In objects, in the method of their enjoyment, in the
know within the bliss of the cessation of mental activity.
even without entering [them], those whose minds are immersed

children.text: tasmai kurvati tatpracāracature saty akṣavarge 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: to it, and when the group of senses, skilled in its operation, also exists,
When the self itself exists as the luminosity whose nature is consciousness, and the heart accordingly renders service

children.text: satsv artheṣu rasādiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yad bhedavandhyodayaṃ
yogī tiṣṭhati pūrṇaraśmikhacitas tat tattvam ādīyatām //
children.translated_text: like a sky filled with the full rays [of the sun] -- let that reality be grasped!
and when objects such as flavors exist -- that the <s>yogin</s> abides with an arising barren of differentiation, most clearly,

children.text: aviveka eva param iha saṃsāra iti pravādamātram /
children.translated_text: Non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) alone is the supreme <s>saṃsāra</s> here -- this is merely a saying;
for non-discrimination alone is indeed the supreme staircase to the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
do you direct attention? Seek that out for yourself.
Abandon your attentions! Indeed, where
nor does the incomplete attain true existence.
Attention toward the complete is surely not appropriate,

children.text: yatraivānandayogaḥ kvacana nanu bhavet tatra pūrṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ
--- --- te veti tatra praśamapadam iyād yady ayaṃ bhedamohaḥ /
children.translated_text: --- [text uncertain] --- if this delusion of difference were to reach the state of quiescence there,
Wherever indeed there is connection with bliss, there surely the nature is complete;
[verse continued from above]

then in that knowledge, even in waking and the like, in every state, the <s>yogin</s> would become the lord of the great wheel of consciousness, though traversing the path of manifold worldly activity, radiant with the power of <s>mantra</s>.
upon reaching water, one alone attains accomplishment;
Just as one who wishes to dig a well --
thus the method of attainment from another is various.
but another, merely from water in the hand and the like --
This is therefore without means (<s>anupāya</s>); through the connection of means and goal,
how could a person be freed from the bondage of differentiation? Or otherwise?
Even in this [state] that is without means, due to a certain relational operation,
the teaching of a means has been variously made in this scripture.

children.text: yathā lipyakṣarair bālāḥ satye varṇātmani sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Just as children are introduced to the true nature of phonemes

children.text: praveśyante tathā mūḍhais tair aupāyikaiḥ kramāt //
children.translated_text: through written letters, so too the confused are [introduced] gradually through those [pedagogical] means.
For that very purpose, even in the non-dual supreme reality, with reverence,
worship, meditation, and the like are appropriately taught in this scripture.
Whatever is mentally delightful, in whatever state of the senses,
is to be united with the abode of the true <s>Brahman</s> of awakening, which is the cavity of <s>Brahman</s>.
Through resorting to the state of absorption in the true being that follows the self,
in the sequence of worship of the wheel of powers of the lords of the respective supreme families (<s>kula</s>),
it naturally attains the status of instrumentality, effortlessly.
with natural flowers gathered mentally, which exude their own fragrance,
Having made the base-ground washed clean by the sprinkling of the delight-essence,
I worship you, O <s>Deva</s>, together with the <s>Devī</s>, in the temple of the body-god, day and night.
through the sequence of the priceless offering-vessel that is one's own heart overflowing with the nectar of bliss --
Thus, wherever one may abide, through the nature of self-reflective awareness,
there the possession by the triad of powers (<s>śaktitrayāveśa</s>) manifests in three ways.
Of [consciousness] manifesting in nine ways, through the twelve wheels spoken of,
the repose achieved in a single moment has one hundred and eight positions.

children.text: ekaiva śatasaṃkhyā ca sā sthitiḥ pravibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: That very repose is also conceived as the number one hundred;

children.text: itthaṃ yat kiṃcanaitasya vacanaṃ yogino bhavet //
children.translated_text: thus, whatever utterance of this <s>yogin</s> there may be,
that itself becomes suitable for the yoga of <s>japa</s> (recitation), on the path of <s>Anuttara</s>,
without depending on the existence of any internal fuel, perpetually.
That which blazes with hundreds of flame-tips extending through the entire flood of senses --
if the entry of all entities into that very [fire] is contemplated,
surely, with their gross form instantly burned, forcibly,
they go to unity with the light of the great flame of awakening, by their very nature.

children.text: sa eṣa paramo homo bhairavīyakrame mataḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the supreme <s>homa</s> (oblation), considered in the tradition of <s>Bhairavī</s>.
Entities properly offered with method into the fire in the belly of one's own awakening

children.text: jahati bhedavibhāgaṃ nijaśaktyā taṃ samindhate yasmāt //
children.translated_text: abandon the division of differentiation, since by their own power they kindle that [fire].
Whatever one creates before oneself by one's own will, due to the naturalness of creation,
as an object of the senses -- that is suitable for <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
For in the formless abode of consciousness, which has the form of the universe,
for those desiring fruit, some particular form alone is established as the object of meditation.

children.text: yathā hy abhedasaṃpūrṇe bhāve 'py udakam āharan /
children.translated_text: Just as, in an entity filled with non-difference, one who draws water,
by abandoning other forms, desires a pot with relish --
just so, from the expansion of the necessity (<s>niyati</s>) of the supreme Lord,
some particular form alone gives rise to some particular conceptualization of fruit.

children.text: yas tu saṃpūrṇacidvṛttir na phalaṃ nāma vāñchati /
children.translated_text: But one whose activity of consciousness is complete does not desire any fruit whatsoever;
for that one, meditation having the form of the entire universe always expands.
For the <s>Kula</s>-yogin, from the intoxicating liquor of the overflowing essence of <s>Bhairavī</s>,

children.text: ghūrṇamānasya yaḥ kaścit ko 'py udeti yathā tathā //
children.translated_text: reeling, some indescribable [experience] arises in whatever way;
the bodily possession (<s>samāveśa</s>) whose nature is delight and melting --
that is the <s>mudrā</s> (seal) that has embraced the universe, in the <s>Nairuttara</s> doctrine.

children.text: eṣa yogavidhiḥ ko 'pi kasyāpi hṛdi vartate /
children.translated_text: This certain indescribable yoga-method resides in the heart of someone or other;
for whom the wheel of consciousness becomes gracious -- quickly, for one in their last birth.
Even while being observed by the world, situated in the condition of bodily bondage,

children.text: abhyeti yoge rūḍhe na kṣaṇāt kām api saṃvidam //
children.translated_text: when yoga is firmly established, one does not fall even for a moment into any [lower] awareness.
In this very [matter], the understanding of our predecessors (<s>pūrvācārya</s>) greatly
established the absence of the confusions of worldly enjoyment.
Through <s>Veda</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, those of <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist), and worldly [systems],
through <s>Pañcarātra</s>, ritual scriptures, <s>Siddhānta</s> and others -- enough!
Through all [traditions] that cultivate the respective appropriate portions of knowledge and action,
all established in their own procedures, through the connection with propriety --
wherein the sequence of activities of sowing seeds, digging, and the like
was performed through many branches of the <s>Śāmbhava</s> [tradition], which is extremely extensive --
of that tree of the <s>Bhairava</s> of consciousness, this is the unsurpassed fruit,
by the observances of life-stages, conduct, and the like, ending with matted locks and eye-ointment,

children.text: kṛtair apy akṛtair vāpi yatra no labhyate bhidā /
children.translated_text: whether performed or not performed -- where no difference is obtained.
For those who rest in that very yoga, the pomp of worldly existence
dissolves of its own accord, like ice in the great summer heat.
Indeed, when this flavorful liquor of awareness is being savored,

children.text: nissaranti mahollāsāḥ saṃkhyā yeṣu na vidyate /
children.translated_text: great ecstasies pour forth, whose number is not found.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca prakaṭīkārāḥ kṛtāḥ prāg eva vistarāt /
children.translated_text: And their manifestation has been made earlier at length;

children.text: atrābhinavagupte tu tattve ke 'py eva niścitāḥ //
children.translated_text: but in this [work of] <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, only certain ones are established in the reality.
only the bee is the connoisseur, not the fly.
In the fragrance of <s>ketakī</s> flowers, intensely,
only someone [special] delights, not one deluded by difference.
In the worship of the supreme non-duality of <s>Bhairavī</s>,

children.text: nātra rūḍhasya kāryā syāc chuddhiḥ kācana kutracit /
children.translated_text: For one established here, no purification whatsoever is required anywhere;

children.text: aśuddhaṃ hi jagaty eva bhairavātmani kiṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: for what impurity could there be in the world when [everything] has <s>Bhairava</s> as its self?

children.text: aśuddhe 'pi ca bhūtaughe kena śuddhiḥ pratāyatām /
children.translated_text: Even in the impure mass of beings, by what should purification be extended?
There would be infinite regress thus, and likewise pointless mutual dependence.
When the impure is concealed, what is called pure dissolves [too];

children.text: pratiyogikṛtaṃ tad dhi na svabhāvena nīlavat //
children.translated_text: for that [purity] is created by its opposite, not by its own nature, like the color blue.
either in grasping or in rejecting sense-objects;
Therefore there is no insistence
the state of being an enjoyer has welled up spontaneously.
of the one whose self is the awareness of the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>,
by this path everything is appropriate;
Since everything has been ordained here,
nothing whatsoever attains propriety.
having pushed aside this path for something else,

children.text: tathāhi dīkṣā nāmeyaṃ yā malānāṃ nikartanī /
children.translated_text: For thus, what is called <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), which is the cutting away of <s>malas</s> (impurities) --
how can that be established in the position of the dualists?

children.text: tathāhi yo malo nāma sa kathaṃ citsvabhāvakam /
children.translated_text: For indeed, what is called <s>mala</s> (impurity) -- how does it cover the self whose nature is consciousness?
Where is the act of covering for the all-pervading one?

children.text: na ca prakāśas tamasā jātu saṃvriyate yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor is light ever covered by darkness, because
this arising of light is itself of the nature of the destruction of darkness.

children.text: kiṃ cāvaraṇam uktaṃ hi raśmyāder gatidharmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, covering has been described for rays and the like, which have the property of motion;
that [covering] is of the nature of obstruction -- what of that for the all-pervading one, which has no property of motion?
Or rather, covering amounts merely to the concealment of knowability;
it would be [like] a pot covered by a cloth -- not an alteration of its own nature.
And selves, being of the nature of consciousness, do not assume the status of being knowable;

children.text: tadāvaraṇam eṣāṃ tu śabdeṣv api na śobhate //
children.translated_text: covering of these does not even look good in words.

children.text: nanv īśvarasya te jñeyā aṇavaḥ katham īdṛśam /
children.translated_text: But are not the <s>aṇus</s> (individual souls) knowable to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord)? How could [there be] such a thing?
For what has consciousness as its nature is not knowable, because the nature of consciousness would be concealed.

children.text: saṃvij jñeyeti śabdo 'yaṃ vandhyā me jananītyadaḥ /
children.translated_text: The statement 'consciousness is knowable' -- this reminds one of the sentence
'the barren woman is my mother,' which is its own fellow <s>brahmacārin</s> (companion in absurdity).
Moreover, the omniscience of <s>Īśvara</s> is thereby impaired to that extent;

children.text: āvṛtān vetti nāṇūn yan na tv eṣāṃ kācana kṣatiḥ //
children.translated_text: He does not know the covered <s>aṇus</s> -- but there is no loss for these [aṇus themselves].

children.text: nanv anāvaraṇe nīle jñātur āvaraṇe sati /
children.translated_text: But if there is no covering on the blue [object], while there is covering on the knower --

children.text: na darśanaṃ tathā bādhā na sarvajño malāvṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Nor is there [an obstruction to] seeing in that way — the omniscient one is not covered by <s>mala</s> (impurity).

children.text: maivaṃ tatra hi dṛgraśmīn gacchataḥ pratihanti tat /
children.translated_text: Not so — for in that case, that [obstruction] impedes the rays of vision as they travel;

children.text: paṭādi na tu vijñātur asty āvaraṇasaṃbhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: a cloth and the like [obstruct], but for the knower there is no possibility of covering.

children.text: malaś cāvyāpako vyāptur āvāraka iti sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: And <s>mala</s> is non-pervading — how can it cover the all-pervading one? Clearly,
it should produce non-emptiness in the space within a pot, by its very nature.

children.text: ātmanaś cādhikāryatvān malaḥ kiṃcitkaro na cet /
children.translated_text: And if <s>mala</s> produces nothing, since the Self is the [true] possessor of jurisdiction,

children.text: katham āvaraṇāyaiṣa śakto nanu ca bhoḥ kimu //
children.translated_text: how is it capable of covering? Indeed, O friend, what then?
For the mere existence of <s>mala</s> is declared to be its covering;
the <s>aṇu</s> (individual soul), accompanied by <s>mala</s>, is described as 'covered.'
Well then, by this reasoning, even for those of the nature that has been described as <s>Śiva</s> —
the covering has endured as real, merely from the existence of <s>mala</s>.

children.text: kiṃcāvṛto malenātmā malam eva na vetti kim /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the Self is covered by <s>mala</s>, does it not know <s>mala</s> itself?
If it does not perceive that [mala], what other <s>mala</s> is to be posited [to explain its non-perception]?

children.text: nanv ataḥ kiṃ malaṃ vettu tarhi vidyākale vinā /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'What then? Let it know <s>mala</s> — in that case, without the <s>vidyākalā</s> (power of knowledge),

children.text: sarvajñatvaṃ bhavet tac ca malaṃ viditam eva sat //
children.translated_text: there would be omniscience — and that <s>mala</s>, being already known,

children.text: jahātv ātmābhyupāyais tais tair vicitraiḥ prakalpitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: let the Self abandon it through those various constructed remedial means.'
Moreover, by this [covering], upon whatever Self it would exist, then
how would its knowership and agentship regarding pots and such come about?
Objection: 'In the <s>vidyākalā</s> (power of knowledge), the limited knowership and agentship are said to be established.'

children.text: itthaṃ vimūḍhamatayo vañcyante na tu paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the confused-minded are deceived — but not the learned.
This <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is inert by nature, and its offspring — <s>kalā</s> and the rest —
being non-conscious, how can they possibly manifest consciousness?
And if consciousness, being all-powerful, is [said to be] manifested — [then]

children.text: viśeṣyatāṃ kathaṃ nāma sāṃśavastūcitaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: how can it be qualified by qualifiers like 'limited' and the like? For that is proper [only] for a thing with parts.
Objection: 'The Lord, equipped with <s>kalā</s> and <s>vidyā</s> as instruments, manifests consciousness.'
Let him manifest [it] fully! Indeed, there is no incapacity or non-grasping in him.

children.text: male sadātane cāsya kathaṃ muktir bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: And if <s>mala</s> is eternal, how will liberation ever come about for him?

children.text: roddhrī śaktir malasyāsti sā ca kvāpi nivartate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mala</s> has a blocking power, and it ceases somewhere

children.text: kvāpi pravartate ceti dhig idaṃ mūḍhabhāṣitam //
children.translated_text: and operates somewhere else' — fie on this speech of the confused!

children.text: jaḍānāṃ ko 'nusandhiḥ syāt taṃ vinaitat kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: For inert things — what connecting awareness (<s>anusandhāna</s>) could they have? Without that, how could this [blocking] occur?
If, even there, the agency of the Lord is accepted —

children.text: kiṃ nimittam asau devas tāṃ śaktiṃ saṃpravartayet /
children.translated_text: for what reason would the Lord set that power in motion?

children.text: pravartitāṃ vā kiṃ nāma tāṃ nivartayate punaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, once set in motion, why would he stop it again?

children.text: svātantryād iti cet pūrṇaṃ tad evāśrīyate na kim /
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'by [his] autonomy' — then why not accept that very full [autonomy as the explanation]?

children.text: malasya dhvāntarūpasya na ca pāko 'pi kaścana //
children.translated_text: And there is no 'ripening' whatsoever of <s>mala</s>, whose form is darkness;

children.text: sa hy anyatādānayogād dhanty amuṣya dhruvātmatām /
children.translated_text: for that [ripening], through the connection of becoming-other, would destroy its permanent nature.
By this [reasoning], the statement 'the soul, by the connection with <s>mala</s>, impelled by the Lord's will,
possessed by the desire for enjoyment-stories, is graced through creation' —

children.text: iti yad bhaṇyate mūlahataṃ taj, janitaṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: that is struck at the root. What is born from that [is as follows]:
They know <s>mala</s> to be merely the play of self-concealment.

children.text: svatantro hi vibhuḥ kiṃcit kiṃ na svātmani bhāsayet //
children.translated_text: For the autonomous, all-pervading [Lord] — what could he not cause to appear within his own self?

children.text: yac ca karmāpi nāmeṣṭaṃ tattāvat pravicāryatām /
children.translated_text: And what is accepted as '<s>karma</s>' (action) — let that be examined to that extent.
For thus: even when the connection with <s>karma</s> is established, how is this

children.text: mahāpralaya ucyate mahāsṛṣṭiś ca vā katham /
children.translated_text: great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>) to be explained? Or how the great creation (<s>mahāsṛṣṭi</s>)?
Objection: 'By the will of the Lord, <s>karma</s> there attains the state of being obstructed.'
Through the indifference-conjunction of <s>karma</s>, [it would] require another <s>karma</s> [to explain its activation].

children.text: īśvaro 'tha navā pūrvapakṣe saṃbhava eva ca //
children.translated_text: If the Lord [is accepted], then [only] in the prima facie [objection] is there possibility;
if there is no possibility [for the Lord], in what aspect does he attain lordship?
[If] everything — creation, dissolution, and the like — would be from <s>karma</s> alone,

children.text: atha karmānapekṣo vā karmaṇāṃ rodhanaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: then, if [the Lord is] independent of <s>karma</s>, let him obstruct those <s>karmas</s>;

children.text: sadā niruddhāny eveśaḥ karmāṇi kurutāṃ vibhuḥ //
children.translated_text: let the all-pervading Lord make <s>karmas</s> always obstructed.
Objection: 'This is their nature — that they have the nature of producing enjoyment.'

children.text: kathaṃ svabhāva eṣa syād yaḥ paropādhitāṃ gataḥ //
children.translated_text: How can this be their nature if it has become dependent on another's condition?

children.text: anapekṣo hi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ karmaṇāṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the nature of things is independent [of external conditions]; therefore, of <s>karmas</s>
that are independent of the Lord's desire — whatever their form is, that is their own body.

children.text: kiṃ ca pralayalīnāni karmāṇi sthitibhāñjy api /
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>karmas</s> dissolved in dissolution — even those that [supposedly] break [the state of] rest —

children.text: kiṃ prabodhayate devaḥ kiṃ nu dṛ[sṛ]ṣṭair hi taiḥ kṛtam //
children.translated_text: what awakens [them]? Does the Lord [do so]? What indeed do those [dissolved karmas] accomplish?
If [you say] 'for the ripening of <s>mala</s>' — that too has been pushed far away [as an explanation].

children.text: kiṃ cātmā vibhur evaiṣa sa kiṃ nāma karoti hi //
children.translated_text: Moreover, this very Self is all-pervading — what indeed does it do?

children.text: iti pūrvaṃ vicāraś ca vistareṇa prapañcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This inquiry has already been elaborated at length.
In clay, stick, wheel, and threads — the wise Lord is established as the agent.
In what aspect does the agency of the potter stand?
In uncultivated, self-ripening seeds — in sprouting, fruiting, and the like,

children.text: pūrvaṃ karotu hetutvaṃ na sasyeṣv iti ko nayaḥ /
children.translated_text: let it first exercise causation, [and only] then not in crops — what kind of principle is this?

children.text: idaṃ duṣkṛtam etac ca sukṛtaṃ phalabhedataḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This is a bad deed, and this is a good deed, from the difference of fruits' —

children.text: iti yat pravibhaktaṃ kiṃ tatrāsyecchaiva jṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: that which is thus distinguished — does his will alone manifest therein?

children.text: svatantro yady asau kasmāt parapīḍākārīṃ nijām //
children.translated_text: If he is autonomous, why does he who is always
overflowing with the essence of compassion adopt his own will that causes suffering to others?
Objection: 'By its own nature, <s>karma</s> is such — it yields fruits accordingly.',
[And] 'It is pacified through the performance of expiation and the like' — reflecting thus,
the Lord fashions the scripture with its varied instructions —

children.text: śaivaṃ, svabhāva edādṛk karmaṇām iti ko nayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Śaiva</s> one. 'The nature of <s>karmas</s> is such' — what kind of principle is this?
'A seed has the nature of producing a sprout' — one of our kind
is capable of knowing from the conduct of earlier elders.

children.text: īśvaras tu nijecchayā vinā na hi kadācana //
children.translated_text: But the Lord, never without his own will,
has beheld the skill of the variety of fruits of <s>karma</s>.
the groups of individual selves would not in any way be agents.
Therefore, if the Lord is the maker of all,
and pointing to those [barren karmas], the Lord would not be the maker of all.
If they too are not agents, then <s>karmas</s> would be barren [of agents] —

children.text: itthaṃ ca bhedadṛṣṭyedaṃ karma nāma na mu[yu]ktimat /
children.translated_text: Thus, from the perspective of difference, this [thing called] <s>karma</s> has no rational basis.

children.text: etāvān atra saṃkṣopo vyāso 'nyatra tu darśitaḥ //
children.translated_text: This much is the summary here; the detailed treatment has been shown elsewhere.

children.text: saṃvedanātmako deva ekas tasmāt svataḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: The Lord, whose nature is awareness, is one. Therefore, by himself indeed,
he is the maker of all; due to variety, he is said to be 'endowed with <s>karma</s>.'

children.text: māyā ca nāma viśvasya yā kāraṇam iti sthitā /
children.translated_text: And what is called <s>māyā</s> — that which is established as the cause of the universe —
if it is eternal, bearing within it the <s>tattva</s>-aspects from earth to the end, then clearly

children.text: pralayo na kadācit syān nanu sa vyaktibhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: there would never be dissolution. Objection: 'That [dissolution] is through the state of manifestation.'

children.text: vyaktiṃ nāma na jānīmo vijñānaṃ grāhyatā yataḥ //
children.translated_text: We do not know [such a thing as] 'manifestation' — for cognition is graspability.
The graspability by the Lord's supreme knowledge of that [<s>māyā</s>] exists eternally;
if it [<s>māyā</s>] did not exist, how would the Lord be the cause?

children.text: sphuṭaṃ prakurute kumbhaṃ tadvad īśe bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: [A potter] clearly produces a pot — it will be the same with the Lord [as cause].
Not so — from the distinction between internal and external kinds of instruments,
the cognition of clear, unclear, and the like is appropriate. The pot-making is clear [and external];
for the Lord, who possesses clear and magnificent prior knowledge,

children.text: ko na jñāto bhaved bhāgo yatrāpi vyaktyapekṣitā /
children.translated_text: what aspect could remain unknown? Even where 'manifestation' is expected,
in the domain of the proponents of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (pre-existence of effect in cause), in the cause too the universe

children.text: viśvam ityapi māyāyāṃ sphuṭaṃ syād asamañjasam /
children.translated_text: exists clearly — [so claiming] it exists clearly in <s>māyā</s> would also be incoherent.

children.text: vyāpakāś ca śivātmānas tattvaiḥ sākaṃ parasparam //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śiva</s>-natured [principles], which are all-pervading — together with the <s>tattvas</s>, mutually —
how can they be said to exist [separately]? For pervasiveness and concealment [are contradictory].

children.text: vikāsaḥ paramo vyāptiḥ saṃvido bheda ucyate //
children.translated_text: The supreme expansion — pervasion — of consciousness is called difference.
The illusory (<s>māyīya</s>) cluster of <s>kañcukas</s> (sheaths), just as the aggregate of sense-organs,

children.text: vicāritaḥ pūrvam eva kāryavargaś ca carcitaḥ //
