children.translated_text: has already been examined previously, and the group of effects has also been discussed.
So long as the universe does not shine forth as barren of the superimposition of the state of <s>Śiva</s>,
let it be firmly understood that this is merely the story of his autonomy.

children.text: evaṃ malādyabhāve hi kā dīkṣā ko hi dīkṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, if <s>mala</s> and the rest do not exist, what <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation)? Who indeed is the initiator?

children.text: dīkṣāpātraṃ ca ko vā syād iti kiṃcin na yujyate //
children.translated_text: And who would be the vessel of initiation? — thus nothing is fitting.
In the disciple, in the path (<s>adhvan</s>), in the fire, in the vessel, in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram), in the ladle and the rest,
the placement (<s>nyāsa</s>) of the entire path — how too would it be tenable?

children.text: nahi tāvanta eva syur nanu saṃkalpanāvaśāt /
children.translated_text: Indeed, they would not be just that many [in number] — but through the force of imaginative construction (<s>saṃkalpanā</s>).
This relation of purifier and purified — all of this is said to arise [from saṃkalpanā].
If what is imagined bears fruit, truly, those whose wealth is earned by daydreaming
would triumph through the connection with the attainment of the sovereignty of heaven and its rest!
What indeed? Do things that travel in the path of a powerful and vivid imaginative construction
not bear fruit — like the destruction of poison through meditation and the like?
'Firmness of imaginative construction' — that itself is meditation, tainted with doubt.

children.text: dhyānaṃ ca na phaled eva svayaṃ pakṣadvayāgrahāt //
children.translated_text: And meditation would not bear fruit by itself, from the non-grasping of both sides.
Well then! If fruit arises from the conjunction of imaginative construction,

children.text: kim asaṃvinmayān bhāvān bāhyān kāṃścit abhīpsasi //
children.translated_text: why do you desire certain external things that are not made of consciousness?
By imaginative construction alone, the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) [travels through] the fire-pit, fire, guru, and disciple;

children.text: sa eva ca phalābhāsī tatsaṃvid avaśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: and that very [imaginative construction] appears as the fruit — [only] the awareness thereof remains.
And the manifestation of autonomous consciousness in precisely such a form —

children.text: dīkṣeti kila mantavyaṃ muñcyante jantavo yayā //
children.translated_text: that is to be understood as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), by which beings are liberated.

children.text: ata eva tilājyādeḥ svarūpe grahaṇe mitau /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the essential nature of sesame, ghee, and the like, in their grasping, in their measure,

children.text: kramo vā niyamo neha kaścic chāstre nirūpitaḥ //
children.translated_text: no sequence or restriction whatsoever has been established here in the scripture.

children.text: nanu mantreṣu kiṃ nāma niyamaḥ sarvavarṇabhāk /
children.translated_text: Objection: 'In the case of <s>mantras</s>, what restriction [is there]? The supreme form

children.text: rūpaṃ paraṃ hi kathitaṃ dīkṣāpi na tathā katham //
children.translated_text: that partakes of all phonemes has been stated — how is <s>dīkṣā</s> not similarly [unrestricted]?'
Exactly so — what you accept as the benefit of the burning of phonemes —

children.text: kiṃ tu tāvati ye rūḍhiṃ na prāptās tān prati dhruvam //
children.translated_text: however, for those who have not attained firm establishment in that much, assuredly

children.text: māntro 'yaṃ niyamaḥ prokta upayogaṃ ca gacchati /
children.translated_text: this <s>mantra</s>-based restriction is proclaimed, and it serves a purpose.
For those <s>mantras</s>, being awakened, traveling in the path of reflective awareness,
of the very nature of agency, from the autonomy of the autonomous abode of consciousness —
the <s>mantras</s> indeed enter the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), through the compulsion of identity [with him].
They make [him] autonomous; even the instruments attain agency.

children.text: itthaṃ dīkṣādividhaye ye 'py anye vidhayo matāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever other procedures are accepted for the performance of <s>dīkṣā</s> and the like —

children.text: kiṃ nāma kurvatāṃ kṛtyaṃ niṣedhaṃ tv api vā katham /
children.translated_text: what duty do they perform for those who act? And how indeed [can there be] prohibition?

children.text: te 'py atraivopapadyante tat sarvaṃ vihitaṃ tv iha //
children.translated_text: They too are tenable right here [in our system]. For all of that is enjoined here;

children.text: sarvaṃ caitad amutraiva pratiṣiddhaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: and all of this is clearly prohibited right there.
Moreover, when its prohibition is demonstrated — what? For one who has resorted to the path of non-duality,
even the prohibition is enjoined, and that too is prohibited.
Thus, the ocean of self-awareness surges abundantly within its own self.
And thus, this entire universe — beautiful with the bliss of the world —
and its opposite, the aspect of difference, are thus fully dissolved.
Of the moon of knowledge, arisen from the face of the Supreme Lord, from all directions,
the beautiful rays shine to that extent, resplendent with the burden of their own radiance.
Merely through the fall of the mass of rays of the <s>Śiva</s>-moon,
the <s>kālakūṭa</s> (poison) — the cool-rayed [moon] of all existents — is dissolved into nectar.
Plunging therein ceaselessly, intoxicated by drinking that nectar,
having become that nectar itself, we stand purified, freed from the triple affliction.

children.text: parameśamukhaṃ tu śaktir uktā bhavatīcchā nanu sodbhavaṃ gatā /
children.translated_text: The face of the Supreme Lord is declared to be [his] power; it is his will (<s>icchā</s>), which has gone forth;
it attains the course of the moon-power of knowledge, [which is] the existence differentiated as <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest.

children.text: śaśinaḥ kila tasya sarvato yaḥ paripūrṇaḥ prasṛto marīcipuñjaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of that moon, the cluster of rays that has spread forth in all directions, fully —

children.text: iyam eva hi sā kriyātmikoktā parameśasya jaganmayī svaśaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: this indeed is that power of the Supreme Lord, declared to be of the nature of action (<s>kriyā</s>), [and] consisting of the world.

children.text: tad idaṃ trikaśaktinirbharaṃ paramaṃ bhairavam eva jṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, this supreme <s>Bhairava</s> alone, charged with the triad of powers, unfolds;

children.text: na tu tadvyatireki saṃbhavet svavijṛmbhā vijayo 'sya kīrtitaḥ //
children.translated_text: nothing separate from him can arise. His self-unfolding is celebrated as victory.

children.text: tata eva jagaj jayanty amī sphuṭam arthaḥ prakaṭo 'pi yujyate naḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'they are victorious over the world' — these [beings], clearly. The meaning is manifest and fits us.

children.text: bahuvācakayoga īdṛśaṃ tat paripūrṇatvam amuṣya vākyabhedam //
children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of many denotations, such is [the meaning of] the fullness of his — [expressed through] the divisions of sentences.

children.text: ity eka eva śloko 'yaṃ cidātmā bhairavaḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: Thus, this single verse — <s>Bhairava</s> himself, whose self is consciousness —
charged with the construction of all existents, has been clearly expounded.
For the destruction of the poison of <s>saṃsāra</s>, those whose vision is mounted upon <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>),
employing poison itself, attain the state of nectar [immortality].
Thus, this much has been shown: by self-luminous self-awareness,

children.text: siddhaṃ tadvyatirekeṇa na kiṃcid eva kalpate //
children.translated_text: what is established — apart from that, nothing whatsoever is to be constructed.

children.text: yāvatsvasaṃvidviśrāntaṃ yat tāvat tat sad eva hi /
children.translated_text: Whatever rests in self-awareness — that alone is truly real;

children.text: kālāntaravyapekṣe hi satyatvaṃ syān na kutracit //
children.translated_text: for if reality depended on another time, it would nowhere be real.
The conjunction of consciousness with time has been refuted at length.

children.text: tat svasaṃvid yathā deśaṃ vitared vartate tathā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, self-awareness extends as it extends, in its own domain — and so it stands.
Thus, in the touchstone of awareness made of the imperishable [syllables], it is established:

children.text: na yat tat saṃśayāyaiva śāstre 'py uktam avastu tat //
children.translated_text: That which does not [lead to certainty] is only for doubt; even if stated in a treatise, it is a non-entity.
That which does not rise up into one's own self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>) is no different from babbling.

children.text: tac cchāstraṃ prakriyā sā ca yat saṃvidi vivartate //
children.translated_text: That treatise and that method [is valid] which revolves within [one's own] awareness.
From the heart of the universe have arisen all these risings and fallings of everything,
like [those] of dream from [the state] called deep sleep — explored in the treatise of self-awareness.
Form, illumination, mental impression, aggregate, withdrawal, maintenance,
creation, closing and opening, and the contraction-construction of existing things —
such states, ever having the form of knower, knowable, and means of knowledge,
are themselves the elaborate construction of self-awareness, which is perfectly full.
For she herself is of the form of all, every self, every direction, place, time, and form;
the determination of truth and falsity arises from that very [self-awareness].
The master <s>Utpaladeva</s> too taught precisely this:
'Even that which externally has the nature of existent and non-existent — my vision within self-awareness
sees [it thus]' — this is the ordinance of the autonomous one, called [the ordinance] together with the sense faculties.

children.text: saiva rūdhā śivād ā ca krimeḥ svāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritā //
children.translated_text: That very [awareness], established from <s>Śiva</s> down to the worm, resorts to its own consciousness.

children.text: tad eva deve saṃsāraḥ sa śivaḥ parameīŭvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: That alone in the Lord is <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence); he is <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme Lord.

children.text: tatra viśrāntim āpanno mukta ity abhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: One who has attained rest therein is called 'liberated' (<s>mukta</s>).
By its grace, [all beings] from <s>Brahmā</s> down to stationary [plants] live.

children.text: aviluptā sadā seyaṃ saṃvittir iti gṛhyatām //
children.translated_text: Let it be understood: this awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>) is ever undiminished.

children.text: vibhānty api hi sā devī na tayā rahitaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: For that Goddess shines; nowhere is anything devoid of her.

children.text: ātmānaṃ sādhayet kvāpi kvāpi dūṣayate kvacit //
children.translated_text: Somewhere she establishes the self, somewhere she refutes [it], and somewhere

children.text: anyathaiva sthāpayate na ca yāti vikāritām /
children.translated_text: she places [it] in yet another way — yet she does not undergo modification.
The supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>), though barren of [real] establishment, refutation, and alteration,

children.text: bhāsate ca tathātvena tat svatantrā sphuṭā hi sā /
children.translated_text: yet shines as having that nature — for she is clearly autonomous.

children.text: śrīmān maheśvaro devaḥ pūrveṣām api yo guruḥ //
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Maheśvara</s>, the Lord, who is the guru even of the ancients —
he spoke precisely this, for the sake of bestowing grace upon the world.

children.text: tiṣṭatha vacasi vṛthaivaṃ svāṃ saṃvidam āvarjya /
children.translated_text: thus diverting your own awareness in vain?
'O deluded ones! Why do you stand uselessly in [mere] words, worthless, resembling the croaking of crows,
all those who honor that become liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>) in that very place.'
Whatever has been enjoined by the deity of awareness itself, [whether] near or far,

children.text: tad atra nītau saṃvittir evāsau gurur ucyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in this teaching, awareness itself is called the guru,
since it 'swallows' (<s>girati</s>) the universe through the conjunction of creation and withdrawal.

children.text: tad atra mukhyā yā rūḍhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ para ucyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, the primary established meaning is called the supreme connection;

children.text: enayā yad yad ādiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ tu tat //
children.translated_text: whatever has been enjoined by her — that is innate knowledge (<s>sāṃsiddhika jñāna</s>).
Wherein the eternal abiding of our lineage of gurus is established,
from which the division of the lineage of <s>Tryambaka</s> and the rest proceeds.
Where it was previously stated that 'identity with ignorance perishes' —

children.text: svasaṃvidas tu vaicitryaṃ gṛhṇatyā bhāty ayaṃ tataḥ //
children.translated_text: the [awareness] that grasps the variety of self-awareness shines forth as this [reality].
The encounter with scripture — the interval, the great divine and non-divine, and so forth —
the rays of one's own speech, fashioned by the self from the guru, like reality itself.
The primacy of self-awareness is manifest —
from the guru, from scripture, and from oneself.
Therefore, this effort has been made principally [toward that].
and that [scripture] is established in one's own self-awareness.
The guru is subordinate to the operation of scripture,
attains accomplishment — it never attains intolerability.
Therefore, all of this, through self-awareness,

children.text: etac chāstraṃ prayatnena carcyatāṃ he mumukṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let this treatise be studied with effort, O seekers of liberation!
Let not [your] lifespan be led away in vain, wearied in other treatises!

children.text: abhedadṛṣṭir yā kācid bhedadṛṣṭir athāpi vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever vision of non-difference [there may be], or else whatever vision of difference —
it reaches its fulfillment here alone; therefore, let this be carefully examined.
Just as one who has attained the knowledge of the dream-state is free from [the sleep of] ignorance, so too
one whose heart is awakened through the practice of this treatise is ever [free].

children.text: svasaṃvid eva tac chāstraṃ sā cāpekṣāvivarjitā /
children.translated_text: Self-awareness itself is that treatise, and she is free from dependence.

children.text: tathā yady abhidhīyeta svataḥ prāmāṇyam ucyatām //
children.translated_text: If it be stated thus, then let self-validity (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>) be affirmed.

children.text: śāsanaṃ śāsitavyaṃ ca śāsakaṃ ceti yat kila /
children.translated_text: The teaching, the taught, and the teacher — all that indeed
is therein without temporal division, beautiful in the non-duality of autonomy.
Having internalized that imperishable state, one's own,
<s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s> spoke in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s> scripture:

children.text: sarvam etat pravṛttyarthaṃ śrot\rr ṇāṃ tu vibhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All this is set forth for the sake of engagement of the listeners, through differentiation;
but this differentiation is constructed figuratively, from the differentiation of meanings.'

children.text: phalabhedo na kalpyo 'tra kalpyaś ced ayathātatham /
children.translated_text: 'No differentiation of fruit should be constructed here; if constructed, it would be contrary to reality.'
This [system] of the Lord, differentiated into divisions of ten, eight, eighteen, eight, and eight,
has as its single fruit the attainment of the true being of <s>Śiva</s>; for the qualified soul (<s>aṇu</s>) who is eager for that attainment,
without regard for caste, family, color (<s>varṇa</s>), and the like —
[the teaching] has been set forth, and it operates as long as it achieves the unity of statement;
to that extent, the knowers understand this as one, on account of the variety of principal and subordinate operations.
The <s>Trika</s> scripture is of such a nature; the guru therein is of non-dual nature.
The mass of sentences immediately following that, and the sections (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) as well,
serve to make clear the account of differentiation belonging to <s>Māyā</s>;

children.text: tathāpi śivasaṃprāptir mukhyam ante phalaṃ sthitam //
children.translated_text: even so, the attainment of <s>Śiva</s> remains as the principal fruit at the end.
And the qualified person is one alone — the recipient of the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>-hood.
Nevertheless, in each section, to that extent,

children.text: yādṛk phalaṃ sphutaṃ mukhyaṃ paryantaphalam aṅgi vā /
children.translated_text: whatever fruit is clearly the principal one, or the final fruit as the principal member,

children.text: tadaṅgaṃ vā tadvipakṣe parapakṣe paraṃ ca vā //
children.translated_text: or its subordinate, or in the opposing case, or the supreme in the rival position —
or even the recipient of the conjuring up of aspects of their respective opposites,
having a body appropriate to that, and partaking of the corresponding initiatory preparation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) —
such a sequence of qualification has been stated for the guru and the disciple as well.
And thus, one who resorts to the procedure of the death-destroying elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>),
first, for the obtainment of [bodily] preparation, through decoctions, emetics, and purgatives —

children.text: dīkṣayā yā ca vikṛtiḥ nottaratra kriyāvidhau //
children.translated_text: [so too,] the transformation that [occurs] through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) does not [apply] to the subsequent ritual procedure.
Therefore, the restriction of qualification arises from that body, condition, and the like.
Hence it is said: <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> and the like, who are bound by the scripture of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>),

children.text: na śaive 'dhikṛtās tantre na śaivā vāmagocare /
children.translated_text: are not qualified in the Śaiva <s>tantra</s>; nor are Śaivas [qualified] in the domain of the <s>Vāma</s> [tradition];

children.text: te 'pi no dakṣiṇe te 'pi na syuḥ kulamate trike //
children.translated_text: nor are those [qualified] in the <s>Dakṣiṇa</s>; nor would those be [qualified] in the <s>Kula</s> doctrine, in the <s>Trika</s>.
It is stated in the <s>Śrī Bhairavakula</s>: 'One who is fit for the five initiatory rites —
the guru who has transcended the lower stream — or one who has entered the <s>Trika</s> scripture.'
Thus, the single qualification [is established] through resort to the Self-principle;
through the difference of the basis of initiatory preparation, there is differentiated qualification.
Therefore it is stated in the <s>Svacchandatantra</s>: '<s>Śiva</s> is the fruit in all scriptures,
since all [scriptures] are born from <s>Śiva</s> and have the abode of <s>Śiva</s> as their fruit.'
And therein again it is stated, in the discrimination of the higher principles:

children.text: yan na sāṃkhyair na yogīndrair na priye pāñcarātrikaiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'That which is not [attained] by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, nor by the chief <s>Yogīs</s>, nor, O beloved, by the <s>Pāñcarātrikas</s> —'

children.text: iyādi yāvad ākṣiptaṃ vādināṃ tu śatatrayam /
children.translated_text: and so on, up to what is cast at the disputants — three hundred
and sixty-three [systems]; for they are discriminators of only that much.
How could they be those who know the undivided <s>Śiva</s>-principle in its fullness?
Now, if even in a mere portion of that, they were to superimpose
the true being of <s>Śiva</s> — that would by no means be a clear fit.
For in a sentence such as '<s>Devadatta</s> [does such-and-such],' which is full in all respects,
how would a hearer of [merely] the word '<s>Devadatta</s>,' in that much of the sentence alone,
perform the superimposition of the complete earlier sentences?
And how would he attain that much meaning from [merely] the sentence?

children.text: tasmād eveti cet tarhi na padaśrotṛtā na ca //
children.translated_text: If [one says] 'Therefore indeed [he would]' — then there is neither the status of being a hearer of [just] a word, nor
does that meaning belong to only that much. Thus, in the domain of <s>Prakṛti</s>,
through the complete cognition of the meaning of the entire Śaiva scripture in its full form,
if one were to fill <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Jaina</s>, <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, <s>Śruti</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s>
with the <s>Śiva</s>-principle —

children.text: tāvad astu na tu sphāras tāvāṃs tatreti carcitam /
children.translated_text: let that be so; but it has been discussed that the scope is not that extensive therein.
And the cognition of the <s>Śiva</s>-principle is preceded by the initiatory preparation of that [tradition].
Otherwise, there would be transgression (<s>pratyavāya</s>) for both the instructor and the instructed.

children.text: tatsaṃskāragrahaś cet syāt kāmaṃ śāstrārtha īdṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: If the initiatory preparation of that [tradition] were to be grasped, then by all means let the meaning of the scripture be such;

children.text: na tu vaiṣṇavatā tasya sāṃkhyatā śrautatāpi vā /
children.translated_text: but then his <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-hood, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>-hood, or <s>Śrauta</s>-hood [no longer holds] —
even after receiving the other preparation progressively higher and higher, one proceeds [accordingly].

children.text: vaiṣṇavādy eva tarhy asya pratyavāyo mahattaraḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one remains] a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> and the like, then the transgression for him is all the greater.
But in this non-dual state, what is this primary construction?

children.text: kiṃ brūṣe svayam eva tvaṃ bhedopahatavṛttikaḥ /
children.translated_text: What do you say? You yourself are one whose activity is marred by differentiation.

children.text: etad eva paraṃ dvaitaṃ bhavān eva saṃśritaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is precisely the supreme duality that you have resorted to —

children.text: yad ahaṃ vaiṣṇavo bhūṣṇuḥ śaive kiṃ nādhikāravān /
children.translated_text: 'I am a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — am I not qualified in the Śaiva [tradition]?'

children.text: tat svayaṃ bhedamūḍhas tvaṃ bhede ca niyater balāt //
children.translated_text: You yourself are deluded by differentiation, and [caught] in the force of restriction in differentiation.

children.text: tatas taiḥ pratyavāyaḥ syād yoga ity upapāditam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, through those [restrictions], the transgression would arise — thus it has been demonstrated.

children.text: kiṃ ca tādātmyayogena devatā pūjyate tataḥ //
children.translated_text: Moreover, through the yoga of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), a deity is worshipped; therefore,
how would one who has attained identity with <s>Viṣṇu</s> worship <s>Rudra</s>?

children.text: gītāsu ca tato gītaṃ yo yac chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ //
children.translated_text: And therefore it is sung in the <s>Gītā</s>: 'Whatever faith one has, that indeed one is.'
The meditations of identity are <s>yogas</s>; the fruit [comes from] <s>mantras</s>, one's own —
they would give [the fruit] to one whose self is absorbed in that; they bestow accomplishment on one who desires fruit.
For one who desires liberation, [one should resort to] the scripture of that liberation; for one who also desires [that liberation], it is clear;
one who is overtaken by the meditation on the faults of that [other tradition] is capable of engagement in only that much.

children.text: mukhyas tāvad ayaṃ kalpo yo yatraiva pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The primary rule is this: whoever is established in whichever [tradition] —

children.text: nityaṃ tādātmyam āpannaḥ sa tatrādhikṛtas tv iti //
children.translated_text: having constantly attained identity [with that deity], he is qualified therein indeed.

children.text: ata eva tato grāhyaṃ jñānam ity abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowledge is to be received from that [tradition] — so it is said.
For he, having attained identity, through the procedure of meditation on that [deity],

children.text: śiṣyas tadaiva śāstraṃ tu gṛhṇan pūrvāparakramāt /
children.translated_text: as a disciple, receiving that very scripture through the sequence of earlier and later [teachings] —

children.text: kathaṃ svabuddhyā saṃdhattāṃ tāvad yat tena saṃhitam //
children.translated_text: how would he, by his own intellect, reconcile that which has been composed by him [the guru]?

children.text: yas tu saṃdhātum īheta sa sākṣāt parameśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who would seek to reconcile [all traditions] — he is directly the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>);

children.text: tasya kiṃ vā guruḥ kuryāt so 'nyeṣāṃ gurur ucyate //
children.translated_text: what indeed would a guru do for him? He is called the guru of others.

children.text: nānyato vedavidbhyaś cetyata eva hi manvate /
children.translated_text: 'Not from another but from the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>' — for this very reason they consider [thus].

children.text: tasmāt tādātmyam āpanno gurur ity abhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who has attained identity [with the tradition] is called 'guru.'

children.text: sa ca yāvati yatraiva tatra tāvati nānyathā /
children.translated_text: And he [is a guru] only in that [tradition] to that extent, and not otherwise.
But [if one says:] 'The meaning of the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> scripture, at that time, from the meditation on <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: tādātmyaṃ gurutāṃ hanti pūrṇadhīḥ pralapaty ayam /
children.translated_text: the identity [with Viṣṇu] destroys the guru-hood!' — this person of complete intellect babbles [nonsense].
For in dramas of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, these are not the actor's [real] roles
by whose change of costume and the like one attains otherness.

children.text: vaiṣṇavo viṣṇur evāhaṃ taddāso veti carcayan //
children.translated_text: 'I am a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, I am <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, I am his servant' — thus contemplating,

children.text: idānīṃ na tathāsmīti kim etat susamañjasam /
children.translated_text: 'Now I am not so' — how is this at all coherent?

children.text: atra hy ekatamā saṃvin mithyājñānatvam aśnute //
children.translated_text: For herein, one of the two awarenesses would attain the status of false knowledge,

children.text: yayā sa eva patitaḥ śiṣyo vā patito bhavet /
children.translated_text: by which either he himself would fall, or the disciple would fall.

children.text: tasmān mukhyo hy ayaṃ kalpaḥ pratiśāstraṃ gurur guruḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the primary rule is this: for each scripture, the guru is [specific to that] guru-tradition.
It is stated in the autonomous (<s>Svatantra</s>) scriptures: 'He does not bestow the fruit of accomplishment —
one who is devoted to another scripture, or even one devoted to that [same] scripture [without proper qualification].'
Even in the world, such is the teaching regarding astrology and the like:

children.text: viṣṇor bhāgavatā magāś ca savituḥ śāṃbhor jaṭābhasmino
māt-ṛṇām atha mātṛmaṇḍalavido viprās tv atha brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: the knowers of the circle of Mothers are of the Mothers; the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are of <s>Brahman</s>;
'The devoted ones of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are <s>Bhāgavatas</s>; the <s>Māgas</s> are of the Sun; the matted, ash-smeared ones are of <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: yo yair deva upāsyate svavidhinā tais tasya kāryā kriyā //
children.translated_text: by whichever [devotees] whichever deity is worshipped according to their own ritual, the rite of that [deity] should be performed by them.'
the <s>Śākyas</s> (Buddhists) are of the <s>Buddha</s>-form, benefactor of beings; the naked ones (Jains) are likewise of <s>Arhat</s>;
For this very reason, even if one possessing superior knowledge is present

children.text: deśe tatra bhaven nānā nādhikārasya bhājanam //
children.translated_text: in a [particular] place, the [practitioner of] another [tradition] would not be a recipient of [that] qualification.

children.text: yas tv asmin pūrṇasaṃbodhe rūḍho vāstavaśāsane /
children.translated_text: But one who is established in this complete awakening, in the true scripture,
with the mental instrument of a child, for the purpose of progressively higher establishment —
or even for the attainment of fruits, for one who possesses the power of [higher] states of being,

children.text: anugrahaṃ sa vai kuryāt pūrṇatvād ūrdhvavṛttitaḥ //
children.translated_text: he indeed would bestow grace, from his fullness, through higher operation.

children.text: nanv advaye kim ūrdhvaṃ syān na kiṃcid bhedamohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But in that non-dual state, what would be 'higher'? Nothing! — O you who are deluded by differentiation!

children.text: bhavatas tv adharāvasthā bheda evadharo yataḥ //
children.translated_text: For you, however, the lower state [applies] — because differentiation is indeed the lower.
Therefore, whoever else there may be, those following the scripture of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) —
<s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>), followers of <s>Śruti</s>, and also proponents of <s>Vedānta</s> —
such as these are never qualified in the scripture of the Lord (<s>pati</s>).
Where, even in the scriptures, in the discrimination of qualification, it has been stated:

children.text: yo vaiṣṇavo manuṃ dadyāc chaivaṃ mūḍhamatiḥ śiśoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> who, deluded in mind, would give a Śaiva <s>mantra</s> to a child —

children.text: taṃ pāpaṃ vañcakaṃ tyaktvā śiśur nyāyyaṃ samācaret //
children.translated_text: that sinful deceiver should be abandoned, and the child should practice what is proper.'

children.text: ihāpy uktaṃ mokṣadaḥ syāt svabhyastajñānavān iti /
children.translated_text: Here too it is stated: 'One who bestows liberation would be one who possesses knowledge practiced by oneself.'

children.text: abhyastaṃ ca paraṃ jñānaṃ yato nāsty eva vicyutiḥ //
children.translated_text: And practiced supreme knowledge is that from which there is absolutely no falling away.

children.text: paramādvayavijñānān na khalv apy asti vicyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: From the supreme non-dual knowledge (<s>paramādvayavijñāna</s>), there is indeed no falling away.
whose activity is full of the entirety of knowledge established in the position of his own Self —

children.text: kathaṃ ko vā kuto vāpi cyavatāṃ tiṣṭhatu kva vā /
children.translated_text: 'How?' 'Who?' 'From where?' — let those who fall [from this understanding] stand wherever they will.

children.text: itthaṃ ya eṣa śāstrārthaḥ sthitaḥ śaktiprabhāvataḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, this meaning of the scripture, established through the power of <s>Śakti</s>,
is full of the burden of all <s>tattvas</s> (realities), syllables, and the like, internalized within —
the all-designating one, whose Self is <s>Bhairava</s> — he alone is the possessor of [his own] essential nature.
In this scripture, by the supreme Lord, [this work] was made under the name <s>Jñānacandra</s> (Moon of Knowledge).

children.text: tadvyākhyātam idaṃ prasannagahanaṃ vākyaṃ mayā svāgama

children.translated_text: from the procedure of establishing the authoritativeness of one's own <s>āgama</s> (tradition), and also from various incidental discussions.
This commentary on that [text] has been composed by me — clear yet profound in its statements —

children.text: bhātīti svayam eva satyahṛdayā jñāsyanti kiṃ ślāghitaiḥ //
children.translated_text: shines forth; those of true hearts will know for themselves — what [need is there] for praises?
For those whose understanding has ascended herein, the greatness of the means of valid knowledge — liberated through the non-duality of the universe —

children.text: ye samyak pravicāriṇo nanu śivāḥ kas tān prati prodyamaḥ

children.translated_text: And what of those who are lame in the procedure of ascending the distant summit of reflective awareness?
Those who properly investigate are indeed <s>Śiva</s> themselves — what effort [is needed] toward them?

children.text: pāṣāṇāyitavṛttayaḥ punar amī ye śāstravandhyā narāḥ
saṃrambhaḥ pralayambudher iva tataḥ svātmany ayaṃ ghūrṇate //
children.translated_text: the fury [of debate] therefore churns within oneself alone, like the ocean at the time of dissolution.
And further, these men whose dispositions have turned to stone, who are barren of scriptural [understanding] —

children.text: saṃśāmya svayam ātmani tyaja javāj jvālājaṭāḍambarān
bhoḥ kalpānala dāhyam asti bhavato nādyāpi kiñcid yataḥ /
children.translated_text: O fire of the aeon's end! For there is nothing combustible for you even now, since
'Subside of your own accord within yourself; quickly abandon the display of your crests of flame,

children.text: viśvaṃ vyāpya vilīnatāṃ gatam idaṃ drāk tvatprakāśātmakam //
children.translated_text: of your swirling conflagration, has quickly become of the nature of your own radiance.'
